Severity held at medium: requires a device-loss event, and other subsystems break across that boundary too.

findings.title: No <LanguageStandard> set, so the project builds as C++14 and every modern fix in this module is blocked
findings.detail:
All four configurations set `<WarningLevel>Level4</WarningLevel>` and `<ConformanceMode>true</ConformanceMode>` but no `<LanguageStandard>` element appears anywhere in the file, so MSVC v145 falls back to its default (/std:c++14). `<TreatWarningAsError>` is likewise absent, which is why the C4100 unreferenced-parameter warnings in this module accumulate silently.

This single omission blocks most of the clean fixes the weapons module needs: `inline constexpr` constants (the per-TU duplication in weapon_consts.h), `std::string_view` members to make `WeaponDetails` a literal type, `std::clamp` for the two open-coded ammo clamps (Weapon.cpp:210-213, :221-224), and `[[nodiscard]]` on `WeaponBuilder::build_weapon` and `Weapon::update_and_get_projectiles` (discarding the latter silently drops the projectiles the player just fired - a plausible mistake given the name starts with `update_`).
findings.suggestion: Set `<LanguageStandard>stdcpp17</LanguageStandard>` (or stdcpp20) in all four configurations and turn on `<TreatWarningAsError>` so the dead-signature warnings cannot reaccumulate. Then apply `[[nodiscard]]` to the factory, `update_and_get_projectiles`, and the pure const accessors.
findings.verify_note: Grepped ArtAttack.vcxproj for LanguageStandard (no hits), PlatformToolset (v145), WarningLevel (Level4 x4), ConformanceMode (true x4), TreatWarningAsError (no hits).

findings.title: Protected data members punch through the accessors the class already provides
findings.suggestion: Make all three private with protected const accessors. Store the details as `const WeaponDetails*` into the single shared table once that table has external linkage, so the immutable data is neither copied per instance nor mutable after construction. Both subclass back-door uses disappear entirely once the sound mode is data-driven.
findings.verify_note: Read Weapon.h:46-50/:64, Weapon.cpp:23/:393-421, WeaponSniper.cpp:32-33, WeaponBucket.cpp:32-33, WeaponRoller.cpp:90.

findings.title: Dead accessors and never-set state leave unreachable branches in both draw functions
findings.detail:
Verified by grepping all of ArtAttack/ for call sites:
- `set_invert_x(bool)` (Weapon.h:74, Weapon.cpp:438) is **never called**, so `_invert_x` (Weapon.h:129) is permanently `false`. That makes the `if (invert_y && invert_x)` and `else if (invert_x)` branches at Weapon.cpp:48-59 and the duplicated copy at WeaponRoller.cpp:72-83 unreachable - `SpriteEffects_FlipBoth` and `SpriteEffects_FlipHorizontally` can never be selected.
- `_gun_player_aligned` (Weapon.h:131) is initialised `true` and the only call to `set_gun_player_aligned` in the whole codebase is `set_gun_player_aligned(true)` at WeaponRoller.cpp:42. So `bool normal_gun_ok_to_shoot = input.primary_shoot && get_gun_player_aligned();` (Weapon.cpp:194-195) is just `input.primary_shoot`, reached through a member, a getter, a setter and two aliases.
- `get_offset()` (Weapon.cpp:398), `get_nozzle_offset()` (:403) and `get_dt()` (:496) are defined and never called - the code uses `*this->_dt` directly at :193.
findings.suggestion: Delete all four members/accessors and the alias chain; collapse the effects selection to `invert_y ? SpriteEffects_FlipVertically : SpriteEffects_None`. If mirrored or aligned firing returns, it belongs in a render-state `flip` field and a `FireControl` precondition, not as permanent base-class state every weapon pays for.
findings.verify_note: Grepped the repo for set_invert_x / set_gun_player_aligned / get_offset() / get_nozzle_offset() / get_dt(): the only hits outside their own definitions are WeaponRoller.cpp:42. Read Weapon.cpp:45-59, :194-197, WeaponRoller.cpp:69-83.

findings.title: get_draw_pos() and get_wep_rotation_origin_offset() are two hand-maintained copies of the same mirroring rule, and neither mirrors the nozzle
findings.detail:
`get_draw_pos()` (:118-132) computes `facing_left ? (center.x - offset.x, center.y + offset.y) : center + offset`, and `get_wep_rotation_origin_offset(bool)` (:157-166) returns exactly that same offset as a vector. They are arithmetically identical (verified branch by branch) but written in different styles - mutate-in-place vs construct-and-return - so a reader is unlikely to notice, and they must stay in agreement or projectiles stop leaving the barrel, since `draw` consumes one and `get_nozzle_pos` the other.

Two further issues at the same site. (a) `get_nozzle_pos()` (:146-155) rotates `nozzle_offset` by `_rotation` but never applies `_invert_y`/`_invert_x`, even though `update_movement_and_rotation` sets `_invert_y = true` whenever the gun faces left (:302-310) and `draw` turns that into `SpriteEffects_FlipVertically`. The sprite is mirrored about the barrel axis; the computed muzzle is not. Dormant only because every weapon has `nozzle_offset.y == 0` (weapon_consts.h:40, 74, 90, 118, 152). (b) The parameter `bool facing_left` shadows the static member function `Weapon::facing_left(float)` (Weapon.h:94), so three lines apart the same identifier means two different things (:152 the function, :157 the parameter).
findings.suggestion: Delete `get_wep_rotation_origin_offset` and implement `get_draw_pos()` as `get_player_center() + <the one offset function>`. Better, give the weapon a single `Transform2D` (position + rotation + flip) that both the renderer and the muzzle query derive from, with an explicit `Vector2F muzzle_local` on the definition independent of sprite size - `_details.size.x` currently leaks art dimensions into where bullets spawn (:149).
findings.verify_note: Read Weapon.cpp:118-166 and :278-311, Weapon.h:94, weapon_consts.h nozzle_offset entries (all y == 0). Verified the two offset computations are identical for both branches.

findings.title: Weapon::calculate_sprite_origin is a second copy of Drawer::calculate_sprite_origin
findings.detail: `Weapon::calculate_sprite_origin(const Vector2F& size, rotation_origin origin)` (Weapon.cpp:88-101) is the same switch as `Drawer::calculate_sprite_origin` (Drawer.cpp:55-67): `CENTER -> Vector2F(size) / 2.0f`, `LEFT_CENTER -> {0, size.y/2}`, else `Vector2F::ZERO`. The only divergence is that Weapon's version spells out a `TOP_LEFT` case that falls through to the identical `default`. This is a pure engine-level sprite helper forked into a gameplay class, and both copies must be kept in sync with `rotation_origin`, which also has a `NO_ROTATION` value neither handles distinctly.
findings.suggestion: Hoist to a single free function in the draw module - `namespace sprite { Vector2F origin_for(const Vector2F& size, rotation_origin); }` - and have `Drawer` and the weapon renderer both call it. Handle every `rotation_origin` enumerator explicitly so adding one is a compile error, not a silent ZERO. In an engine-first codebase this clearly belongs in shared engine code.
findings.verify_note: Read Weapon.cpp:88-101 and Drawer.cpp:55-67 side by side; read projectile_details.h/rotation_origin usage confirming NO_ROTATION exists.

findings.title: Max ammo is a bare 1.0f in three places and does not track STARTING_AMMO
findings.detail: `weapon_consts::STARTING_AMMO = 1.0f` (weapon_consts.h:11) is used in exactly one place - the NSDMI at Weapon.h:126. The regen clamp writes the literal (`if (this->get_ammo() > 1.0f) { this->set_ammo(1.0f); }`, Weapon.cpp:221-224) and `Weapon::reset_ammo()` writes it again (`this->_ammo = 1.0f;`, :485). There is no `MAX_AMMO` constant at all. Change `STARTING_AMMO` to anything other than 1.0 and weapons spawn with ammo they can never regain, and `reset_ammo()` on respawn (Player.cpp:1000) silently *reduces* a full clip. Three independent spellings of one invariant.
findings.suggestion: Add `constexpr float MAX_AMMO = 1.0f;` to weapon_consts, clamp against it, and make `reset_ammo()` assign `STARTING_AMMO`. Replace both mutate-then-test clamps with a single `set_ammo(std::clamp(...))` once the project is on C++17.
findings.verify_note: Read weapon_consts.h:9-11, Weapon.h:126, Weapon.cpp:209-224 and :483-486, Player.cpp:992-1002.

findings.title: DETAILS_ROLLER.shoot_sound_volume = 3.0f is silently clamped to 1.0 and does nothing
findings.detail: `DETAILS_ROLLER` sets `3.0f, //shoot_sound_volume`. `WeaponRoller` does not override `handle_shoot_sound`, so it goes through `SoundBank::play_effect`, whose first statement is `clamp_levels(volume, pitch, pan)` (SoundBank.cpp:32), and `clamp_levels` does `volume = clamp(volume, 0.0f, 1.0f)` (SoundBank.cpp:174-178). `play_wave` clamps identically (SoundBank.cpp:18). So 3.0 becomes 1.0 with no diagnostic - whoever wrote it wanted the roller louder and got no indication the request was discarded. Every other weapon's volume (0.2-1.0) is in range, so this is the sole outlier and the config table now carries a value that is a lie.
findings.suggestion: Set it to 1.0f and fix the loudness in the asset, or raise the ceiling in `clamp_levels` (XAudio2 accepts gain > 1.0) if amplification is genuinely wanted. A constant should never silently disagree with the engine that consumes it.
findings.verify_note: Read weapon_consts.h:86-100 (roller has no handle_shoot_sound override - checked WeaponRoller.h:22-30), SoundBank.cpp:16-37 and :173-179.

findings.title: Cluster of unreferenced parameters through the virtual weapon interface (C4100 noise at /W4)
findings.detail:
Several signatures advertise dependencies their bodies do not have. With /W4 on and no TreatWarningAsError, these accumulate silently:
- `Weapon::check_if_shooting_and_ammo_update(PlayerInputData input, const Vector2F& player_center, const Vector2F& player_velocity)` (Weapon.cpp:188-235) uses only `input.primary_shoot`; both vectors are never referenced. It has no override anywhere, so these are pure noise - and `RelativeVelocityWeapon` faithfully forwards both (Weapon.cpp:585-586).
- `Weapon::update_movement_and_rotation` (:278-311) never uses `player_velocity`.
- `WeaponRoller::update_movement_and_rotation` (WeaponRoller.cpp:29-57) uses neither `input` nor `player_velocity`.
- `WeaponSniper::handle_shoot_sound` (WeaponSniper.cpp:28-35) and `WeaponBucket::handle_shoot_sound` (WeaponBucket.cpp:28-35) never use `holding_shoot`.

`PlayerInputData` is also taken **by value** at every layer (Weapon.h:36, 106, 110, 164; WeaponRoller.h:23) even though the caller already holds it by reference (`Player::get_input()`). It is ~48 bytes - three `Vector2F`, two floats, seven bools, an enum (PlayerInputData.h:7-23) - copied three times per weapon per tick to read two or three fields.
findings.suggestion: Delete `player_center`/`player_velocity` from `check_if_shooting_and_ammo_update` outright. For genuinely polymorphic signatures where an override ignores an argument, omit the parameter name (`bool /*holding_shoot*/`) so C4100 is suppressed deliberately. Take input by `const&`, or better by a narrow `WeaponIntent`. Turn on TreatWarningAsError.
findings.verify_note: Read each cited body and confirmed the parameters are unreferenced; read PlayerInputData.h and Player.cpp:742-750 confirming the caller has it by reference.

findings.title: wep_type mixes implemented weapons, unimplemented weapons, a menu sentinel and an array bound in one enum
findings.detail:
```
enum class wep_type { SPRAYER, SNIPER, ROLLER, MISTER, BUCKET, RANDOM_PRIMARY,
                      GRENADE_STD, MINE, CURLING, WATER, NONE,
                      MAX_PRIM_WEP = RANDOM_PRIMARY };
```
Only five can be built (WeaponBuilder.cpp:18-37 throws for the rest), yet `GRENADE_STD` is passed as a live value at PlayerBuilder.cpp:55 and stored in `Player::_secondary_type` with no weapon object behind it. `RANDOM_PRIMARY` is not a weapon but a menu option, resolved at MainMenu.cpp:1499. `MAX_PRIM_WEP` is an aliased sentinel used as an *exclusive* bound - `rand() % static_cast<int>(wep_type::MAX_PRIM_WEP)` (MainMenu.cpp:1521, also :1527) yields 0-4, correct only because the name says MAX when it means COUNT; it is also written last, after `NONE = 10`, so it reads as the largest enumerator. Enum ordering is therefore load-bearing for the menu's random pick: inserting a weapon before RANDOM_PRIMARY silently changes it.

The same enum simultaneously means "class to instantiate", "menu option", "stored identity tag" and "array bound".
findings.suggestion: Split the concerns: an engine-side opaque `weapon_id` resolved by a registry for instantiation, and a separate game-side menu enum including RANDOM, with an explicit `constexpr std::array<weapon_id, N> SELECTABLE_PRIMARIES` for the random pick instead of enum arithmetic. Rename the sentinel `PRIMARY_WEAPON_COUNT` or move it out of the enum entirely.
findings.verify_note: Read wep_type.h, WeaponBuilder.cpp:16-40, MainMenu.cpp:1499/:1521/:1527/:1583-1612, PlayerBuilder.cpp:55.

findings.title: wep_type is both the factory discriminator and a constructor parameter, so a weapon can be built with the wrong type tag
findings.detail:
`build_weapon` switches on `type` to choose the class and then hands the same `type` back into the constructor, which stores it in `Weapon::_type` (Weapon.h:138):
```
case wep_type::SPRAYER:
    return std::make_unique<WeaponSprayer>(team, player_num, team_colour, type, player_center, resource_manager, dt);
```
Nothing prevents `WeaponSprayer(team, num, col, wep_type::ROLLER, ...)` from compiling and running - it would produce a sprayer that plays and stops `"roller_a0"`, two weapons fighting over one `SoundEffectInstance`, because `_type` is the sole key used by `get_sound_effect_instance_name()` (Weapon.cpp:258-277). The class already knows what it is: `WeaponSprayer` hardcodes `DETAILS_SPRAYER` (WeaponSprayer.cpp:20). The parameter is a redundant second source of truth for the same fact, kept in sync only because `WeaponBuilder` is the only caller and happens to pass what it dispatched on.
findings.suggestion: Drop `wep_type` from all five concrete constructors and have each subclass pass its own literal up to `Weapon` alongside its `DETAILS_*`, exactly as it already does for the details - or fold the tag into `WeaponDetails` so the two cannot disagree at all. Best: remove `_type` entirely once the audio configuration is data-driven; a class knows what it is.
findings.verify_note: Read WeaponBuilder.cpp:16-40, all five subclass constructors (each hardcodes its own DETAILS_* while forwarding the caller's `type`), Weapon.cpp:29 and :258-277.

findings.title: Unscoped projectile_type enum leaks SPRAY/JET/BALL/MIST/ROLLING into the global namespace
findings.detail: `WeaponDetails` stores `projectile_type proj_type = SPRAY;`, and weapon_consts.h initialises it with bare global identifiers at :24 (`SPRAY`), :46 (`SPRAY`), :80 (`JET`), :96 (`ROLLING`), :124 (`MIST`), :158 (`BALL`). These come from `enum projectile_type` (Projectile.h:10-17), which is unscoped - the only unscoped enum in a codebase that otherwise uses `enum class` consistently (`wep_type`, `add_player_velocity` in this very header at :7, `rotation_origin`, `player_team`, `diffusion_type`). Five extremely generic names are injected into the global namespace of every TU that includes Weapon.h, and they implicitly convert to `int`. That last part makes the positional aggregate initialisers more dangerous than they look: `projectile_type` sits between `float ammo_usage` and `std::string sheet_name` in the member order, so a misordered brace-list can silently initialise a float from an enumerator.
findings.suggestion: Change it to `enum class projectile_type` and qualify the six use sites in weapon_consts.h. Six edits, and it removes an implicit-conversion hazard from every aggregate initialiser in both consts headers.
findings.verify_note: Read Projectile.h:10-17 (unscoped), WeaponDetails.h:7-13/:35-49, weapon_consts.h bare enumerator use sites at the cited lines.

findings.title: Weapon.h drags the whole projectile hierarchy into every consumer and relies on a four-level transitive chain for rotation_origin
findings.detail:
`rotation_origin` is used in the declaration at Weapon.h:104 with **no** include for it - it arrives only via WeaponDetails.h -> Projectile.h -> projectile_consts.h -> projectile_details.h -> rotation_origin.h. Reordering any of those headers breaks this one.

The expensive include is `#include "ProjectileBuilder.h"` (Weapon.h:11), needed only for the `std::unique_ptr<ProjectileBuilder> _proj_builder` member. ProjectileBuilder.h includes all five concrete projectile headers (ProjectileBuilder.h:4-9), so every TU that includes Player.h (which includes Weapon.h) compiles the entire projectile hierarchy, and a change to any projectile recompiles the whole weapon module. WeaponBuilder.h:4-8 repeats the pattern with all five concrete weapon headers.
findings.suggestion: Add `#include "rotation_origin.h"` directly. Forward-declare `class ProjectileBuilder;` and declare an out-of-line `~Weapon();` so the unique_ptr deleter is not instantiated in the header, moving the ProjectileBuilder.h include into Weapon.cpp - or delete the member entirely per the stateless-builder finding, which removes the include outright.
findings.verify_note: Read Weapon.h:1-12 and :104, ProjectileBuilder.h:1-9, WeaponBuilder.h:4-8, and traced the rotation_origin chain through WeaponDetails.h -> Projectile.h -> projectile_consts.h -> projectile_details.h:4.

findings.title: Polymorphic bases are implicitly movable, so slicing compiles
findings.detail: `class Weapon : public TextureObject` and `class RelativeVelocityWeapon : public Weapon` are polymorphic bases with `final` leaves, but neither declares any special member. Copy construction is blocked only as a side effect of the `std::unique_ptr<ProjectileBuilder>` member (Weapon.h:122) - not by intent, so deleting that member (which the stateless-builder finding recommends) silently re-enables slicing copies. Move is available today: `DrawObject` has a user-declared destructor (`virtual ~DrawObject() = default;`, DrawObject.h:9) which suppresses its move operations but leaves its copy constructor implicitly generated, and `Weapon`'s own members are all movable - so `Weapon w = std::move(*some_weapon_sniper);` compiles and slices a `WeaponSniper` down to a `Weapon`. The intended ownership model is `std::unique_ptr<Weapon>` throughout (WeaponBuilder.cpp:19-37, Player.h:142), so value semantics on these types should be impossible rather than accidental.
findings.suggestion: Add an explicit deleted special-member block to `Weapon` and `RelativeVelocityWeapon` (copy and move ctor/assign). The same treatment belongs on `DrawObject`/`SpriteSheetObject`/`TextureObject`, which are the actual slicing surface.
findings.verify_note: Read Weapon.h (no special members declared), DrawObject.h:9 (user-declared virtual defaulted destructor), TextureObject.h / SpriteSheetObject.h (no special members). Traced implicit move-ctor availability through the chain.

findings.title: Weapon::draw hides the inherited TextureObject::draw overloads, forcing qualification that defeats dispatch
findings.detail: `Weapon` declares `virtual void draw(SpriteBatch*, const Camera&, bool debug = false)` and `virtual void draw(SpriteBatch*, bool debug = false)`. These are new names in the derived scope, so they hide the five inherited `TextureObject::draw` overloads (TextureObject.h:20-32). The workaround is visible throughout: every internal call must be explicitly qualified - `TextureObject::draw(sprite_batch, draw_rectangle, camera)` (Weapon.cpp:66, :80; WeaponRoller.cpp:99, :113). Explicit qualification on a virtual also defeats virtual dispatch, so any future `TextureObject::draw` override would be silently bypassed. The same qualification habit is applied inconsistently to the setters - `DrawObject::set_origin` at Weapon.cpp:62 and `TextureObject::set_origin` at :76 name the same function.
findings.suggestion: Add `using TextureObject::draw;` in Weapon's protected section and drop the class qualification from the call sites. The two-argument `draw(SpriteBatch*, bool)` overload should just be deleted - it only forwards to the camera version with `Camera::DEFAULT_CAMERA` (Weapon.cpp:83-86), which the caller can pass itself.
findings.verify_note: Read Weapon.h:31-33, TextureObject.h:19-32 (five protected virtual draw overloads), Weapon.cpp:61-86, WeaponRoller.cpp:85-114.

findings.title: Every shot heap-allocates a transport vector the caller immediately empties, and the mist path never reserves
findings.detail: `update_and_get_projectiles` returns `std::vector<std::unique_ptr<ICollisionGameObject>>` by value and both `shoot` implementations build a fresh one per call (Weapon.cpp:313-328, :552-574). The caller does `for (auto& proj : new_projs) this->_collision_objects->push_back(std::move(proj));` (Level.cpp:204-210) and destroys the vector - it exists purely as a transport buffer, allocated and freed 60 times a second per player given `shoot_interval == 0.0f` on the sprayer. Inside, `ProjectileBuilder::build_mist_projectiles` (ProjectileBuilder.cpp:131-201) does five `push_back`s on a default-constructed vector with no `reserve(5)`, so it reallocates at capacities 1->2->4->8: three extra allocations plus three moves per mist shot, 10 shots/second/player. Both `return std::vector<std::unique_ptr<ICollisionGameObject>>();` sites (:184, :593) also spell out the full type where `return {};` says the same thing.
findings.suggestion: Change the signature to append into a caller-supplied container - `void update_and_append_projectiles(..., std::vector<std::unique_ptr<ICollisionGameObject>>& out)` with `Level` passing `*_collision_objects` - so there is no transport allocation and the projectiles land where they are going in one move. At minimum add `projectiles.reserve(5)` in `build_mist_projectiles`.
findings.verify_note: Read Weapon.cpp:168-186/:313-328/:552-574, Level.cpp:203-211, ProjectileBuilder.cpp:131-201 (five push_backs, no reserve).

findings.title: Needless local copies in the per-shot path
findings.detail: `RelativeVelocityWeapon::shoot` opens with `RelativeWeaponDetails rel_details = this->_rel_details;` (:556) followed by `add_player_velocity add_player_vel = rel_details.add_vel;` (:558) - copying a member inside a `const` function that could read `_rel_details.add_vel` and `_rel_details.player_vel_amount` directly. Similarly `Weapon::calculate_sprite_origin` writes `return Vector2F(size) / 2.0f;` (:93) where `size` is already a `const Vector2F&`, so the explicit `Vector2F(...)` is a redundant copy-construct before the division (the same expression is duplicated in Drawer.cpp:61).
findings.suggestion: Read the members directly, drop the `Vector2F(...)` wrapper, and use `return {};` for the two empty-vector returns.
findings.verify_note: Read Weapon.cpp:88-101 and :552-574.

findings.title: Weapon asset names are string literals duplicated across three files with no load-time validation
findings.detail: Each `WeaponDetails` entry hardcodes `sheet_name`/`frame_name`/`sound_bank_name`/`shoot_sound_name` as literals (e.g. weapon_consts.h:44-48 `"sprite_sheet_1", "sprayer", ..., "sound_bank_1", "WaterSprayIntoBucket"`), and the three `SoundEffectInstanceWeaponDetails` tables (:58-68, :102-112, :136-146) hardcode 24 more instance names. Every one must match an entry in `ArtAttack/sounds/sound_bank_1.json` (spot-checked: `sprayer_a0` -> wave `WaterSprayIntoBucket` at lines 33-34, currently correct) and every frame name a sprite-sheet entry. Nothing checks either. A rename on the sound side becomes an `std::out_of_range` thrown mid-frame from `handle_shoot_sound` with no catch on the path; a rename on the texture side is worse - `SpriteSheet::draw`'s `_sprite_frames[frame_name]` silently *inserts* a default frame and the weapon just goes invisible with no diagnostic at all.
findings.suggestion: Add a one-shot validation pass after resource loading that walks the weapon tables and asserts every referenced sheet/frame/bank/instance name resolves, failing with a message naming the offending weapon and key. Better, move the weapon table into JSON alongside the assets it references. Make `SpriteSheet::draw` use `find()` and report a missing frame rather than inserting one.
findings.verify_note: Read weapon_consts.h asset strings, checked sounds/sound_bank_1.json:25/:33-62 for the sprayer names, read SoundBank.cpp:74 (get_sound_effect_instance) and ResourceManager.cpp:46-58. Severity lowered from medium: the names currently all match, so this is a guardrail gap rather than a live defect.

findings.title: get_delete_timer() returns _timer, so the lifetime check is `_timer > _timer` and no projectile ever expires
findings.detail:
Verified verbatim. `float Projectile::get_delete_timer() const { return this->_timer; }` (Projectile.cpp:285-288) returns the elapsed timer instead of `_details.delete_timer`. The sole caller is `if (this->get_timer() > this->get_delete_timer())` at Projectile.cpp:278, and `get_timer()` (line 220-223) also returns `_timer` — so the test is a strict self-comparison and is never true. Grep confirms `ProjectileDetails::delete_timer` (projectile_details.h:12) is written at projectile_consts.h:19,32,53,66,79,100 and read nowhere.

Consequences I traced end to end:
- The only removal path left is `Projectile::on_collision` (Projectile.cpp:120-154), which sets deletion on a structure or enemy-player hit.
- `DETAILS_JET` and `DETAILS_MIST` have `gravity = 0.0f, wind_resistance = 0.0f` (projectile_consts.h:50-51, 76-77), so a missed jet/mist shot flies dead straight forever.
- `Level::update_level_logic` responds to anything leaving the level with `throw std::exception("Collision object out of bounds")` (Level.cpp:315-321). I grepped every `catch` in ArtAttack/*.cpp: the only handlers are in Level.cpp:727 (bad_cast), ResourceLoader, ResourceManager and SoundBank. There is no handler on the update path, so a missed shot terminates the process.
- Survivors accumulate in `_collision_objects`, which is walked object-vs-object in a full O(n^2) double loop every frame (Level.cpp:259-293).

Secondary defect confirmed in the same block: the expiry test at line 278 runs before `alter_timer(dt)` at line 282, so even once fixed a projectile survives one frame past its deadline.

Merged from 5 duplicate candidate reports (all naming Projectile.cpp:278-288).
findings.suggestion: `return this->get_details().delete_timer;`, and move the test after `alter_timer(dt)`. Rename the pair to `get_age()` / `get_lifetime()` (or collapse both into `bool has_expired() const`) so the self-comparison becomes unwritable. Separately, `Level::is_object_out_of_bounds` must mark transient objects for deletion, not throw — an escaped projectile is not an exceptional condition, and today it is a guaranteed process kill.
findings.verify_note: Read Projectile.cpp:220-298 — both accessors return `_timer`. Grepped `delete_timer` repo-wide: only the struct field, the six initialisers in projectile_consts.h, and these two lines. Read Level.cpp:296-321 to confirm the swap-and-pop deletion loop and the unconditional `throw` for out-of-bounds collision objects. Grepped `catch` across ArtAttack/*.cpp to confirm no handler on the update path.

findings.title: ProjectileMist constructs its base with `SPRAY` as its projectile_type
findings.detail:
Verified: ProjectileMist.cpp:19-22 passes `SPRAY` as the fifth base-constructor argument where the type tag belongs. Cross-checked every sibling — ProjectileSpray.cpp:20 `SPRAY`, ProjectileJet.cpp:20 `JET`, ProjectileBall.cpp:20 `BALL`, ProjectileRolling.cpp:20 `ROLLING`. Mist is the only one wrong.

`Projectile::get_collision_object_type()` (Projectile.cpp:155-195) switches on the stored `_type`, so every mist particle reports `PROJECTILE_SPRAY_TEAM_A/B`. Downstream:
- `Player::on_projectile_collision` (Player.cpp:649-654) applies `SPRAY_DAMAGE` instead of `MIST_DAMAGE`. Both are 0.01f today (player_consts.h:65,69), so the bug is currently invisible and will surface the instant either constant is tuned.
- `PaintTile::on_collision` (PaintTile.cpp:118-133) and `StructurePaintable::on_collision` classify mist as spray.
- `collision_object_type::PROJECTILE_MIST_TEAM_A/B` (collision_object_type.h:23-24) are unreachable at runtime, so the mist branches at Player.cpp:673-678 and in every other ladder are dead code.

Contributing cause, verified: `ProjectileBuilder::build_mist_projectiles` takes a `projectile_type type` parameter (ProjectileBuilder.h:36, ProjectileBuilder.cpp:123) that its body never references — the caller at ProjectileBuilder.cpp:86 forwards `MIST` and the function discards it. That is also a live C4100 under /W4.

Merged from 4 duplicate candidate reports.
findings.suggestion: Pass `MIST`. Then remove the cause: the type tag is a fixed property of the concrete class, so it should not be a hand-copied constructor argument at all — either make it a pure virtual `projectile_type get_type() const` implemented once per leaf, or (better) add the identity to `ProjectileDetails` so `DETAILS_MIST` carries it and the tuning data and the tag cannot disagree. Delete the unused `type` parameter from `build_mist_projectiles`.
findings.verify_note: Read ProjectileMist.cpp:19-22 and all four sibling constructors. Read Projectile.cpp:155-195 (the switch on `get_type()`), Player.cpp:645-682 and player_consts.h:65-69 to confirm SPRAY_DAMAGE == MIST_DAMAGE == 0.01f. Read ProjectileBuilder.cpp:116-201 and confirmed `type` is never referenced in the body.

findings.title: ProjectileRolling never applies its displacement and never advances its animation — the roller emits stationary invisible hitboxes
findings.detail:
Verified. `ProjectileRolling::update()` (lines 29-35) is:
```cpp
const ProjectileDetails& details = this->get_details();
Projectile::update_movement(details.gravity, details.wind_resistance);
```
and stops there. `Projectile::update_movement` only *computes* the displacement into `MovingObject::_dx` (Projectile.cpp:275-276); applying it is each subclass's job. All four siblings do it — ProjectileSpray.cpp:39-40, ProjectileJet.cpp:37-38, ProjectileMist.cpp:39-40, ProjectileBall.cpp:37-38 all call `_rectangle.offset(get_dx_x(), get_dx_y())`, and all four also call `AnimationObject::update()`. Rolling does neither, so its collision rectangle never leaves the spawn point and its animation is frozen.

It is also inert on the render side: both `draw` overloads are `// do nothing` (lines 36-43) and `is_visible_in_viewport` returns a hardcoded `false` (line 44-47).

Surrounding data confirms the weapon is broken end to end: `DETAILS_ROLLER.starting_vel_length = 0.0f` and `shoot_interval = 0.0001f` (weapon_consts.h:91-92), `DETAILS_ROLLING` has `gravity = 0.0f, wind_resistance = 0.0f, delete_timer = 0.000001f, player_damage = -1000.0f` (projectile_consts.h:63-67). The tiny delete_timer shows the intent was a one-frame melee volume; the broken `get_delete_timer()` means that intent is never honoured.

I am tempering one claim several reviewers made: these volumes are NOT permanently immortal in all cases. `Projectile::on_collision` still deletes them on contact with any structure or enemy player, so a volume spawned overlapping the ground dies immediately. Only a volume spawned touching nothing persists indefinitely. The class is still functionally broken.

Merged from 3 duplicate candidate reports (two filed as correctness, one as design).
findings.suggestion: Decide what this type is. If it is a projectile, apply the offset and call `AnimationObject::update()` like every sibling, implement the draw overloads, and give it non-degenerate velocity/gravity/lifetime. If it is a one-frame melee volume — which the data says — it should not derive from `Projectile`/`MovingObject`/`AnimationObject` at all: an engine-level `HitVolume` (shape + payload + lifetime, no sprite, no velocity) implementing only `ICollisionGameObject` is the right type, and it should `set_for_deletion(true)` at the end of its first update. The reason this was forgettable is that the same `_rectangle.offset(...)` line is duplicated across five subclasses — see the finding on hoisting the shape into `Projectile`.
findings.verify_note: Read ProjectileRolling.cpp in full and diffed update()/draw() against all four siblings. Read projectile_consts.h:61-72 and weapon_consts.h:86-92 for the degenerate tuning values. Re-read Projectile::on_collision (Projectile.cpp:120-154) to check the 'immortal' claim — it does still delete on structure/enemy contact, so I downgraded that part of the reviewers' consequence.

findings.title: Projectile's hand-rolled structure filter omits both ramp types, so projectiles fly through every ramp in the shipped level
findings.detail:
Verified. `is_matching_collision_object_type` (Projectile.cpp:98-101) hand-writes:
```cpp
bool structure_collision =
    other_type == collision_object_type::STRUCTURE ||
    other_type == collision_object_type::STRUCTURE_PAINTABLE ||
    other_type == collision_object_type::STRUCTURE_JUMP_THROUGH;
```
`collision_object_type` has five structure enumerators (collision_object_type.h:6-10); this list covers three. For a ramp, `structure_collision` is false and the team switch then asks `other_type == PLAYER_TEAM_A/B`, which is also false. Every projectile's `is_colliding` short-circuits on this predicate first (ProjectileSpray.cpp:59, ProjectileJet.cpp:57, ProjectileBall.cpp:58, ProjectileMist.cpp:59, ProjectileRolling.cpp:51), so no projectile of any kind can hit a ramp.

The correct predicate already exists and is not used: `inline bool is_structure(collision_object_type)` at collision_object_type.h:75-82 lists all five, including the ramps. `Level::update_level_logic` itself calls that function (Level.cpp:238) — the projectile code is the outlier.

This is live content, not theoretical: `ArtAttack/levels/king_of_the_hill.json:271` declares `STRUCTURE_RAMP` collision types. Players collide with ramps; bullets pass through and ramps never take paint.

The identical hand-written list is duplicated 25 lines below in `on_collision` (Projectile.cpp:124-127), so both copies carry the same omission.

Merged from 2 duplicate candidate reports.
findings.suggestion: Replace both hand-written blocks with the existing `is_structure(other_type)` — it is already `inline` in the header, so there is no call cost. Then delete the duplicate entirely by reducing `on_collision` to `set_for_deletion(is_matching_collision_object_type(other));`. Longer term this should not be an enum whitelist at all — see the collision-filter finding.
findings.verify_note: Read Projectile.cpp:93-154 and collision_object_type.h in full; confirmed is_structure() covers STRUCTURE_RAMP_LEFT/RIGHT and the projectile copies do not. Grepped king_of_the_hill.json for STRUCTURE_RAMP — present at line 271. Confirmed all five leaf is_colliding bodies gate on this predicate first.

findings.title: Splatoon team rules are baked into the projectile base class, blocking the engine-reuse goal
findings.detail:
Verified against the header. `Projectile.h:4` includes `player_team.h`; the constructor (lines 24-36) takes `player_team team, int player_num, const Colour& team_colour, projectile_type type`; the class stores all four as members (lines 72-76). `Projectile.cpp:110-118` and `:136-152` then hard-switch `case player_team::A: / case player_team::B: / default: throw`, so a two-team King-of-the-Hill ruleset is a compile-time dependency of what should be the engine's generic 'moving thing that hits stuff'. Free-for-all, 3+ teams, PvE and neutral projectiles are literally unrepresentable, and `player_team::NONE` — the default value of `_team` at Projectile.h:76 — throws on the first collision query.

Two of the four members are provably dead weight: I grepped `Projectile::get_player_num` and `Projectile::get_team_colour` repo-wide and found only the declarations (Projectile.h:60-61) and definitions (Projectile.cpp:208-215). No caller. `_team_colour` is also pure duplicated state — every leaf constructor passes the same `team_colour` argument twice, once as the `Projectile` team colour and once as the `DrawObject` `color` (e.g. ProjectileSpray.cpp:19-22), and `DrawObject` already stores it as `_colour` (DrawObject.h:37).

Merged with the near-duplicate candidate reporting the duplicated team colour and dead `_player_num`.
findings.suggestion: Split the class along the engine/game seam. Engine layer: a `Projectile` that knows shape, velocity, lifetime, a sprite, an opaque `owner_id`, and a `CollisionFilter { uint32_t layer; uint32_t mask; }`. Game layer: a payload struct the engine carries but never interprets — `struct PaintPayload { TeamId team; Colour colour; float damage; }`. `player_team.h` must not appear in any header the engine ships. Delete `_team_colour` and `_player_num` and their dead accessors outright.
findings.verify_note: Read Projectile.h in full and Projectile.cpp:7-31, 108-154, 208-215. Grepped get_player_num/get_team_colour repo-wide — the only hits on Projectile's versions are its own declaration and definition; all other hits belong to Player, Weapon, PauseMenuData and TeamColour. Read DrawObject.h:37 and ProjectileSpray.cpp:19-22 to confirm the double-passed colour.

findings.title: collision_object_type is a team x weapon cross-product enum, re-expanded by hand in six places
findings.detail:
Verified. `Projectile::get_collision_object_type()` is a 40-line nested switch mapping 2 teams x 5 projectile types onto ten distinct enumerators, with three `throw std::exception` fallbacks (lines 174, 190, 193). Object identity is therefore a flat enum that multiplies class by team, and every consumer re-expands that cross product by hand. I confirmed all the expansion sites:
- `collision_object_type.h:43-73` — three separate predicates `is_projectile`, `is_team_a_projectile`, `is_team_b_projectile`, each listing all ten/five values.
- `Player::on_projectile_collision` (Player.cpp:645-682) — a 5-branch ladder over pairs, ending in `throw std::exception("Invalid projectile type.")`.
- `PaintTile::on_collision` (PaintTile.cpp:114-137) — re-derives the attacker's team from the same ten values, also ending in a throw.
- `StructurePaintable::on_collision`, `Player::on_collision`.

Adding one weapon type means editing at least six files; adding a third team doubles the enum. For a project whose stated goal is a reusable engine, this is the single structural decision that makes the projectile system unextensible.
findings.suggestion: Replace the identity enum with a collision filter: `get_collision_filter()` returning `{ layer, mask }` bitmasks, where 'projectile' is one layer bit and team membership is a bit in a separate team mask. The cross product disappears. Where a target genuinely needs to know what hit it, give `ICollisionGameObject` a virtual returning a game-side payload pointer rather than forcing the target to reverse-engineer the attacker from an enum. `is_team_a_projectile`/`is_team_b_projectile` and all five hand expansions then delete.
findings.verify_note: Read Projectile.cpp:155-195, collision_object_type.h:43-73, Player.cpp:645-682 and PaintTile.cpp:114-137. All the claimed duplicate expansions exist as described.

findings.title: Each object hardcodes its own slice of the collision matrix, and the resulting relation is asymmetric
findings.detail:
Verified. `Projectile::is_matching_collision_object_type` encodes inside the projectile class exactly which of the 23 `collision_object_type` values a projectile may interact with. Two verified consequences:

(a) `PAINT_TILE` is absent from the list, so a projectile always answers 'no' to a paint tile. Painting only works because `PaintTile::is_colliding` (PaintTile.cpp:84-109) has **no type filter at all** — it collides with literally anything. `Level::update_level_logic` calls both orderings (`object->is_colliding(object_2.get())` at Level.cpp:287 inside a loop that visits every ordered pair), so the effective rule is 'collide if either side says yes'. `a->is_colliding(b)` and `b->is_colliding(a)` genuinely disagree here.

(b) `STRUCTURE_RAMP_LEFT/RIGHT` are absent — see the separate ramp finding.

The knowledge of who-hits-what is scattered across every object rather than living in one place, which is precisely why it has already drifted twice.
findings.suggestion: Move filtering out of the objects and into the collision system: one `CollisionFilter` (layer + mask) per object and one `bool should_test(a, b) { return (a.layer & b.mask) && (b.layer & a.mask); }` evaluated once per pair by the broad phase. That makes the relation symmetric by construction, makes 'projectiles now hit ramps' a one-bit data change, and deletes `is_matching_collision_object_type` from all five projectile leaves plus Player and PaintTile.
findings.verify_note: Read Projectile.cpp:93-119, PaintTile.cpp:84-109 (confirmed no type filter), and Level.cpp:259-293 (confirmed both orderings are tested for every ordered pair, and on_collision is invoked on both objects).

findings.title: The same 32-line is_colliding() is copy-pasted into all five projectile leaves (and again into Player and PaintTile)
findings.detail:
Verified byte-for-byte identical, including the comments, at ProjectileSpray.cpp:56-87, ProjectileJet.cpp:54-85, ProjectileBall.cpp:55-86, ProjectileMist.cpp:56-87 and ProjectileRolling.cpp:48-79; near-identical (minus the type filter) at PaintTile.cpp:84-109 and in Player.cpp. Nothing in the body is projectile-specific: it is generic narrow-phase dispatch pasted into seven leaf classes.

Because it is duplicated, the 'if other is a RECTANGLE, the passed AABB test means a hit' shortcut — only sound when `this` is itself an AABB — is now wrong in seven places instead of one.

Performance detail confirmed while reading it: each call invokes the virtual `this->get_shape()` up to 3 times and `other->get_shape()` up to 4 times with no hoisting. `Shape::AABB_intersects` (MattMath.cpp:143-146) is `get_bounding_box().intersects(other->get_bounding_box())`, and `get_bounding_box()` is `virtual RectangleF ... const = 0` (MattMath.h:71) returning a **polymorphic RectangleF by value** — two vtable-carrying temporaries per test, when for a projectile `this` already *is* a RectangleF. When `other` is not a rectangle (ramps are triangles), the fall-through reaches `Shape::intersects` (MattMath.cpp:119-136), which performs a `dynamic_cast` per switch branch — an RTTI lookup in the innermost loop of the O(n^2) pass at Level.cpp:277-292.

Merged from 2 candidate reports (one design, one performance).
findings.suggestion: `is_colliding` should not be a virtual on every game object. Put one `bool shapes_overlap(const Shape&, const Shape&)` in the collision module, have the level call it, and delete the override from all seven leaves. At minimum hoist `const Shape* self = get_shape(); const Shape* o = other->get_shape();`. In `Shape::intersects`, replace the `dynamic_cast` chain with `static_cast` — the switch on `get_shape_type()` has already established the dynamic type.
findings.verify_note: Read all five leaf is_colliding bodies and PaintTile.cpp:84-109 — identical apart from the type-filter prologue. Read MattMath.cpp:119-151 (dynamic_cast chain, AABB_intersects) and MattMath.h:71 (virtual RectangleF get_bounding_box() const = 0, returned by value).

findings.title: The collision shape lives in the leaves, so five subclasses exist only to re-declare the same RectangleF
findings.detail:
Verified. Every concrete projectile privately declares `MattMath::RectangleF _rectangle = MattMath::RectangleF::ZERO;` (ProjectileBall.h:31, ProjectileJet.h:31, ProjectileSpray.h:31, ProjectileMist.h:31, ProjectileRolling.h:30) and therefore must re-implement `update`, both `draw` overloads, `is_visible_in_viewport`, `is_colliding` and `get_shape` — all pure boilerplate over that one member. `Projectile` declares five of those as `= 0` (Projectile.h:38-46) purely because it refuses to own the shape.

I diffed the files directly: ProjectileJet.cpp:30-53 and ProjectileBall.cpp:30-54 are identical modulo whitespace; ProjectileSpray.cpp:30-51 and ProjectileMist.cpp:30-51 differ by nothing at all. The complete behavioural difference across four of the five classes is which `DETAILS_*` constant goes to the base constructor, plus one extra `inflate_to_size(calculate_diffusion_size())` line for the two diffusing ones.

The repeated constructor tail is duplicated the same way — `Vector2F size = get_details().col_rect_size; _rectangle.offset(-size.x/2, -size.y/2);` appears verbatim in all five (ProjectileSpray.cpp:25-27 and equivalents), and it also copies the Vector2F instead of binding a const reference. So does the `update()` prologue that reads two fields out of `_details` and hands them back to the base.

Merged with the candidate reporting the `DiffusingProjectile` inheritance level, which adds one member and one function and re-declares four pure virtuals a third time (Projectile.h:102-108) for no effect.
findings.suggestion: Move `_rectangle` into `Projectile` (all five leaves use a rectangle) and implement `update()`, both `draw`s, `is_visible_in_viewport`, `get_shape` and the centring offset once in the base, with a small protected `virtual void update_shape()` hook for the diffusion case. Fold `DiffusionDetails` onto `ProjectileDetails` behind the already-present `diffusion_type::NO_DIFFUSION` and delete `DiffusingProjectile`. Four of the five subclasses then vanish, replaced by a data record.
findings.verify_note: Read all five leaf headers and all five leaf .cpp files in full; the duplication is exactly as described. Read Projectile.h:82-114 to confirm DiffusingProjectile adds one member (_diffusion_details), one protected function, one private function, and re-declares four already-pure virtuals.

findings.title: Projectiles are class-per-variant behind a switch factory, while the rest of the engine is already data-driven
findings.detail:
Verified. Adding one projectile requires edits in at least five places: an enumerator in `enum projectile_type` (Projectile.h:10-17), a `DETAILS_*` blob in projectile_consts.h, a new `case` block in `build_projectiles` (ProjectileBuilder.cpp:23-113), two enumerators in `collision_object_type`, and two branches in `Projectile::get_collision_object_type`. The four non-mist case bodies (lines 25-42, 43-60, 61-78, 93-110) are the same eight statements four times, differing only in the concrete type and the `DETAILS_*` constant.

Meanwhile the actual variation between the five projectiles is 6 floats, 2 Vector2Fs and 2 strings — precisely `ProjectileDetails`. And the engine already has a data pipeline: levels, sprite sheets and sound banks all load through rapidjson (LevelObjectBuilder.cpp, SpriteSheet.cpp, SoundBank.cpp), yet projectile and weapon tuning is compiled in, so retuning a weapon requires a rebuild.

Merged with the candidate on the hand-unrolled mist spread: `build_mist_projectiles` (ProjectileBuilder.cpp:131-201) is five copy-pasted 14-line blocks differing only in the rotation — `0`, `+PI/12`, `-PI/12`, `+PI/6`, `-PI/6`. 70 lines encoding a 5-element array of angles, with the pellet count and spread baked into the shape of the code. It is also the sole reason `build_mist_projectiles` exists as a separate function. There is no `reserve(5)`, so the vector reallocates three times per shot, and `Level` then re-pushes the results one at a time into the live `_collision_objects` (Level.cpp:207-210).
findings.suggestion: Load `ProjectileDetails`/`DiffusionDetails` from JSON through the existing rapidjson path into a `std::unordered_map<std::string, ProjectileDefinition>`, and make the factory `spawn(const ProjectileDefinition&, const SpawnParams&)` returning one generic `Projectile`. Add `int pellet_count` and `float spread_radians` to the definition and emit the spread in a loop with a `reserve(pellet_count)`. `enum projectile_type`, the switch, and `build_mist_projectiles` all disappear. In `Level`, use a single `insert` with move iterators instead of the per-element push_back loop.
findings.verify_note: Read ProjectileBuilder.cpp in full — the four duplicated case bodies and the five duplicated mist blocks are exactly as described, with no reserve. Read Level.cpp:203-213 for the per-element push_back into the live collision vector.

findings.title: A projectile's only hit response is a bool; its actual effect is implemented by whatever it hits
findings.detail:
Verified. `Projectile::on_collision` does exactly one thing — `set_for_deletion(true)` — after re-deriving, for the second time in the same file, the structure/enemy-player predicate that `is_matching_collision_object_type` computed 30 lines earlier (compare Projectile.cpp:98-101 with :124-127; identical text).

Everything a projectile actually *does* lives in the target: `Player::on_projectile_collision` (Player.cpp:645-682) picks the damage by inspecting the attacker's enum; `StructurePaintable::on_collision` decides a paint splat happens and plays the sound; `PaintTile::on_collision` (PaintTile.cpp:114-138) re-derives the attacker's team from the same enum a third time. A projectile therefore cannot introduce a new effect — bounce, explode, splash radius, freeze — without editing every class it might touch. This responsibility inversion is what makes the type enum load-bearing.

Merged with the candidate noting that `on_collision` re-implements the type filter instead of calling the `virtual` predicate declared at Projectile.h:58. Because it duplicates rather than delegates, any subclass that overrides the virtual — the reason it is virtual — collides with the new type but is silently not consumed by it. Both copies also `throw std::exception("Invalid player_team value.")` on `player_team::NONE`, which is the default value of `_team` (Projectile.h:76), from inside the O(n^2) collision loop.
findings.suggestion: Collapse the body to `if (this->is_matching_collision_object_type(other)) this->set_for_deletion(true);` — one source of truth, and the virtual starts meaning something. Then give the projectile a payload it carries and the collision system applies: `struct HitPayload { float damage; Colour paint_colour; TeamId team; }` exposed as `const HitPayload& get_payload() const`. Targets implement `apply(const HitPayload&)` and stop inspecting the attacker's type. Drop the `NONE` throws by making team a required construction-time invariant instead of re-validating on every collision.
findings.verify_note: Read Projectile.cpp:93-154 (the two copies of the structure list are textually identical), Projectile.h:58 (the virtual), Player.cpp:645-682, PaintTile.cpp:114-138.

findings.title: update_movement() does four unrelated jobs and makes every subclass hand the base its own data back
findings.detail:
Verified. All five leaves open `update()` with the identical two statements (ProjectileSpray.cpp:32-35, Jet:32-35, Ball:32-35, Mist:32-35, Rolling:31-34):
```cpp
const ProjectileDetails& details = this->get_details();
Projectile::update_movement(details.gravity, details.wind_resistance);
```
The base already owns `_details`; making the derived class read two fields out of it and pass them back down is pure ceremony that exists in five places.

The function itself does four unrelated things: gravity integration, clamping against a namespace-scope `projectile_consts::MAX_VELOCITY` that no projectile definition can override (projectile_consts.h:12), wind resistance, and lifetime accounting — despite being named `update_movement`. That naming is part of why the expiry bug stayed hidden.

A real ordering coupling falls out of it, which I verified: `ProjectileSpray::update` calls `update_movement` (which advances `_timer` at line 282) and *then* `calculate_diffusion_size()` (which reads `_timer` at Projectile.cpp:63), so the diffusion is evaluated one frame ahead of the movement it accompanies.

Merged with the candidate noting `update_movement` is declared `virtual` (Projectile.h:67) with no overrides anywhere and all five call sites explicitly qualified — the vtable slot is dead. Same for `virtual bool is_matching_collision_object_type` (Projectile.h:58). The clamp is also written out longhand four times (lines 238-245 and 265-272).
findings.suggestion: Make `Projectile::update()` a non-virtual template method that integrates from its own `_details`, advances lifetime, applies deletion, then calls a protected `virtual void on_updated()` hook for the one thing that varies. Drop `virtual` from `update_movement` and `is_matching_collision_object_type`. Move `MAX_VELOCITY` into `ProjectileDetails` so it is per-definition data. Collapse the four clamp ladders into one `clamp_abs` helper (or `std::clamp` once the language standard is raised).
findings.verify_note: Read Projectile.cpp:232-283 and all five leaf update() bodies. Grepped `update_movement` repo-wide: only the declaration, the definition, and five explicitly-qualified `Projectile::update_movement(...)` calls — no overrides. Confirmed the timer is advanced at line 282 before the diffusion call at ProjectileSpray.cpp:37.

findings.title: calculate_diffusion_size() interpolates toward 1+end_scale but clamps to end_scale, so the sprite and hitbox pop down
findings.detail:
Verified. The two branches disagree at the join:
```cpp
else if (time >= details.end_time) { multiple = details.end_scale; }
else { ... multiple = Vector2F::ONE + Vector2F(details.end_scale.x * ratio, details.end_scale.y * ratio); }
```
As `ratio -> 1` the interpolating branch converges on `ONE + end_scale`; at `time == end_time` the clamp branch returns `end_scale`. The scale therefore jumps down by exactly 1.0 at `end_time`.
- Spray (`DIFFUSION_DETAILS_SPRAY`, end_scale 1.5, projectile_consts.h:40-46): grows 1.0x -> 2.5x over 0.2s..1.0s, then snaps to 1.5x — a 40% drop.
- Mist (end_scale 5.0, projectile_consts.h:87-93): 1.0x -> 6.0x over 0.2s..2.0s, then snaps to 5.0x.

This is not cosmetic only: the result feeds `_rectangle.inflate_to_size(...)` (ProjectileSpray.cpp:37, ProjectileMist.cpp:37) and `_rectangle` *is* the collision shape (`get_shape()` returns `&_rectangle`), so the hitbox discontinuously shrinks mid-flight.

Secondary issues on the same lines, all verified: the three locals at 77-82 are non-const; `Vector2F(end_scale.x * ratio, end_scale.y * ratio)` hand-reimplements `operator*(const Vector2F&, float)` which exists at MattMath.h:503; and `diff_length` is an unguarded divisor, so a details blob with `start_time == end_time` yields inf/NaN sizes.

Merged from 4 duplicate candidate reports.
findings.suggestion: `multiple = Vector2F::ONE + (details.end_scale - Vector2F::ONE) * ratio;` — or `Vector2F::lerp(Vector2F::ONE, details.end_scale, ratio)`, which already exists at MattMath.h:468. Make the locals const, and either assert `end_time > start_time` at construction or divide by `std::max(diff_length, epsilon)`. This is exactly the kind of pure function MattMathTests should cover: assert continuity at both `start_time` and `end_time`.
findings.verify_note: Read Projectile.cpp:61-89, projectile_consts.h:40-46 and :87-93 for the end_scale values, ProjectileSpray.cpp:37 / ProjectileMist.cpp:37 for the application to _rectangle, MattMath.cpp:957-963 for inflate_to_size (writes width/height directly, recentring), and MattMath.h:468/503 to confirm lerp and operator* exist.

findings.title: get_col_rect_size() and get_base_size() both return `size` instead of `col_rect_size`
findings.detail:
Verified. `Vector2F Projectile::get_col_rect_size() const { return this->get_details().size; }` (Projectile.cpp:290-293) returns the wrong field — `ProjectileDetails` has both `size` and `col_rect_size` (projectile_details.h:14-15). The same confusion is in `DiffusingProjectile::get_base_size()` (Projectile.cpp:56-59), which returns `get_details().size` and is the base that `calculate_diffusion_size()` scales — while `_rectangle` was seeded from `col_rect_size` by both the factory (ProjectileBuilder.cpp:30,48,66,98,134) and every leaf constructor (ProjectileSpray.cpp:25 etc.).

So the diffusion path silently mixes the two fields. It is masked today because every `DETAILS_*` sets `size == col_rect_size` (projectile_consts.h lines 21-22, 34-35, 55-56, 68-69, 81-82, 102-103), i.e. the entire render-size/collision-size split the struct promises is unimplemented. The first time anyone gives a projectile a hitbox different from its sprite — the only reason to have two fields — the collision box is wrong.

`get_col_rect_size()` also has zero callers (grep: declaration Projectile.h:50 + this definition only), so nothing would catch it. It returns by value where the neighbouring accessors return `const Vector2F&`.

Merged from 3 duplicate candidate reports.
findings.suggestion: Return `col_rect_size` from both. Then decide whether the field earns its place: if projectiles should have a hitbox distinct from their sprite, they need two rectangles kept in sync in `update()` with `get_shape()` returning the collision one; if not, delete `col_rect_size` from `ProjectileDetails` and all six initialisers rather than leaving a trap.
findings.verify_note: Read Projectile.cpp:56-59 and :290-293, projectile_details.h:14-15, all six DETAILS_* blobs (size == col_rect_size in every one), and the five constructor tails. Grepped get_col_rect_size — declaration and definition only.

findings.title: Four of nine detail fields are never read, and damage has a second, sign-inverted source of truth in player_consts.h
findings.detail:
Verified by repo-wide grep. Dead fields:
- `rotation_origin rotat_origin` (line 11) — set by all six constants (projectile_consts.h:18,31,52,65,78,99, including a meaningful `rotation_origin::CENTER` for the jet) and read by nothing. The only repo hits are the declaration and those six initialisers. Jets are never oriented along their velocity despite the data saying they should be.
- `diffusion_type type` (line 32) — set to `LINEAR_SIZE_AND_COL_RECT` by both diffusion blobs and never consulted. `calculate_diffusion_size` (Projectile.cpp:61-89) never branches on it, so `NO_DIFFUSION` does not disable diffusion and all three enumerators (lines 20-25) behave identically.
- `float delete_timer` (line 12) — dead because of the `get_delete_timer()` bug; see that finding.
- `float player_damage` (line 13) — the only reader would be `Projectile::get_player_damage()` (Projectile.cpp:295-298), which has zero callers.

The damage duplication is the worst of it, and I verified both tables. projectile_consts.h uses **negative** values (`-0.1f` spray :33, `-0.5f` jet :54, `-1000.0f` rolling :67, `-0.05f` mist :80, `-0.1f` ball :101), implying `health += damage`. The live values are the **positive** `player_consts.h:65-69` (`SPRAY_DAMAGE = 0.01f`, `JET_DAMAGE = 0.334f`, `ROLLING_DAMAGE = 0.015f`, `BALL_DAMAGE = 0.201f`, `MIST_DAMAGE = 0.01f`), applied with `-=` in an 11-branch enum ladder (Player.cpp:645-682). Two tables, opposite sign conventions, magnitudes differing by up to 5 orders of magnitude (rolling: -1000.0 vs 0.015), and the one that lives with the projectile — the obvious place to tune — is the dead one.

One reviewer additionally claimed the `-1.0f` sentinel defaults in `DiffusionDetails` (lines 29-31) produce a negative-size rectangle through `inflate_to_size`. The mechanism is real (I checked MattMath.cpp:957-963 — it writes width/height straight through), but no code path constructs a `DiffusingProjectile` with default `DiffusionDetails`, so I am not reporting that as a live defect.

Merged from 4 candidate reports.
findings.suggestion: Damage belongs to the attacker: delete `player_consts.h:65-69`, fix the sign convention in projectile_consts.h, and have `Player::on_projectile_collision` do `this->_health -= projectile->get_player_damage();`. That collapses a 38-line ladder to one line and removes the `throw std::exception("Invalid projectile type.")` at Player.cpp:681. Then either honour `rotat_origin` in the draw path and branch on `diffusion_type`, or delete both fields and the enum. Do not leave aspirational fields that read as working features.
findings.verify_note: Grepped rotat_origin, diffusion_type, player_damage, delete_timer, get_player_damage repo-wide — all dead as described. Read player_consts.h:65-69 and Player.cpp:645-682 for the live table. Read MattMath.cpp:950-963 to check the negative-size claim; mechanism real but unreachable, so excluded.

findings.title: Namespace-scope const/static const aggregates with std::string members in a header: per-TU copies, dynamic init, and a cross-header init-order dependency
findings.detail:
Verified. Every constant in `namespace projectile_consts` is a namespace-scope object defined in a header. Both plain `const` (lines 8-12) and `static const` (lines 14-106) give internal linkage at namespace scope, so every TU including this header gets its own private copy — and the file itself is inconsistent about which spelling it uses, for no reason.

`ProjectileDetails` holds two `std::string` members (projectile_details.h:16-17) and `Vector2F`'s constructors are defined out-of-line in MattMath.cpp, so none of these are literal types: all eight aggregates are **dynamically initialised** globals doing 12 string constructions per TU at static-init time, plus destructors at exit. projectile_consts.h is pulled in transitively through Projectile.h -> the five projectile headers -> ProjectileBuilder.h -> Weapon.h -> Player.h -> Level.h, reaching most of the game.

A real init-order hazard falls out of it, which I verified: `weapon_consts.h` initialises its own namespace-scope statics by *reading* these ones — `{ projectile_consts::DETAILS_SPRAY.size.x / 2.0f, 0.0f }` at weapon_consts.h:40, and the same at :74, :90, :118, :152. One dynamically-initialised object depends on another. It works only because weapon_consts.h includes projectile_consts.h first, so declaration order within each TU saves it — a guarantee that breaks silently the day someone reorders an include.

Five constants are entirely dead, confirmed by grep: `DEFAULT_STARTING_POSITION` (:8), `DEFAULT_SIZE` (:9), `STARTING_DX` (:10), `STARTING_VELOCITY` (:11) and `DETAILS_DEFAULT` (:14-25, whose animation strip is literally named "test"). The four Vector2F names are verbatim duplicates of `player_consts::DEFAULT_STARTING_POSITION/DEFAULT_SIZE/STARTING_DX/STARTING_VELOCITY` (player_consts.h:20-25).

Merged from 3 candidate reports.
findings.suggestion: Delete the five dead constants. Make `ProjectileDetails` a literal type (`std::string_view` or `const char*` for the two names), give `Vector2F` constexpr constructors, and declare every blob `inline constexpr` — one object program-wide, zero dynamic init, zero allocation, no init-order question. That needs `<LanguageStandard>` set (see the C++14 finding). If the standard must stay put, at minimum use `extern const` in the header with a single definition in a .cpp.
findings.verify_note: Read projectile_consts.h in full. Confirmed std::string members in projectile_details.h:16-17. Read weapon_consts.h:36-154 for the cross-header static-init dependency. Grepped DETAILS_DEFAULT / DEFAULT_STARTING_POSITION / STARTING_DX / STARTING_VELOCITY / DEFAULT_SIZE — the only DEFAULT_SIZE use is PlayerBuilder.cpp:38 against player_consts, so all five projectile_consts entries are dead.

findings.title: Public defaulted default-constructors on Projectile, Ball, Jet and Rolling produce objects that crash on first use
findings.detail:
Verified. `Projectile() = default;` (Projectile.h:23), `ProjectileBall() = default;` (ProjectileBall.h:9), `ProjectileJet() = default;` (ProjectileJet.h:9) and `ProjectileRolling() = default;` (ProjectileRolling.h:9). The three leaves are `final` and override every pure virtual, so `ProjectileJet j;` compiles and yields a fully-formed `ICollisionGameObject` that is permanently broken:
- `Projectile::_dt == nullptr` (Projectile.h:79); `Projectile::get_dt()` is `return *this->_dt;` (Projectile.cpp:228-231), called unconditionally at the top of `update_movement` (line 234) — null dereference on the first update.
- `AnimationObject::_dt == nullptr` separately (AnimationObject.h:49), dereferenced at AnimationObject.cpp:88.
- `DrawObject::_resource_manager == nullptr` (DrawObject.h:36).
- `_team == player_team::NONE` (Projectile.h:76), which makes both `is_matching_collision_object_type` (Projectile.cpp:117) and `get_collision_object_type` (line 193) throw on first call.
- `_details` is the all-`-1.0f` sentinel default from projectile_details.h:9-13 — negative gravity, negative drag, empty sheet names.

The hierarchy is inconsistent about it: `ProjectileSpray() = delete;` (ProjectileSpray.h:9) and `ProjectileMist() = delete;` (ProjectileMist.h:9) get it right. Five siblings, two different answers to the same question — which is itself evidence the defaults were unintentional.

Nothing constructs them this way today, so this is a latent API hazard rather than a live crash. Merged from 4 candidate reports; two filed it as memory-safety at high severity, which I have downgraded on that basis.
findings.suggestion: `= delete` all four, matching Spray and Mist, then remove the `= nullptr`/`-1.0f` in-class initialisers that only exist to make those defaults compile. Better: stop threading frame time as `const float*` entirely — take `void update(float dt)` and pass it by value. That makes 'no dt' unrepresentable and removes the null-`_dt` class of bug across every class that currently stores one.
findings.verify_note: Read all five leaf headers and Projectile.h:23. Read Projectile.cpp:228-234 (unconditional `*_dt`), AnimationObject.h:49 / AnimationObject.cpp:88 (second independent _dt), DrawObject.h:36, projectile_details.h:9-17 (sentinels). Confirmed no call site default-constructs a projectile, so severity is latent-API not live-crash.

findings.title: Sprite-sheet lookup uses mutating map::operator[] behind a dead catch, and is called from thread-pool draw tasks
findings.detail:
Verified, and reached on every projectile draw and every projectile animation tick. `ResourceManager::get_sprite_sheet` is a non-const member whose whole body is:
```cpp
try { return this->_sprite_sheets[sprite_sheet_name].get(); }
catch (const std::out_of_range&) { ... throw std::out_of_range(error); }
```
Two real defects:

(a) **The catch is dead code.** `std::map::operator[]` default-inserts on a miss and never throws `out_of_range`. So a wrong sheet name silently returns `nullptr` instead of the intended diagnostic, and the caller dereferences it unchecked — `AnimationObject`'s constructor does `this->_frame_time = this->get_animation_strip()->get_frame_time();` (AnimationObject.cpp:21) with no null check. Access violation, no message. The identical dead-catch pattern is at ResourceManager.cpp:7-19 (get_texture), :27-38 (get_sprite_font), :66-80 and :91-102.

(b) **The API is not const and is called concurrently.** `Level::draw_active_level` submits one task per player partition to a real thread pool (Level.cpp:375-399), and each task's `draw` path reaches `SpriteSheetObject::get_sprite_sheet()` -> this lookup. I am tempering the reviewers' framing here: with all keys present, `operator[]` performs no tree mutation, so this is a latent race rather than live corruption — but the function's signature permits insertion, so the safety of the entire multi-threaded draw path rests on 'the key always happens to be there'.

Merged from 3 candidate reports; two graded this high/critical on the corruption claim, which I do not think holds for present keys.
findings.suggestion: Make the getters `const` and non-mutating: `auto it = _sprite_sheets.find(name); if (it == _sprite_sheets.end()) throw std::runtime_error("SpriteSheet " + name + " not found");`. That kills the dead catch, restores the diagnostic, and makes the draw path provably read-only. Then remove the lookup from the hot path entirely — see the caching finding.
findings.verify_note: Read ResourceManager.cpp:1-102 — all five getters use operator[] or .at() inside a try/catch for out_of_range; the operator[] ones can never throw it. Read AnimationObject.cpp:21 (unchecked deref in a constructor) and Level.cpp:375-399 (thread_pool->add_task per partition, each running draw_player_view_level).

findings.title: Every projectile re-resolves its sprite sheet and animation strip through two string-keyed map lookups, multiple times per frame per viewport
findings.detail:
Verified. `AnimationObject::get_animation_strip()` resolves from scratch on every call:
```cpp
return this->get_sprite_sheet()->get_animation_strip(this->get_element_name());
```
That is two red-black-tree lookups keyed on `std::string`: `ResourceManager::_sprite_sheets` (ResourceManager.cpp:51) then `SpriteSheet::_animation_strips`. Per projectile per frame it happens:
- once in `AnimationObject::update()` (line 87), called from every projectile's `update()`;
- once in `AnimationObject::draw()` for `get_sprite_sheet()` (line 33), plus again inside `get_source_rectangle()` (line 141), which calls `get_animation_strip()` a second time.

And `draw` runs once per player viewport (Level.cpp:375-399 partitions the players), so 4-player split screen is on the order of a dozen string-keyed tree walks per projectile per frame. Every one of these values is immutable after load and identical for all projectiles of a given type.

The strings are also stored twice per projectile: `SpriteSheetObject::_sheet_name`/`_element_name` (SpriteSheetObject.h:25-26) duplicate `_details.sheet_name`/`_details.animation_strip_name` (projectile_details.h:16-17), so spawning one projectile constructs four `std::string`s. The mister does this five times per shot.
findings.suggestion: Resolve `SpriteSheet*` and `const AnimationStrip*` once in the `AnimationObject` constructor and cache them as members; keep the strings only for the rare `set_animation_strip_and_reset` path, which re-resolves. That deletes every per-frame lookup and, as a side effect, removes the multi-threaded `ResourceManager` access described in the related finding. Where string-keyed lookup must remain, `std::unordered_map` beats `std::map` — nothing here needs ordering.
findings.verify_note: Read AnimationObject.cpp in full — get_animation_strip() at :24-28 is called from update() at :87, from get_source_rectangle() at :141, and get_sprite_sheet() from draw() at :33 and :52. Read SpriteSheetObject.h:25-26 and projectile_details.h:16-17 for the duplicated strings. Read Level.cpp:375-399 for the per-viewport draw.

findings.title: get_collision_object_type() re-evaluates a nested switch on every call, inside the O(n^2) collision loop
findings.detail:
Verified. The function computes its answer from `_team` and `_type` through a nested switch every single call, though both members are fixed at construction. Call sites I traced:
- `Projectile::is_matching_collision_object_type` calls `other->get_collision_object_type()` (Projectile.cpp:96), which is invoked from each leaf's `is_colliding` — and `Level::update_level_logic` runs `is_colliding` for **every ordered pair** of collision objects (Level.cpp:277-292, a full N x N loop, not N choose 2) plus every player-vs-object pair twice (Level.cpp:227-243 and 262-273).
- `Projectile::on_collision` calls it again (line 122).
- `Player::on_projectile_collision` (Player.cpp:647) and `PaintTile::on_collision` (PaintTile.cpp:116) call it on every hit.

So it is O(N^2) nested-switch evaluations plus a virtual call each, per frame, to recompute a constant. With the delete-timer bug letting N grow without bound, this sits on the critical path. The `default:` arms also throw from inside that loop.
findings.suggestion: Compute the `collision_object_type` once in the `Projectile` constructor and store it; `get_collision_object_type()` becomes a member read. This is a strictly local fix that can land before the larger collision-filter redesign.
findings.verify_note: Read Projectile.cpp:155-195 and 93-96, Level.cpp:222-293 (confirmed the inner loop is over all collision objects with an `object == object_2` skip, i.e. every ordered pair), Player.cpp:647, PaintTile.cpp:116.

findings.title: MovingObject is a polymorphic base with 30 protected virtual accessors, of which exactly one is ever overridden
findings.detail:
Verified. `MovingObject` (MovingObject.h:6-58) is a pure state mixin — `_velocity`, `_dx`, `_rotation` — yet declares `virtual ~MovingObject() = default;` (line 9) and 30 protected virtual accessors (lines 17-51). I grepped the whole of ArtAttack/ for overrides: there is exactly one, `Player::get_velocity` (Player.h:104). Nothing in the projectile hierarchy overrides any of them.

`Projectile::update_movement` (Projectile.cpp:232-283) reads and writes velocity/dx entirely through those virtuals — roughly 16 non-inlinable dispatches per projectile per frame to update two floats that are members of the same object. The vtable indirection buys nothing and blocks inlining of the hottest per-object function in the game.

Structurally, `Projectile : public MovingObject, public AnimationObject, public ICollisionGameObject` (Projectile.h:19-20) therefore carries a second vptr and two independent polymorphic-base identities, so `delete static_cast<MovingObject*>(p)` and `delete static_cast<ICollisionGameObject*>(p)` are both well-formed but need different pointer adjustments — a real hazard in a codebase where every dependency travels as a raw pointer.

Merged from 2 candidate reports (one design, one performance).
findings.suggestion: Make the `MovingObject` accessors non-virtual and inline, and drop its virtual destructor. Better still, make it a value member (`MovingObject _motion;`) rather than a base, leaving `Projectile` with exactly one polymorphic chain, one vptr and one delete path. Restructure `Player` so it does not need to override `get_velocity`.
findings.verify_note: Read MovingObject.h in full (30 protected virtuals). Grepped for overrides of the velocity/dx accessors across ArtAttack/ — only Player::get_velocity. Counted the accessor calls in Projectile.cpp:232-283.

findings.title: Projectile construction can null-deref or throw from inside a constructor when an asset name is wrong, mid-frame with no handler
findings.detail:
Verified end to end. `Projectile`'s ctor forwards `details.sheet_name` / `details.animation_strip_name` to `AnimationObject` (Projectile.cpp:21-22), whose ctor body immediately does `this->_frame_time = this->get_animation_strip()->get_frame_time();` (AnimationObject.cpp:21). That chains to `get_sprite_sheet()` -> `ResourceManager::get_sprite_sheet`, which returns `nullptr` on a miss (map `operator[]`, ResourceManager.cpp:51) and is dereferenced unchecked; or, if the sheet exists but the strip name does not, `SpriteSheet::get_animation_strip` uses `.at(name)` and throws `std::out_of_range` **from inside a constructor**.

That exception escapes `std::make_unique<ProjectileSpray>(...)` (ProjectileBuilder.cpp:28-40), then `Weapon::shoot`, then `Level::update_level_logic` (Level.cpp:204-210). I grepped every `catch` in ArtAttack/*.cpp: nothing on that path. So a content rename turns the act of firing into a hard crash rather than a load-time error.

The names are hardcoded string literals in projectile_consts.h — all five projectiles share `"sprite_sheet_1"`/`"projectile_3"` (lines 23-24, 36-37, 57-58, 70-71, 83-84, 104-105), and `DETAILS_DEFAULT` points at a strip literally named `"test"`. Nothing validates them, and nothing validates the `-1.0f` sentinel defaults in `ProjectileDetails` either — a partially-filled struct yields negative gravity and a negative delete timer with no complaint.

Merged from 2 candidate reports.
findings.suggestion: Validate sheet/strip names once at load time — better, resolve the detail tables into `const AnimationStrip*` handles during resource load so constructing a gameplay object cannot fail. Add a `validate()` on `ProjectileDetails`/`DiffusionDetails` (gravity finite, `delete_timer > 0`, `size > 0`, `end_time > start_time`, names non-empty) reporting every bad field at once. At minimum make the resource getters fail loudly with the missing key named.
findings.verify_note: Read Projectile.cpp:7-31, AnimationObject.cpp:7-28, ResourceManager.cpp:46-58, and the SpriteSheet .at() lookup. Grepped `catch` across ArtAttack/*.cpp — no handler between make_unique and the game loop.

findings.title: Projectile::update() silently overrides two unrelated base virtuals; only an explicit qualification prevents infinite recursion
findings.detail:
Verified. `Projectile` inherits `void update()` from two independent bases with identical signatures:
- `IGameObject::update()` — public pure virtual (IGameObject.h:10), the per-frame game-object tick;
- `AnimationObject::update()` — protected virtual (AnimationObject.h:21), which only advances the sprite frame index.

The single declaration `void update() override = 0;` at Projectile.h:38, in the public section, therefore overrides **both** and promotes the protected one to public. Legal C++, compiles clean, and fuses two semantically unrelated virtuals into one slot.

The trap is live in the subclasses. `ProjectileSpray::update()` ends with `AnimationObject::update();` (ProjectileSpray.cpp:42). That only works because the call is explicitly qualified — dropping the `AnimationObject::` prefix, a completely natural edit since every other call in the file is unqualified, turns it into a virtual self-call and an immediate stack overflow. The same one-token trap sits at ProjectileJet.cpp:40, ProjectileMist.cpp:42 and ProjectileBall.cpp:40. `ProjectileRolling::update()` omits the call entirely, which is how its animation ended up frozen.
findings.suggestion: Rename the animation tick so the collision is impossible — `AnimationObject::advance_animation(float dt)`. That removes the accidental override and makes the four call sites self-documenting. While there, drive it from the base `Projectile::update()` so no subclass can forget it (which is exactly what ProjectileRolling did).
findings.verify_note: Read IGameObject.h:10 (public pure virtual void update()), AnimationObject.h:21 (protected virtual void update()), Projectile.h:38 (public `void update() override = 0;`), and all five leaf update() bodies to confirm the qualified calls and Rolling's omission.

findings.title: Abstract classes re-declare already-pure virtuals as `= 0`, and the draw re-declaration hides the inherited overload set
findings.detail:
Verified. `Projectile.h:38-46` re-declares five functions that are already pure in `IGameObject`/`ICollisionGameObject` purely to write `override = 0` again, and `DiffusingProjectile` re-declares four of them a third time (Projectile.h:102-108). Four signatures maintained in three places for zero effect — removing them changes nothing, since an unimplemented pure virtual stays pure.

It is not harmless. Declaring *any* `draw` in `Projectile` hides every inherited `draw` by name lookup. Projectile.h:39-40 declares only `draw(SpriteBatch*, const Camera&)`, so `IGameObject::draw(SpriteBatch*)` (IGameObject.h:12) and the five protected `AnimationObject::draw` overloads (AnimationObject.h:34-46) are invisible in `Projectile` and below. That is why every leaf must write the explicit `this->AnimationObject::draw(sprite_batch, this->_rectangle, camera)` (ProjectileSpray.cpp:46, ProjectileMist.cpp:46, ProjectileBall.cpp:45, ProjectileJet.cpp:44) — an unqualified `draw(...)` would not compile against the leaf's own two declarations.
findings.suggestion: Delete the redundant `override = 0` re-declarations in both `Projectile` and `DiffusingProjectile`.
