Where a derived class needs the base overload set, pull it in with `using AnimationObject::draw;` rather than qualifying every call site. Note `Projectile` also has no user-declared destructor while `DiffusingProjectile` has `~DiffusingProjectile() override = default;` (Projectile.h:99) — pick one convention (the virtual destructor is already inherited from `IGameObject`, so neither is required).
findings.verify_note: Read Projectile.h:38-46 and 102-108 against IGameObject.h:10-13 and ICollisionGameObject.h:12-16 — every re-declaration is redundant. Confirmed AnimationObject::draw overloads at AnimationObject.h:34-46 and the four qualified call sites in the leaves.

findings.title: Stateless ProjectileBuilder is heap-allocated per weapon, takes 12 positional parameters, and drags all five concrete headers into most of the game
findings.detail:
Verified. `ProjectileBuilder` has zero data members (ProjectileBuilder.h:11-44). `build_projectiles` is a non-static `const` member that touches no state; `build_mist_projectiles` is already `static` — which the class half-acknowledges by calling `this->build_mist_projectiles(...)` on a static function (ProjectileBuilder.cpp:80). Yet `Weapon` owns one on the heap: `std::unique_ptr<ProjectileBuilder> _proj_builder = nullptr;` (Weapon.h:122), allocated at Weapon.cpp:32 — one allocation per weapon per player per level for an empty object.

The signature is 12 positional parameters written out four times (ProjectileBuilder.h:15-27 and :30-42, ProjectileBuilder.cpp:9-21 and :117-129). Both real call sites — Weapon.cpp:319-327 and Weapon.cpp:565-573 — pass only the first eight, so `rotation`, `origin`, `effects` and `layer_depth` are always defaults, threaded down through every leaf constructor to `DrawObject` for nothing. With 12 same-shaped neighbours an argument-order mistake compiles cleanly, which is precisely how the `SPRAY`-instead-of-`MIST` bug survived. `build_mist_projectiles` additionally takes a `projectile_type type` it never reads (C4100 under /W4).

Header coupling: ProjectileBuilder.h:4-9 includes `Projectile.h` plus all five concrete projectile headers, and Weapon.h:11 includes ProjectileBuilder.h, so every TU reaching Weapon.h — Player.h, Level.h, the game states — parses all five projectile classes, though nothing in the builder's interface names a concrete type (the return is `vector<unique_ptr<ICollisionGameObject>>`).

Correction to the reviewers: two of them claimed `Weapon::get_projectile_builder()` has zero callers. That is **false** — it is called at Weapon.cpp:565. The rest of the finding stands. Merged from 4 candidate reports.
findings.suggestion: Make these free functions in a `projectile_builder` namespace (or plain statics) marked `[[nodiscard]]`, delete `_proj_builder`, the `make_unique` at Weapon.cpp:32 and the `get_projectile_builder()` accessor. Replace the 12 positional parameters with one `ProjectileSpawnParams` struct by const&, and drop the four unused draw parameters from the whole chain. Move the five concrete `#include`s into ProjectileBuilder.cpp and add the missing `<vector>`/`<memory>`. Also: `ProjectileBuilder.cpp:113` has a stray `;` after the switch's closing brace.
findings.verify_note: Read ProjectileBuilder.h and .cpp in full, Weapon.h:115-125, Weapon.cpp:32, :319-327, :488-491, :565-573. Grepped get_projectile_builder — it IS called at Weapon.cpp:565, so I corrected that sub-claim. Confirmed the unused `type` parameter and the stray semicolon at ProjectileBuilder.cpp:113.

findings.title: The project sets no <LanguageStandard>, so it silently builds as C++14 and blocks the idioms this module most needs
findings.detail:
Verified: I grepped ArtAttack.vcxproj for `LanguageStandard` and there is no such element in any of the four `ItemDefinitionGroup` blocks, so MSVC defaults to /std:c++14. `WarningLevel Level4` and `ConformanceMode true` are set (lines 91/96, 113/117, 134/141, 160/166), and `/Zc:__cplusplus` is already in AdditionalOptions.

Concretely, within this module that costs:
- `inline constexpr` variables — the correct fix for the eight per-TU dynamically-initialised globals in projectile_consts.h.
- `std::string_view` for `ProjectileDetails::sheet_name`/`animation_strip_name`, which are compile-time literals in all six blobs yet force heap allocations per TU per blob.
- `std::clamp` for the four hand-rolled clamp ladders at Projectile.cpp:238-245 and 265-272 (`<algorithm>` is already in pch.h).
- `[[nodiscard]]` on `build_projectiles` — today, silently dropping the returned volley of `unique_ptr`s compiles without a peep.
- `std::size` for the spread-angle array that should replace the five copy-pasted mist blocks.

Nothing in this module depends on pre-C++17 behaviour.
findings.suggestion: Add `<LanguageStandard>stdcpp20</LanguageStandard>` (or `stdcpp17` as a first step) to all four ItemDefinitionGroup blocks in ArtAttack.vcxproj, and to MattMathTests.vcxproj. Then land the `inline constexpr` / `string_view` / `std::clamp` / `[[nodiscard]]` changes the other findings call for.
findings.verify_note: Grepped ArtAttack.vcxproj for LanguageStandard/ConformanceMode/WarningLevel/AdditionalOptions — no LanguageStandard element exists; Level4, ConformanceMode true and /Zc:__cplusplus are all present in four configurations.

findings.title: Each projectile carries a by-value copy of its immutable shared detail table plus a duplicate copy of the same two strings, and a second aliasing _dt pointer
findings.detail:
Verified. `ProjectileDetails _details` (Projectile.h:70) and `DiffusionDetails _diffusion_details` (Projectile.h:112) are stored by value per instance, although the values are compile-time constants identical for every projectile of a given class and never mutated (`get_details()` is the only accessor and it is const). `ProjectileDetails` holds two `std::string`s, so that is ~100 bytes plus two string constructions per spawn — and the ctor then forwards those same two strings to `SpriteSheetObject`, which stores them **again** as `_sheet_name`/`_element_name` (SpriteSheetObject.h:25-26). Four `std::string`s per projectile to represent two string literals. The mister does this five times per shot.

Part of the copied payload is provably dead: `_details.player_damage`, `_details.rotat_origin` and `DiffusionDetails::type` are never read (see the dead-fields finding).

Merged with the candidate on the duplicated `_dt`: `Projectile` declares `const float* _dt = nullptr;` (Projectile.h:79) and initialises it at Projectile.cpp:28 from the *same* argument it already forwarded to `AnimationObject` at line 21, which stores its own `const float* _dt` (AnimationObject.h:49). Each projectile therefore carries two independent non-owning aliases to one heap `float` owned by `Game`, both dereferenced without a null check, with the lifetime contract recorded nowhere. The pointer is threaded Game -> GameData -> Level -> Player -> Weapon -> ProjectileBuilder -> Projectile purely so a float can be read once per frame.

With the delete-timer bug letting live projectile counts grow without bound, this per-instance footprint multiplies straight into cache pressure on the O(n^2) collision loop.
findings.suggestion: Once the detail tables have external linkage, replace both by-value members with `const ProjectileDetails* _details` (the constants outlive every projectile by construction) and have `SpriteSheetObject` take its names from that table instead of copying them. Delete both `_dt` members and change the interface to `void update(float dt)` — frame time is a value, not a resource; passing it by value removes the dangling/null exposure entirely and makes projectiles testable without a live `Game`.
findings.verify_note: Read Projectile.h:70-79 and 112, Projectile.cpp:7-31 (both _dt initialisations), AnimationObject.h:49, SpriteSheetObject.h:25-26, projectile_details.h:16-17.

findings.title: Wind resistance compares a velocity against an acceleration times a magic 4.0f, then snaps x-velocity to exactly zero
findings.detail:
Verified verbatim at Projectile.cpp:248-264. Two distinct problems:

1. **Dimensionally meaningless threshold.** `wind_resistance` is an acceleration — it is multiplied by `dt` two lines below to produce a velocity delta. `wind_resistance * 4.0f` is an acceleration times an unexplained `4`, compared against a velocity in units/s. The threshold has no physical meaning and does not scale if the drag constant is retuned. (The `4` looks like an attempt at 'about four frames of decel', which would only be right at exactly 60 fps.)

2. **Hard snap to zero.** Below the threshold, `set_velocity_x(0.0f)` discards horizontal velocity in a single frame instead of decaying it. With `DETAILS_SPRAY.wind_resistance = 20.0f` the cutoff is 80 units/s and `DETAILS_SPRAYER.starting_vel_length` is 1100 (weapon_consts.h:42), so any sprayer shot within a few degrees of vertical has its horizontal component annihilated on the first update — the shot goes perfectly vertical instead of slightly angled. A projectile can also never asymptotically slow down: it either drags linearly or stops dead.

For JET, ROLLING and MIST `wind_resistance == 0` (projectile_consts.h:51, 64, 77), so the threshold is 0 and the whole block degenerates to a no-op.

Also in the same function: `projectile_consts::MAX_VELOCITY = {5000, 5000}` (projectile_consts.h:12) is applied as four hand-written clamp ladders (lines 238-245, 265-272) with no explanation of why one ceiling suits every projectile type when their launch speeds differ by an order of magnitude.

Merged from 2 candidate reports (severity downgraded from the reviewers' medium/low split to a single medium).
findings.verify_note: Read Projectile.cpp:232-283. Read projectile_consts.h:12, 30, 51, 64, 77, 98 and weapon_consts.h:41-42 for the wind_resistance and launch-speed values, confirming both the 80-unit cutoff for spray and the degenerate zero-threshold case for jet/mist/rolling.

findings.title: Unscoped `enum projectile_type` leaks SPRAY/JET/ROLLING/MIST/BALL into the global namespace of most of the codebase
findings.detail:
Verified. `enum projectile_type { SPRAY, JET, ROLLING, MIST, BALL };` at Projectile.h:10-17 is the only unscoped enum in this subsystem — every neighbour is scoped: `collision_object_type` (collision_object_type.h:4), `diffusion_type` (projectile_details.h:20), `player_team`, `rotation_origin`, `shape_type`.

Because Weapon.h:11 includes ProjectileBuilder.h which includes Projectile.h, and Player.h includes Weapon.h, and Level.h includes Player.h, five extremely generic identifiers — `BALL`, `SPRAY`, `MIST`, `JET`, `ROLLING` — become global-namespace ints across essentially the entire game, including the menu code. Exactly the kind of short common noun that will collide with a future engine or third-party header.

They also convert implicitly to `int`, so `build_projectiles(..., 3, ...)` compiles, and the switch in `get_collision_object_type` (Projectile.cpp:161-191) cannot get exhaustiveness diagnostics from /W4. It is also a weapon-taxonomy enum — a game concept — living in what should be a generic engine header.

Merged from 2 candidate reports.
findings.suggestion: At minimum `enum class projectile_type : std::uint8_t` and qualify the ~15 use sites (Projectile.h:74, Projectile.cpp:163-188, the five leaf constructors, ProjectileBuilder.cpp:25-93). With scoped enums and all cases handled, the `default: throw` arms can go and the compiler enforces exhaustiveness. Better: delete the enum along with the class-per-projectile design so identity is an ID in a definition registry.
findings.verify_note: Read Projectile.h:10-17, collision_object_type.h:4, projectile_details.h:20. Confirmed the include chain ProjectileBuilder.h:4 -> Projectile.h and Weapon.h:11 -> ProjectileBuilder.h.

findings.title: Spawn geometry is split across the factory and the constructor, duplicated in all five leaves
findings.suggestion: Add `static RectangleF RectangleF::from_centre(const Vector2F& centre, const Vector2F& size)` and let the factory produce the already-centred rect once. The projectile constructor then stores what it is given and does no geometry — a constructor should not be recomputing placement.
findings.verify_note: Read all five leaf constructors and ProjectileBuilder.cpp:28-200; the offset block is identical in all five and the factory always passes the un-centred position.

findings.title: Rotation is stored twice, in two bases, with no synchronisation — and rotat_origin is never applied
findings.detail:
Verified. The single `rotation` argument seeds two separate members: `MovingObject::_rotation` (MovingObject.h:56, via `MovingObject(velocity, rotation)` at Projectile.cpp:20) and `DrawObject::_draw_rotation` (DrawObject.h:38, via the `AnimationObject` base at Projectile.cpp:21-22). They are read through different accessors (`MovingObject::get_rotation()` vs `DrawObject::get_draw_rotation()`) and written through different mutators, and nothing keeps them equal after construction. `AnimationObject::draw` uses `get_draw_rotation()` (AnimationObject.cpp:39), so any future code that spins a projectile via the `MovingObject` API — the natural choice, since that is where the physics lives — rotates the physics rotation while the sprite stays put.

This is latent today because projectiles are never rotated: both `build_projectiles` call sites (Weapon.cpp:319-327 and :565-573) stop at `resource_manager`, so `rotation` is always the `0.0f` default. Which exposes the related dead-data problem — `DETAILS_JET` sets `rotation_origin::CENTER` (projectile_consts.h:52) and nothing reads `rotat_origin` anywhere, so jets are never oriented along their velocity despite the data saying they should be.

Severity downgraded from the reviewer's medium: the desync is unreachable in the current code.
findings.suggestion: Pick one owner. Since `MovingObject` owns the physics state, keep `MovingObject::_rotation` and have the draw path read it (or push `get_rotation()` into `set_draw_rotation()` each frame in the base `update()`). Then either implement `rotat_origin` — `MovingObject::get_velocity_angle()` already exists at MovingObject.h:31 — or delete the field from `ProjectileDetails` and all six initialisers.
findings.verify_note: Read Projectile.cpp:19-22, MovingObject.h:49-56, DrawObject.h:22/28/38, AnimationObject.cpp:39. Confirmed both Weapon.cpp call sites pass only eight arguments, so rotation is always 0. Grepped rotat_origin — declaration plus six initialisers, no readers.

findings.title: Polymorphic bases with implicit public copy/move while holding borrowed pointers; rule of 0/3/5 applied inconsistently
findings.detail:
Verified. `Projectile` (Projectile.h:19-80) declares no destructor and no copy/move operations while owning a borrowed `const float* _dt` (line 79) and inheriting a borrowed `ResourceManager*` (DrawObject.h:36). The compiler therefore generates public copy construction and copy assignment that silently duplicate those non-owning pointers; and because `Projectile` is a polymorphic base with public assignment, assigning through a base reference compiles and slices, leaving a `ProjectileSpray` carrying another projectile's team, type and timer.

The inconsistency is one level down: `DiffusingProjectile` *does* declare `~DiffusingProjectile() override = default;` (Projectile.h:99). A user-declared destructor suppresses the implicit move constructor and move assignment, so `DiffusingProjectile` — and hence `ProjectileSpray`/`ProjectileMist` — silently degrades every move to a copy, including its `std::string` members. `Projectile` and the five leaves declare no destructor at all. The redundant destructor is also unnecessary: `IGameObject` (IGameObject.h:9) already supplies a virtual one.

Severity kept low: nothing in the codebase copies or assigns a projectile today.
findings.suggestion: On `Projectile` and `DiffusingProjectile`: `= delete` the copy constructor and copy assignment (and the move equivalents, or make them protected if a clone path is ever wanted). Remove the redundant `~DiffusingProjectile() override = default;`. Apply one convention across the hierarchy rather than three.
findings.verify_note: Read Projectile.h in full and IGameObject.h:9. No copy/move declarations on Projectile or any leaf; DiffusingProjectile has the user-declared defaulted destructor at line 99. Confirmed no call site copies or assigns a projectile.

findings.title: Four unreferenced formal parameters (C4100 under /W4), and an invisible object paying for full animation state
findings.suggestion: Omit the parameter names (`void draw(SpriteBatch*, const Camera&) override {}`) so the intent is explicit. Longer term, an invisible collision volume should not be an `AnimationObject` at all — that is the multiple-inheritance hierarchy forcing drawing state onto a non-drawn object; see the HitVolume suggestion on the ProjectileRolling finding.
findings.verify_note: Read ProjectileRolling.cpp:36-47 and ProjectileBuilder.cpp:116-130. Confirmed WarningLevel Level4 in all four vcxproj configurations and no TreatWarningAsError.

findings.title: A single float silently becomes a Vector2F in the diffusion constants, under a comment that names the wrong field
findings.detail:
Verified. `DIFFUSION_DETAILS_SPRAY` (projectile_consts.h:40-46) and `DIFFUSION_DETAILS_MIST` (:87-93) initialise the third member with a bare `1.5f` / `5.0f`, but that member is `MattMath::Vector2F end_scale` (projectile_details.h:31). This compiles only because `Vector2F(float f)` (MattMath.h:409) is a non-explicit converting constructor. It happens to do what was meant, but nothing at the call site says so — and the trailing comment reads `//end_size` while the field is named `end_scale`, so the source of truth for what `1.5f` means is wrong twice. Non-uniform diffusion is silently unexpressible at these call sites even though the field is a vector.

The same implicit conversion means any `float` binds to any `const Vector2F&` parameter across the whole codebase.
findings.suggestion: Write `MattMath::Vector2F(1.5f, 1.5f)` here, as the `DETAILS_*` blobs already do for `size`, and fix the comment to `//end_scale`. Mark `Vector2F(float)` `explicit` in MattMath.h:409 — the compiler will then point at every other site relying on the silent conversion.
findings.verify_note: Read projectile_consts.h:40-46 and :87-93, projectile_details.h:27-33, MattMath.h:406-413 (Vector2F(float f) is declared without `explicit`).

findings.title: Header hygiene: Projectile.h pulls in constants it does not use; ProjectileBuilder.h and projectile_details.h omit includes they do use
findings.detail:
Verified. `Projectile.h:5` includes `projectile_consts.h`, but the header only needs the `ProjectileDetails`/`DiffusionDetails` *types*, which live in projectile_details.h — no `projectile_consts::` name appears in Projectile.h. The consequence is that all eight dynamically-initialised global blobs land in every TU that touches a projectile. The constants are actually used only in Projectile.cpp:238-271 and the five leaf .cpp files, all of which could include projectile_consts.h directly.

Missing includes, also verified: ProjectileBuilder.h uses `std::vector` and `std::unique_ptr` with no `<vector>`/`<memory>` — it gets `<vector>` transitively from MattMath.h:8 and `<memory>` only from each .cpp's pch.h. projectile_details.h uses `std::string` with no `<string>` (MattMath.h does not include it).

Combined with ProjectileBuilder.h:4-9 including all five concrete projectile headers into Weapon.h, touching any leaf projectile header rebuilds most of the project.
findings.suggestion: In Projectile.h, include `projectile_details.h` and move `projectile_consts.h` down into the .cpp files that read constants. In ProjectileBuilder.h, drop the five concrete includes (move them to the .cpp), forward-declare `class ICollisionGameObject;`, and add `<vector>`/`<memory>`. Add `<string>` to projectile_details.h. Headers should include what they use and nothing more.
findings.verify_note: Read Projectile.h in full — no projectile_consts:: name is used. Read ProjectileBuilder.h and projectile_details.h; grepped MattMath.h's includes (SimpleMath.h, shape_type.h, d3d11.h, cmath, vector — no <string>, no <memory>).

findings.title: get_shape() hands out an interior pointer with no documented lifetime contract
findings.detail:
The code is exactly as described: `const Shape* ProjectileSpray::get_shape() const { return &this->_rectangle; }` at ProjectileSpray.cpp:88-91, identical at ProjectileBall.cpp:87-90, ProjectileJet.cpp:86-89, ProjectileMist.cpp:88-91, ProjectileRolling.cpp:80-83. `ICollisionGameObject::get_shape()` (ICollisionGameObject.h:15) documents nothing about validity, and `Level::update_level_logic` both distributes these pointers (Level.cpp:227-293) and destroys projectiles by swap-and-pop in the same function (Level.cpp:296-305).

I am downgrading this from the reviewer's medium. Returning a `const*` to a member is ordinary C++, no current caller retains the pointer past the call, and the swap-and-pop loop runs after all collision testing has finished. The claimed use-after-free is entirely hypothetical — it only materialises if someone later adds a broad-phase cache or a deferred resolution list. Worth a comment, not a rewrite.
findings.suggestion: Document the contract on `ICollisionGameObject::get_shape()` — non-owning, valid until the next mutation of this object, never store. If a retained copy is ever needed, `MattMath::Shape::clone()` already exists.
findings.verify_note: Read all five get_shape() definitions, ICollisionGameObject.h:15, and Level.cpp:259-305 to confirm the deletion pass runs strictly after the collision passes and no pointer is held across it. Severity downgraded because the failure mode is not reachable in current code.

findings.title: Paintable face selection maps edge indices to the wrong faces — 3 of 4 faces paint on the wrong side
findings.detail:
generate_paint_tiles() recovers which faces are paintable by matching `this->get_shape()->get_edges()` against `_paintable_edges` and mapping the positional index: `if (i==0) top_edge=true; else if (i==1) right_edge=true; else if (i==2) bottom_edge=true; else if (i==3) left_edge=true;`.

MattMath.cpp:808-818 returns `{ get_top_edge(), get_bottom_edge(), get_left_edge(), get_right_edge() }` — top, bottom, left, right. So the actual mapping is: JSON top→top (correct), JSON bottom→right face, JSON left→bottom face, JSON right→left face.

I verified this against the shipped level data (all three files parsed). Live consequences:
- king_of_the_hill.json `castle_ceiling` (1650x25, bottom only): should get ~412 tiles on its underside, actually gets ~6 on its right end. The castle ceiling is unpaintable.
- `castle_wall_left` (25x750, right only) and `castle_wall_right` (25x750, left only): tiles land on the opposite face, i.e. the outside of the castle instead of the inside.
- `castle_floor_left` (top+right) → generates top+left; `castle_floor_right` (left+top) → generates bottom+top.
- close_quarters.json `lower_paint` (3000x50, top+bottom) → generates top+right, losing ~738 tiles.
- turbulence.json `central_divider_ledge_paint` (left+top+right) → generates bottom+top+left.
All-four-face structures (mountain_platform_left/right, upper_top_paint, etc.) are unaffected because the set is symmetric — which is why this has gone unnoticed.

The root cause is the round trip itself: LevelObjectBuilder.cpp:107-130 encodes four JSON booleans as `Segment`s, and this code decodes them back into booleans via an undocumented positional ordering. Candidates 1, 43, 57 and 76 all report this; merged here.
findings.suggestion: Delete the encode/decode entirely. Pass the four booleans (or a `paintable_faces` bitmask) straight from LevelObjectBuilder into StructurePaintable — the commented-out `PaintableFaces` struct at StructurePaintable.h:17-23 and LevelObjectBuilder.cpp:101-105 already did exactly this. If edge matching must stay, compare against the named accessors (`rect.get_top_edge()` etc.) rather than positional indices, and add a unit test pinning `RectangleF::get_edges()` ordering.
findings.verify_note: Read StructurePaintable.cpp:188-213 and MattMath.cpp:808-818 — the orderings genuinely differ. Parsed all three levels/*.json and enumerated every StructurePaintable's paintable_faces to confirm the mismatch is live in shipped data, not hypothetical.

findings.title: Level JSON parsed through a 1-byte heap buffer declared as 8 bytes — heap overflow on every level load
findings.detail:
```cpp
FILE* fp = fopen(json_path, "rb");                            // unchecked
std::unique_ptr<char> readBuffer = std::make_unique<char>();  // ONE char
FileReadStream is(fp, readBuffer.get(), sizeof(readBuffer));  // sizeof(unique_ptr) == 8
Document d;
d.ParseStream(is);                                            // return value discarded
fclose(fp);
readBuffer.release();                                          // leaks the allocation
```
Four independent defects. (1) `make_unique<char>()` allocates one byte; `sizeof(readBuffer)` is the size of the `unique_ptr` object, 8 on x64. I read the vendored rapidjson (external/rapidjson/include/rapidjson/filereadstream.h:66-81): `Read()` does `readCount_ = std::fread(buffer_, 1, bufferSize_, fp_)` and, on the final short read, `buffer_[readCount_] = '\0'` — so it writes up to 8 bytes, plus a terminator at offset up to 8, into a 1-byte allocation. king_of_the_hill.json is 21,955 bytes, so the refill loop runs ~2,700 times per load, each time overwriting the allocator's block header. (2) `readBuffer.release()` relinquishes ownership without deleting. (3) `fopen` is unchecked; `RAPIDJSON_ASSERT(fp_ != 0)` compiles out under NDEBUG and `fclose(nullptr)` is UB. (4) `d.HasParseError()` is never queried, so a malformed file yields a null Document and every later `_json_doc["level_name"]` (line 17) etc. is UB in Release.

Candidates 3, 19, 58 and 72 all report this; merged. The same `sizeof(unique_ptr)` idiom also exists at SpriteSheet.cpp:74-81 (I confirmed `read_buffer.release()` there), and reviewers cite Save.cpp and SoundBank.cpp — treat it as one shared helper to fix.
findings.suggestion: Write one `rapidjson::Document parse_json_file(const std::string& path)` helper that checks `fopen`, uses a real `std::vector<char> buffer(65536)`, closes the FILE* with an RAII guard, and throws a message naming the path and `GetParseError()`/`GetErrorOffset()` on failure. Replace all four copy-pasted loaders with it.
findings.verify_note: Read LevelLoadedInfo.cpp:96-110 and the vendored external/rapidjson/include/rapidjson/filereadstream.h:44-81 to confirm bufferSize_ is used verbatim as the fread length and that buffer_[readCount_] is written. Confirmed file size 21955 bytes for king_of_the_hill.json.

findings.title: Level is a god class: object storage, simulation, collision, camera, HUD, audio, match rules and the D3D11 render backend
findings.detail:
`Level` carries ~30 data members and mixes at least eight unrelated responsibilities: object ownership (Level.h:95-105), simulation tick (update_level_logic, Level.cpp:180-322), collision iteration and response (Level.cpp:221-293), deletion/out-of-bounds culling (Level.cpp:296-321), camera control (`_camera_tools`, `_zoom_out_camera`), HUD (`_interface_gameplay`, `_debug_text`, `_countdown_text`), audio policy (`_sound_bank`, `_music_name`, `stop_music`, `stop_player_sounds`), match rules and scoring (`_timer`, `_state`, `get_level_end_info`), and the multithreaded D3D11 render backend (`_thread_pool`, `_partitioner`, `_sampler_state`, `FinishCommandList` at Level.cpp:587).

Nothing here can be reused or tested independently, and none of it can run without a live D3D11 device. Given the stated goal of a reusable engine with the game as a proof, this is the single largest structural obstacle in the module: everything reusable is welded to everything game-specific.
findings.suggestion: Split into: `Scene`/`World` (owns and updates objects), `CollisionSystem` (unique pairs, dispatch), `SceneRenderer` (the only piece that knows SpriteBatch/deferred contexts), `GameMode`/`RuleSet` (timer, countdown, win condition, scoring — game code, not engine), and `Hud`. `Level` then becomes a thin composition root the game supplies.
findings.verify_note: Read Level.h in full and Level.cpp 1-745; the responsibility list is directly observable in the member declarations and method bodies cited.

findings.title: Level's public draw API is three raw pointers to vectors of D3D11 objects
findings.detail:
`void draw(std::vector<ID3D11DeviceContext*>*, std::vector<ID3D11CommandList*>*, std::vector<DirectX::SpriteBatch*>*) const;` — a simulation type whose public signature exposes the deferred-context/command-list scheme. The same triple is repeated on `draw_active_level` (Level.h:156-158), `draw_zoom_out_level` (160-162), `draw_player_view_level` (168-171) and `draw_zoom_out_level_component` (173-175).

The implementation does the graphics work itself: `deferred_contexts->at(i)->GetType() != D3D11_DEVICE_CONTEXT_DEFERRED` with a throw (Level.cpp:498-501), `sprite_batches->at(i)->Begin(SpriteSortMode_Deferred, nullptr, _sampler_state)` (Level.cpp:513), `FinishCommandList(TRUE, &command_lists->at(i))` (Level.cpp:587). The caller then has to `ExecuteCommandList` and `Release` them by hand (GameStates.cpp:321-330).

Additional problems in the one signature: `command_lists` is a pure out-parameter mixed in among inputs with nothing in the type saying so; the three vectors must be index-aligned and at least `_player_objects->size()` long, which is neither stated nor checked; and the meaning of the index differs between the two paths (`draw_player_view_level` uses partition indices, `draw_zoom_out_level_component` hard-codes 0 at Level.cpp:614/620/624/646). Candidates 37 and 67 merged.
findings.suggestion: Define an engine-level `IRenderer`/`RenderContext` and make `Level::draw(IRenderer&)` the whole API. Command-list recording, deferred contexts, sampler state and the parallel-recording strategy become the renderer's private business. Until then, at minimum pass one `RenderTargets` struct by const reference with a single invariant check.
findings.verify_note: Read Level.h:83-85, 156-175 and the corresponding implementations in Level.cpp:354-651, plus the caller at GameStates.cpp:311-330.

findings.title: Splatoon paint scoring and a fixed two-team model are baked into an engine-level interface
findings.suggestion: Engine side: a generic score-contribution hook, or better a game-owned `ScoringSystem` the level notifies of events. Teams become a `TeamId` handle with scores in a container sized by the game mode. `PaintTotal`, `PaintTile`, `StructurePaintable` and the `PROJECTILE_*_TEAM_*` enum values all move to a game layer built on top of the engine.
findings.verify_note: Read IPaintableGameObject.h in full, collision_object_type.h:4-29, LevelEndInfo.h:7-27 and Level.cpp:706-735.

findings.title: Multithreaded draw calls non-const draw() on shared objects — concurrent writes to the same PaintTile
findings.suggestion: Set the tile colour once in `PaintTile::on_collision`, pass the splash rectangle as a local rather than storing it, then make `IGameObject::draw` const-qualified. Change `SpriteSheet::draw` to `.at(name)` on a const SpriteSheet, or better resolve sheet/frame handles at load time so the render loop touches no string-keyed maps.
findings.verify_note: Read Level.cpp:379-399 and 496-540, PaintTile.cpp:34-75 and 172-175, TextureObject.h:19-32, SpriteSheet.cpp:92-132, Partitioner.cpp:4-22 (confirms 2 players → 2 partitions → 2 concurrent tasks).

findings.title: Zoom-out draw permanently forces ONE_PLAYER layout on the shared ViewportManager; Restart then renders every player fullscreen
findings.detail:
`draw_zoom_out_level_component` begins with:
```cpp
this->_viewport_manager->set_layout(screen_layout::ONE_PLAYER);
this->_viewport_manager->apply_player_viewport(0);
```
`_layout` is a member of the shared `ViewportManager` (ViewportManager.cpp:79-82), it is never restored, and the only place it is set from the match settings is `GameLevel::init` (GameStates.cpp:122-123). Neither restart path re-runs `init` — both just rebuild the level: `pause_menu_action::RESTART` (GameStates.cpp:200-205) and `end_menu_action::RESTART` (GameStates.cpp:276-283).

Every match reaches ZOOM_OUT before the results/end menu appears (`level_state::FINISHED` is only reachable via ZOOM_OUT → OVERVIEW, Level.cpp:133-167), so by the time the end-menu Restart is available the layout is *always* ONE_PLAYER. The rebuilt level then takes each player's viewport from `get_player_viewport(...)` (which returns fullscreen for every player_num under ONE_PLAYER, ViewportManager.cpp:160-165) and `build_viewport_dividers` gets an empty list (ViewportManager.cpp:129-132). Every player renders fullscreen on top of everyone else with no dividers.

This is also mutation of shared presentation state from inside a `const` method running on a thread-pool worker.
findings.suggestion: Do not mutate ViewportManager here — render the overview through the deferred-context overload with an explicitly-constructed fullscreen viewport. Independently, make GameLevel re-apply `set_layout(_settings.get_screen_layout())` on both restart paths, or move level construction into one helper that always does it.
findings.verify_note: Read Level.cpp:609-651, ViewportManager.cpp:63-70/79-88/129-152/154-165, GameStates.cpp:105-127/196-215/276-283, and Level.cpp:126-175 to confirm FINISHED is only reachable through ZOOM_OUT.

findings.title: Zoom-out worker task drives the immediate D3D context and the main thread's SpriteBatch
findings.suggestion: Use the three-argument overload here too, and delete the single-argument `apply_player_viewport(int)` plus ViewportManager's `_sprite_batch` member so the broken call cannot be written again.
findings.verify_note: Read ViewportManager.cpp:45-70 (three overloads, only the 1-arg one uses the immediate context), Level.cpp:595-651, and Game.cpp:124-151 confirming deferred contexts get RSSetViewports every frame in clear().

findings.title: Exceptions thrown inside thread-pool draw tasks escape a Win32 callback and terminate the process
findings.detail:
`draw_player_view_level` throws from inside a worker task at Level.cpp:500 (`throw std::exception("Deferred context not created")`) and :590 (`FinishCommandList` failed); `draw_zoom_out_level_component` does the same at :616 and :649. The `.at()` calls on all three vectors can also throw `std::out_of_range`.

The task body is invoked from `ThreadPool::work_callback` (ThreadPool.cpp:60-65):
```cpp
std::function<void()>* task = static_cast<std::function<void()>*>(parameter);
(*task)();      // no try/catch
delete task;    // skipped if it throws
```
This is a `void CALLBACK` Win32 thread-pool entry point. An exception escaping it calls `std::terminate` — no message, no log. `wait_for_tasks_to_complete()` (ThreadPool.cpp:50-58) never observes it and the task object leaks.

There is no top-level handler either: I grepped Main.cpp and it contains no `try` or `catch` at all, so the same is true of the `throw std::exception("Player out of bounds")` at Level.cpp:312. `FinishCommandList` failing on device-removal/OOM is a realistic path. Candidates 7, 23 and 80 merged.
findings.suggestion: Wrap the body in `work_callback` in `try { (*task)(); } catch (...) { store std::exception_ptr on the work item; }` and rethrow from `wait_for_tasks_to_complete()` on the calling thread. Put a top-level try/catch around the message loop in Main.cpp. In the draw path, prefer returning HRESULT/bool; the `GetType()` check is an invariant assertion, not a runtime error.
findings.verify_note: Read ThreadPool.cpp in full (no handler in work_callback), Level.cpp:491-651, and grepped Main.cpp for try/catch — zero matches.

findings.title: player_inputs is indexed by player-object position but the vector only contains connected pads
findings.suggestion: Have PlayerInput return a fixed 4-element array indexed by pad slot with a `connected` flag, and look it up as `player_inputs[object->get_player_num()]` with a neutral-input fallback when that pad is absent. Switch Level.cpp:198 to `get_player_num()` so update and draw agree.
findings.verify_note: Read Level.cpp:188-213 and PlayerInput.cpp:119-138 — the vector is genuinely compacted by `connected`, and the index is genuinely the loop position with no bounds check.

findings.title: "Still on the ground" is inferred from any structure overlap, so wall and jump-through contact suppresses on_no_collision()
findings.suggestion: Have `Player` track a per-frame `_grounded_this_frame` flag that only `on_bottom_collision` and the ramp handlers set, and call `on_no_collision()` at the end of the player's collision pass when it is still false. `Level` should not be classifying collision types at all.
findings.verify_note: Read Level.cpp:221-249, Player.cpp:1252-1263 (only IN_AIR transition), Player.cpp:553-575 (left/right leave move_state alone), Player.cpp:360-382 (early-return path), collision_object_type.h:75-82 (is_structure includes JUMP_THROUGH).

findings.title: An object leaving the play area throws an unhandled exception instead of being despawned
findings.suggestion: Make out-of-bounds a policy: mark projectiles for deletion, respawn players at their team spawn. Fold the test into the existing deletion sweep so the list is walked once. Reserve exceptions for programmer errors and add a top-level handler regardless.
findings.verify_note: Read Level.cpp:296-321 and 689-694; grepped Main.cpp for try/catch (zero hits) and confirmed GameStates.cpp:128-301 has no handler.

findings.title: Every level JSON field is read with unchecked rapidjson accessors — missing or mistyped fields are UB in Release
findings.detail:
Every read goes straight through rapidjson's precondition-asserting accessors: `json["type"].GetString()` (:19), `json["rectangle"]["x"].GetFloat()` (:40-43), `json["paintable_faces"]["left"].GetBool()` (:110), `json["triangle"]["x1"].GetFloat()` (:161-167), `json["sheet_name"].GetString()` (:59). `operator[](const char*)` and the typed getters enforce their preconditions with `RAPIDJSON_ASSERT`, which is `assert` and compiles out under NDEBUG. A level file missing `sheet_name`, or with `"width": "100"` as a string, is undefined behaviour in Release.

Only two things are checked at all, both via `HasMember`: `rectangle`/`rectangle_tlbr` (:38-56, :81-99) and `paintable_faces` (:108-130).

The one field looked up by name degrades silently instead: `colour_consts::colour_from_name` falls back to WHITE on an unknown name, so a typo'd colour produces a white object with no diagnostic.

There is no value validation either: nothing rejects negative or zero width/height, which is the precondition the paint-tile divide-by-zero (separate finding) depends on. Combined with the unchecked parse-error in `LevelLoadedInfo::load_from_json`, a bad level file has no failure mode that produces a usable message.
findings.suggestion: Add `require_float(json, "x")` / `require_string(json, "type")` / `require_object(json, "rectangle")` helpers that check `HasMember` **and** the type and throw a message naming the file, object index and field. Validate ranges (width/height > 0, spawns inside out_of_bounds) at build time. Make `colour_from_name` return a failure the caller must handle.
findings.verify_note: Read LevelObjectBuilder.cpp in full; confirmed only two HasMember guards exist and every other access is a bare typed getter.

findings.title: Paint tiles are never viewport-culled — thousands of sprites submitted per viewport per frame
findings.suggestion: Cull per tile — pass `camera_view` down and `if (!paint_tile.is_visible_in_viewport(camera_view)) continue;`. Better, exploit the regular grid: compute the visible index range with two divisions and draw only that slice. Resolve the sheet pointer and source RECT once per structure rather than once per tile per frame.
findings.verify_note: Read StructurePaintable.cpp:45-62 and 104-299, Level.cpp:525-531, Structure.cpp:39-42, PaintTile.cpp:149-152, SpriteSheet.cpp:92-132. Confirmed boundary_floor's dimensions and top-only face from levels/king_of_the_hill.json.

findings.title: StructurePaintable stores a reference member bound to a caller's local vector — dangles for the object's whole life
findings.detail:
`const std::vector<MattMath::Segment>& _paintable_edges;` (StructurePaintable.h:56), bound in the member-init list at StructurePaintable.cpp:30 to the constructor parameter.

The caller passes a function-local: `std::vector<Segment> paintable_edges;` at LevelObjectBuilder.cpp:107, filled at :110-125, passed at :140 to `std::make_unique<StructurePaintable>(...)`. `build_collision_object` then returns and the vector dies — but the StructurePaintable lives for the whole level holding a reference to that dead stack object.

The UB is latent rather than firing today because the only reads (StructurePaintable.cpp:191, :193) happen inside `generate_paint_tiles()`, called from the constructor body at :33 while the argument is still alive. It is one method away from being live.

Two side effects prove the member is wrong: `StructurePaintable() = default;` (StructurePaintable.h:28) is implicitly **deleted** because a reference member cannot be default-initialised — the declaration says the opposite of what it means — and copy/move assignment are deleted too.
findings.suggestion: The data is only consumed during construction, so keep no member at all: pass it as an argument to `generate_paint_tiles(const std::vector<Segment>&)`. Better still, delete the vector round-trip entirely (see the face-mapping finding) and pass a face bitmask by value. Then delete the meaningless `= default` constructor.
findings.verify_note: Read StructurePaintable.h:25-62, StructurePaintable.cpp:9-35 and 188-213, LevelObjectBuilder.cpp:107-143 — the local's scope genuinely ends at the return.

findings.title: Level caches raw SoundBank* and ResourceManager* that device-loss destroys and replaces
findings.detail:
`SoundBank* _sound_bank` (Level.h:107, assigned Level.cpp:59) and `ResourceManager* _resource_manager` (Level.h:119). `StructurePaintable.h:59` caches a `SoundBank*` too (assigned StructurePaintable.cpp:34).

The pointees are owned by `ResourceManager::_sound_banks`. `Game::OnDeviceLost()` (Game.cpp:269-280) calls `_resource_manager->reset_all_sounds()`, which at ResourceManager.cpp:119-126 does `sound_bank.second.reset()` on every entry — the SoundBanks are **destroyed**. `Game::OnDeviceRestored()` (Game.cpp:282-287) then calls `create_device_dependent_resources()`, which at Game.cpp:239 does `this->_resource_manager = std::make_unique<ResourceManager>();` — the entire ResourceManager is replaced with a new object. Nothing notifies the live `Level`, and the state machine is not rebuilt.

So after any device-lost event (Alt-Tab, driver reset, TDR), the surviving `Level` holds dangling `_sound_bank` **and** `_resource_manager`. The next frame dereferences them: Level.cpp:63, :73-74, :134, :136, :147, :171, and `StructurePaintable::on_collision` at :97 on every paint hit.
findings.suggestion: Either don't cache — look the bank up by name at each use through a null-checked accessor — or, for a reusable engine, give resources generation-counted handles so a stale handle is detectable rather than dangling. Whatever you pick, document every raw pointer member with its owner and its validity window.
findings.verify_note: Read Game.cpp:218-243 (create_device_dependent_resources replaces the ResourceManager outright), Game.cpp:269-287, ResourceManager.cpp:119-126, Level.cpp:54-63, StructurePaintable.cpp:34/97. The candidate understated it — the ResourceManager itself is replaced, not just the sound banks.

findings.title: 23-parameter constructor, five of whose members are written and never read
findings.detail:
`Level::Level` takes 23 positional parameters (Level.h:58-80; several reviewers said 24 — I counted, it is 23). The call site (LevelBuilder.cpp:59-82) cannot be read without counting commas, and there are four adjacent `const MattMath::RectangleF&` parameters (out_of_bounds, camera_bounds, zoom_out_start_bounds, zoom_out_finish_bounds) plus two adjacent `const std::vector<Vector2F>&` spawn parameters — transposable at a call site with no diagnostic.

I grepped every member across the whole first-party tree. Five are written and never read:
- `_stage` (Level.h:129, written Level.cpp:42) — the only other hits are MenuLevelSettings' unrelated member.
- `_team_a_spawns` / `_team_b_spawns` (Level.h:136-137, written Level.cpp:47-48) — two whole `std::vector<Vector2F>` copies per level build, per Restart. Spawns are actually consumed by PlayerBuilder (LevelBuilder.cpp:50-53).
- `_level_name` (Level.h:116, written Level.cpp:37) — a `std::string` copy for nothing.
- `_player_inputs` (Level.h:143) — never written *or* read anywhere; `update()` takes inputs by reference and forwards them.

Related dead surface in the same class: `void set_state(level_state)` (Level.h:88, Level.cpp:701-704) is public with zero callers and lets any client jam the FSM into an arbitrary state, bypassing every transition side-effect in `update()`; `void draw_end_screen()` (Level.h:152, Level.cpp:696-699) is an empty `// TODO` with zero callers.
findings.suggestion: Delete the five dead members, their four constructor parameters, `set_state` and `draw_end_screen` (or wire the spawn vectors into a respawn path — see the out-of-bounds finding). Then collapse the remainder into a `LevelDescription` value struct plus an engine-services struct, so designated-initialiser construction names every field at the one call site.
findings.verify_note: Counted the parameter list in Level.h:58-80 (23). Ran a repo-wide grep for each of _stage, _level_name, _team_a_spawns, _team_b_spawns, _player_inputs, set_state, draw_end_screen — every hit is the declaration or the ctor initialiser, confirming they are dead.

findings.title: Split-screen is hardwired: render-slot index == player index, and there is no View concept
findings.detail:
`draw_player_view_level(int start, int end, ...)` uses one loop variable `i` as (a) the index into `_player_objects`, (b) the index into `deferred_contexts`, (c) the index into `sprite_batches`, and (d) the index into `command_lists` (Level.cpp:496-591). The camera comes from `_player_objects->at(i)->get_camera()`, the viewport from that player's `get_player_num()`, and the HUD is drawn from the same player's health/ammo/team (Level.cpp:560-569). `draw_active_level` partitions `_player_objects->size()` across threads (Level.cpp:382-383).

The engine therefore cannot render a spectator view, a minimap, a render-to-texture pass, a level with zero players, or any view not owned by a `Player`. "A thing we render the scene from" does not exist as a concept — `Player` *is* the camera, the viewport and the HUD owner. The zoom-out path had to be written as a completely separate function (Level.cpp:609-651) for exactly this reason, and it is where two other bugs in this review live.
findings.suggestion: Introduce a first-class `View` (camera + viewport + optional HUD overlay) and have the renderer iterate `std::vector<View>`. Player contributes a View; the zoom-out sequence contributes a View; a minimap contributes a View. Partition views, not players.
findings.verify_note: Read Level.cpp:375-400 and 491-651; the single index doing quadruple duty and the duplicated zoom-out path are directly observable.

findings.title: O(n²) collision inlined into Level with no broad phase, and object-object pairs visited in both orderings
findings.detail:
Three hand-written nested loops with no abstraction between them and the object list:
- loop 1 (:222-249): for each player, for each collision object
- loop 2 (:259-273): for each collision object, for each player
- loop 3 (:277-292): for each object, for each *other* object — the pair (a,b) is visited as (a,b) and again as (b,a), so `is_colliding` is evaluated twice per pair every frame

`_collision_objects` holds all 24-40 level structures plus every live projectile, so a busy frame is tens of thousands of virtual `is_colliding` calls, each doing two virtual `get_bounding_box()` calls that return `RectangleF` **by value** and, on an AABB hit, a `Shape::intersects` dynamic_cast chain (MattMath.cpp:119-136). The `ThreadPool` and `Partitioner` that exist in this very class are used only for drawing (Level.cpp:379-399), never here.

Storage compounds it: `unique_ptr<vector<unique_ptr<T>>>` means every candidate test chases two levels of indirection.

Note: I explicitly checked and **rejected** the related claim that response callbacks fire 2-4 times per pair (see the separate rejected finding) — that does not happen. The redundant *detection* work is real; the double *response* is not.
findings.suggestion: Collapse to one pass over unique pairs (`for i, for j > i`) and dispatch once. Add a broad phase — a uniform grid or sweep-and-prune over AABBs cached in a flat `std::vector<RectangleF>` parallel to the object list, rebuilt once per frame (structures are static and only need inserting once). Add a collision layer/mask so structure-vs-structure pairs are never generated.
findings.verify_note: Read Level.cpp:221-293 in full; loop 3 genuinely has no `j > i` guard, only an identity check at :283. Traced the actual dispatch behaviour through Player::is_matching_collision_object_type (Player.cpp:145-147), Structure::is_colliding (Structure.cpp:43-46) and Projectile::is_matching_collision_object_type (Projectile.cpp:93-118).

findings.title: Every projectile hit linear-scans all of a structure's paint tiles, and the splash sound fires once per projectile
findings.suggestion: Store tiles as an explicit grid (origin, tile size, counts, `std::vector<player_team>`) and convert the projectile AABB to an index range — a handful of integer ops with no virtual calls. Add a per-structure per-frame flag or short cooldown before `play_wave`.
findings.verify_note: Read StructurePaintable.cpp:64-102 and 219-296, PaintTile.cpp:84-109. Confirmed boundary_floor is 6000x1000 with top-only faces → 6000/4 = 1500 tiles.

findings.title: Adjacent paintable faces overlap at every corner, so the same physical area is scored twice
findings.detail:
The top/bottom loops emit tiles spanning the structure's full width (`get_left() + paint_tile_width * i`, height THICKNESS=12) and the left/right loops emit tiles spanning the full height (`get_top() + paint_tile_height * i`, width THICKNESS). Nothing excludes the corners, so for any structure with two adjacent faces enabled the 12x12 corner square is covered by tiles from both faces.

`get_paint_total` (StructurePaintable.cpp:300-319) sums `paint_tile.get_area()` over all tiles, so that area is counted twice. Worse, the overlapping tiles are independent: team A can own the top corner tile while team B owns the left corner tile at the same screen position, and both are added to their team's score. Both are also drawn, one over the other.

I verified the arithmetic against turbulence.json `upper_top_paint` (1200x50, all four faces): top and bottom contribute 300 tiles each of 4x12 = 14,400 units each; left and right contribute 12 tiles each of 12x4.167 = 600 each; total 30,000. The four double-counted corners are 4 × 144 = 576, about 1.9% of that structure's scoreable area. Every all-four-face structure in every level has this.
findings.suggestion: Inset the horizontal runs by THICKNESS on each end when the corresponding vertical face is enabled (adjusting the tile count), or generate the border ring as a single grid and de-duplicate, so each unit of surface belongs to exactly one tile.
findings.verify_note: Read StructurePaintable.cpp:217-319 and confirmed no corner exclusion. Recomputed the tile geometry for turbulence.json upper_top_paint from the actual JSON dimensions; the candidate's 576/30000 figure checks out.

findings.title: Tile size divides by a truncated tile count that can legitimately be zero, and fabs is applied to the count but not the divisor
findings.suggestion: Normalise the rectangle first, then `if (num_x < 1 || num_y < 1) throw` with a message naming the offending object, or clamp to 1 if that is the intended behaviour. Validate width/height > 0 at parse time in LevelObjectBuilder.
findings.verify_note: Read StructurePaintable.cpp:104-116, PaintTile.h:10-21, LevelObjectBuilder.cpp:80-99, and grepped ArtAttack.vcxproj confirming FloatingPointModel=Fast in all four configs and no TreatWarningAsError.

findings.title: Paintable faces are matched by exact float equality on Segment endpoints under /fp:fast
findings.suggestion: Delete `_paintable_edges` and carry the booleans through from JSON. If edge matching must stay, compare with an epsilon and assert that at least one edge matched when `_paintable_edges` is non-empty.
findings.verify_note: Read MattMath.cpp:1574-1577 and 4045-4049 (exact float ==), StructurePaintable.cpp:188-213, LevelObjectBuilder.cpp:107-142 confirming the same RectangleF object feeds both the edges and the shape.

findings.title: try/catch around a pointer dynamic_cast is dead code; a failed cast null-derefs instead
findings.suggestion: `if (auto* paintable = dynamic_cast<IPaintableGameObject*>(object.get())) { ... }` — no enum check, no try/catch, no null deref, and a future paintable type is picked up automatically. Better still, have the builder collect a `std::vector<IPaintableGameObject*>` at construction so the query is a straight loop with no RTTI.
findings.verify_note: Read Level.cpp:706-735, Structure.cpp:51-54, LevelObjectBuilder.cpp:67-78. Confirmed no code path currently constructs a plain Structure with the STRUCTURE_PAINTABLE tag, which is why this is latent.

findings.title: winning_ratio/losing_percentage compute winner-over-loser, divide by zero, and can return negative percentages
findings.suggestion: Express everything as a share of the total with one guard: `const float t = team_a_area + team_b_area; return t > 0.0f ? winning_score()/t : 0.5f;`. Delete the four unreferenced accessors. Replace the three unreachable throws with a `switch` on `player_team` so MSVC proves exhaustiveness.
findings.verify_note: Read LevelEndInfo.cpp in full and LevelEndInfo.h:7-27. Ran a repo-wide grep for winning_ratio/losing_ratio/winning_percentage/losing_percentage — the only hits are the definitions, declarations and their mutual calls, confirming zero external callers.

findings.title: _countdown_text is created lazily in update() but dereferenced unconditionally in draw()
findings.suggestion: Build `_countdown_text` in the constructor — resolution, resource manager and the constants are all available there — and delete the `_start_timer >= START_TIMER` sentinel. Move the one-shot music/sound/camera work into an explicit `init()`/`on_enter()` called once by GameLevel::init, then delete FIRST_UPDATE/SECOND_UPDATE and the public `set_state`.
findings.verify_note: Read Level.cpp:65-125, 580-585, 737-745; Level.h:88/111; GameStates.cpp:128-190 and 303-330; GameStates.h:36-44. Verified the guard is exactly the two dummy states.

findings.title: Thread-pool lambda copies the whole partition vector per task, every frame
findings.suggestion: Capture the two ints for this task only, not the vector. Cache the partition as a member and recompute it only when the player count changes. Hoist the command-list vector into a member of GameLevel reused across frames. Replace `std::pair<int,int>` with a named `struct PartitionRange { int begin, end; }`.
findings.verify_note: Read Level.cpp:375-400, Partitioner.h/.cpp in full, ThreadPool.cpp:38-48, GameStates.cpp:311-330. Confirmed /W4 with no TreatWarningAsError in ArtAttack.vcxproj.

findings.title: unique_ptr<vector<unique_ptr<T>>> adds an owning indirection with no owner semantics — and it is what lets const methods mutate the world
findings.suggestion: Hold and return `std::vector<std::unique_ptr<T>>` by value throughout — members, ctor params (by value + move), builder returns. Four heap allocations and four null states disappear, and `update_level_logic`/`draw_active_level` correctly stop compiling as `const`, which is the point. Route spawned projectiles through a deferred queue drained at end of tick rather than push_back into the container being walked.
findings.verify_note: Read Level.h:58-61/95-105, LevelObjectBuilder.h:19-38, LevelBuilder.cpp:41-56, and Level.cpp:180-322 confirming the const method mutates and appends.

findings.title: Structure::is_colliding unconditionally returns false — the collision contract is asymmetric and undiscoverable
findings.detail:
```cpp
bool Structure::is_colliding(const ICollisionGameObject* other) const { return false; }
void Structure::on_collision(const ICollisionGameObject* other) { /* do nothing */ }
```
Structures — the majority of every level's collision objects, including StructurePaintable which inherits this `is_colliding` — report that they never collide with anything. All structure collision behaviour lives in the *other* participant. `StructurePaintable` then *does* override `on_collision` (StructurePaintable.cpp:64) and depends on the projectile's `is_colliding` returning true for it.

So whether a collision is noticed depends entirely on which participant is the loop's initiator, and the loops are written as though `is_colliding` were symmetric — Level.cpp:259-273 tests `object->is_colliding(player)` and :277-292 tests both orderings, and for structures both are dead. Any future object type whose `is_colliding` filter does not name structures will pass through every wall in the level with no diagnostic.

`other` is also an unused parameter in both functions (C4100 under /W4).

The interface itself is the problem: `ICollisionGameObject::is_colliding` (ICollisionGameObject.h:12) makes every implementer answer a question about geometry, which is why the identical AABB-then-narrow-phase body is copy-pasted in PaintTile.cpp:84-109, Player.cpp:148-185 and every Projectile subclass.
findings.suggestion: `is_colliding` belongs on a `Collider` (shape + layer mask) resolved once by a CollisionSystem, not as a virtual on every game object. Response should be a handler keyed on the layer pair, called exactly once per pair with a documented (a,b) ordering. Failing that, at minimum implement `Structure::is_colliding` properly so the contract is symmetric.
findings.verify_note: Read Structure.cpp:43-50, Level.cpp:259-292, ICollisionGameObject.h, PaintTile.cpp:84-109, Player.cpp:145-185. Traced the dispatch to confirm structure collisions currently only fire via the other participant.

findings.title: Ramps are built with collision types no projectile recognises, so projectiles pass straight through them
findings.detail:
The `"StructureRamp"` branch produces a plain `Structure` tagged `STRUCTURE_RAMP_LEFT` or `STRUCTURE_RAMP_RIGHT` (LevelObjectBuilder.cpp:148-155, 169-176).

`Projectile::is_matching_collision_object_type` (Projectile.cpp:93-118) only accepts three structure types:
```cpp
bool structure_collision =
    other_type == collision_object_type::STRUCTURE ||
    other_type == collision_object_type::STRUCTURE_PAINTABLE ||
    other_type == collision_object_type::STRUCTURE_JUMP_THROUGH;
```
Ramp types are absent, so projectiles never register a collision with a ramp — they fly through and are never marked for deletion by it. `Projectile::on_collision` (Projectile.cpp:120-132) repeats the same three-way list, so even if detection were fixed the despawn would still miss ramps.

Players *do* collide with ramps: `Player::is_matching_collision_object_type` (Player.cpp:145-147) is `return is_structure(other_type);`, and `is_structure` includes both ramp types (collision_object_type.h:75-82). So the two systems disagree about what a ramp is.

The root cause is that "is this thing solid" is spelled out in three hand-written type lists that have already drifted: collision_object_type.h:75-88, Projectile.cpp:98-101 and Projectile.cpp:124-127.
findings.suggestion: Replace the hand-rolled lists in `Projectile::is_matching_collision_object_type` and `Projectile::on_collision` with the shared `is_structure(other_type)` predicate. Long term, replace the type-tag enum with per-object collision layer/mask flags so there is exactly one definition of "solid".
findings.verify_note: Read LevelObjectBuilder.cpp:144-177, Projectile.cpp:93-132, Player.cpp:145-147, collision_object_type.h:75-88. The omission is unambiguous.

findings.title: Match rules, asset names and UI styling for one specific game are compile-time constants inside Level.h
findings.detail:
`namespace level_consts` hardcodes, in the level class's own header: the match length `TIMER = 240.0f`, `START_TIMER = 3.0f`, the countdown font `"gill_sans_mt_bold_144"`, the countdown string `"3"`, two colours, a shadow offset, a text scale, the cue names `"smash_countdown"` and `"slide_whistle_up"` with their volumes, and `ZOOM_OUT_TIMER`/`OVERVIEW_TIMER`.

Every one is game content, not engine behaviour, and none is overridable per level — even though the level JSON already carries `sound.music_name`, `sound.music_volume` and the four bounds rectangles, so the data path exists and was simply not used for these.

Separately, these are namespace-scope `const std::string`/`const Colour` objects in a header. `const` at namespace scope gives internal linkage, so every TU including Level.h gets its own copy with a dynamic initialiser at startup and a destructor at exit. The `static` on some (line 35-40) and not others (line 47, 50) changes nothing. Same pattern at PaintTile.h:15-20 and StructurePaintable.h:12-14 — including `SOUND_BANK_NAME = "sound_bank_1"`, a hardcoded asset name inside a wall class.
findings.suggestion: Move match length, countdown length and the post-match timings into a GameModeConfig loaded from level/mode JSON; move cue names and font/colour styling into a HUD/UI theme resource. For the storage issue, use `inline constexpr std::string_view` (needs the language standard raised — see the separate finding) or move definitions to a .cpp with `extern const` declarations.
findings.verify_note: Read Level.h:31-52, PaintTile.h:10-21, StructurePaintable.h:10-15, and confirmed the level JSON already carries sound.music_name/music_volume and the four bounds rectangles.

findings.title: Shape ownership is unstatable from the signature: a raw const Shape* that is silently cloned, with no null check
findings.detail:
`Structure`'s constructor takes `const MattMath::Shape* collision_shape` (Structure.h:14) and quietly deep-copies it in the member-init list: `_collision_shape(collision_shape->clone())` (Structure.cpp:22). Nothing in the signature says whether the callee retains, adopts or copies, and there is no null check before `->clone()`.

Because the contract is invisible, callers pass the address of stack locals and it only works by luck: LevelObjectBuilder.cpp:62 passes `&rectangle` (local declared at :37), :136 passes `&rectangle` (local at :80), :173 passes `&triangle` (local at :161). Each dies at the end of `build_collision_object`. If the constructor ever stops cloning, or a subclass caches the argument, every structure in every level holds a dangling `Shape*` and nothing at the call site would look wrong. `StructurePaintable` forwards the same raw pointer (StructurePaintable.h:32 → .cpp:25).

Note also that LevelObjectBuilder.cpp:61-62 passes the *same* rectangle as both the sprite rectangle and the collision shape, while :172-173 passes a bounding box and a triangle — the API gives no hint that these may legitimately differ, which is precisely what makes the StructurePaintable face-mapping bug possible (it reads tile positions from `get_rectangle()` and the face set from `get_shape()`).
findings.suggestion: Make the contract part of the type: `const MattMath::Shape& collision_shape` (clones internally, cannot be null) or `std::unique_ptr<MattMath::Shape>` (caller gives it up). The reference form fits the builder, which always has a stack shape it wants copied. Also rename `Structure::get_rectangle()` to `get_sprite_rectangle()`.
findings.verify_note: Read Structure.h:11-41, Structure.cpp:7-25/63-66, LevelObjectBuilder.cpp:37-65/80-142/161-176, StructurePaintable.cpp:9-35.

findings.title: Object factory is a closed if/else chain over hardcoded strings, with duplicated parsing and rapidjson in the public API
findings.detail:
`build_collision_object` is a 165-line chain of `if (type == "Structure") ... if (type == "StructurePaintable") ... if (type == "StructureRamp") ... throw std::exception("Invalid collision object type")` (:19, :67, :144, :179). `build_non_collision_object` (:182-200) knows exactly one type, `"Visual"`. Every new object type in any game built on this engine requires editing this engine-side file — there is no registration point.

The rectangle-parsing block is copy-pasted verbatim: lines 37-56 and 80-99 are byte-identical apart from indentation, and a third partial copy is inlined at :191-194. Any fix to rectangle parsing (e.g. the width/height validation the paint-tile divide needs) has to be made three times.

The public API leaks the parser: `build_collision_objects(const rapidjson::Value& json, ...)` (LevelObjectBuilder.h:20) and `LevelLoadedInfo::get_collision_objects_json()` returning `const rapidjson::Value&` (LevelLoadedInfo.h:26) weld the engine's level format to rapidjson forever, and LevelObjectBuilder.h:6 pulls `rapidjson/document.h` into every consumer.

Parsing is also split with no shared schema: bounds/spawns/audio in LevelLoadedInfo, objects here.

Minor but pervasive: every `if (type == "...")` heap-allocates a `std::string` from a `const char*` rapidjson already owns (:19, 23, 70, 147, 185), and `colour_from_name(json["colour"].GetString())` builds another and linear-scans ~150 string comparisons per object.
findings.suggestion: Replace the chain with a registry `std::unordered_map<std::string, factory_fn>` populated by the *game* at startup. Parse JSON once into engine-neutral `ObjectDesc`/`LevelDesc` PODs so rapidjson never appears in a header. Factor out `parse_rectangle(const Value&)`. Use `std::string_view` for the type comparisons.
findings.verify_note: Read LevelObjectBuilder.cpp and .h in full and LevelLoadedInfo.h:26-27. Diffed lines 37-56 against 80-99 — identical apart from whitespace.

findings.title: get_sound_bank uses map::operator[] so an unknown name returns nullptr through a dead catch, and Level dereferences it unchecked
findings.suggestion: Use `.at()` inside the try so the catch becomes live, or return by reference and throw a descriptive exception on miss. Independently, Level's constructor should validate its injected dependencies (`resource_manager`, `dt`, `sampler_state`, the resolved sound bank) and fail loudly at construction.
findings.verify_note: Read ResourceManager.cpp:66-102 — get_level_info uses .at(), get_sound_bank uses operator[]. Confirmed the unchecked store at Level.cpp:59 and the unguarded use at Level.cpp:73.

findings.title: Game owns its managers as members but the active State lives in a base subobject destroyed last
findings.detail:
`class Game final : public DX::IDeviceNotify, public StateContext` (Game.h:16). The active `State` — `GameLevel`, which owns `std::unique_ptr<Level> _level` (GameStates.h:57) — lives in the `StateContext` **base** subobject. Every manager `Level` points at is a **member** of `Game`: `_resource_manager` (Game.h:65), `_dt` (:66), `_viewport_manager` (:69), `_thread_pool` (:71), `_sprite_batches` (:72), `_audio_engine` (:74), `_partitioner` (:75).

C++ destruction order is body, then members in reverse declaration order, then base classes. So on shutdown every manager is destroyed **before** the StateContext base destroys GameLevel and Level. During `~Level`, `_sound_bank`, `_resolution_manager`, `_viewport_manager`, `_resource_manager`, `_thread_pool`, `_partitioner` and `_dt` (Level.h:107-147) all point at freed memory, as do the equivalents in every Player, Weapon, Structure and PaintTile it transitively owns. It survives only because none of those destructors happens to touch its back-pointers — an invariant nobody wrote down.

Two smaller things in the same header: `std::unique_ptr<State> _state = nullptr;` (Game.h:67) duplicates the base's state pointer and is dead — I grepped Game.cpp and the only `_state` hits are the unrelated `_states` (CommonStates). And Game.h:22-23 defaults the move operations while the constructor publishes `this` via `RegisterDeviceNotify`, so a moved-from Game leaves DeviceResources holding a stale `IDeviceNotify*`.
findings.suggestion: Make `Game` *contain* a `StateContext` member declared after all the managers it depends on, rather than inheriting from it — reverse-order destruction then tears the state machine down first. Delete the unused `_state` member and the defaulted move operations.
findings.verify_note: Read Game.h in full; grepped Game.cpp for `_state` (only `_states` matches, confirming the member is dead); confirmed Level.h:107-147 back-pointer members.

findings.title: GameLevel member declaration order is the inverse of its dependency order — menu States outlive the data they point at
findings.detail:
Declaration order is `_pause_menu` (60), `_pause_menu_action` (61), `_pause_menu_data` (62), `_menu_input` (63), `_results_menu` (64), `_results_menu_action` (65), `_results_menu_data` (66), `_end_menu` (67), `_end_menu_action` (68), `_end_menu_data` (69).

The dependency chain runs `_pause_menu` → `PauseMenuData*` → `MenuInput*` and `pause_menu_action*`, wired at GameStates.cpp:150-162. Reverse-order destruction therefore destroys `_menu_input` (63), then `_pause_menu_data` (62), then `_pause_menu_action` (61), and only then `_pause_menu` (60) — the live `PauseMenuInitial` State is destroyed while its `PauseMenuData*` is already freed, which in turn already had a freed `MenuInput*`. Identical inversion for results (64/66) and end (67/69), which are additionally destroyed before `_menu_input` too.

No destructor currently dereferences those pointers, so it does not crash — the correctness rests entirely on an undocumented "no State destructor may touch its data" rule.

Same file, minor: GameStates.cpp:202 and :279 do `this->_level = std::move(this->_level_builder->build_level(this->_settings));` — `std::move` on a prvalue, suppressing copy elision to force a needless move-construct.
findings.suggestion: Reorder so owners of pointees precede their dependents: `_menu_input`, `_pause_menu_action`, `_pause_menu_data`, `_pause_menu` (and likewise for results/end), with a comment stating the rule. Better, have the data objects own what they need so order stops mattering. Drop the redundant `std::move`.
findings.verify_note: Read GameStates.h:54-74 and GameStates.cpp:150-162, 196-215, 276-283. Declaration order and the wiring are exactly as described.

findings.title: StructurePaintable is a second, hand-rolled mini-level: hidden object list, own broadphase, own draw loop, own audio
findings.detail:
`StructurePaintable` generates a grid of `PaintTile` objects in its **constructor** (`_paint_tiles = generate_paint_tiles()`, :33) and then re-implements the level's own responsibilities for them: update loop (:37-43), draw loop duplicated across both overloads (:45-62), a linear-scan broadphase in `on_collision` (:89-101), audio via its own `SoundBank*` looked up from the hardcoded literal `"sound_bank_1"` playing `"WaterSplashing"` (StructurePaintable.h:12-14, .cpp:34, :97), and scoring (:300-319).

The tiles are full `ICollisionGameObject`s (PaintTile.h:51) that the level never sees, so they get none of the level's culling, partitioning or parallel draw — which is exactly why the never-culled-tiles and linear-scan-per-hit performance findings exist. `PaintTile` implements `is_colliding`/`get_for_deletion`/`get_collision_object_type` purely so its parent can call them by hand; the interface is being used as a "give me collision helpers" mixin.

Doing 195 lines of grid generation in a constructor also means construction can throw or divide by zero (see that finding) with no recovery point.
findings.suggestion: Make the paint surface a component, not an object graph: a `PaintSurface` holding a flat `std::vector<uint8_t> team_per_cell` plus origin and cell size, with O(1) world-position→cell indexing. Rendering becomes one batched pass; scoring becomes a counter updated on write. Audio belongs to an event the level's audio system reacts to, not a `SoundBank*` looked up by a string literal inside a wall.
findings.verify_note: Read StructurePaintable.cpp and .h in full plus PaintTile.h:51-84; every responsibility listed is directly present.

findings.title: PaintTile is a heavyweight polymorphic object with four std::strings and a full animation object, instantiated thousands of times
findings.suggestion: Replace `std::vector<PaintTile>` with a grid: `{ Vector2F origin; float tile_w, tile_h; int nx, ny; std::vector<uint8_t> team; }` — per-cell storage drops from ~300 bytes to 1, and position/colour/sheet/frame are all derivable. Keep a small list of *active* splashes so `update` iterates those, not every cell. Meanwhile: delete `_dt` and move `_splash` into the member-init list.
findings.verify_note: Read PaintTile.h and PaintTile.cpp in full plus the DrawObject/SpriteSheetObject/TextureObject bases; grepped PaintTile.cpp for `_dt` (only the ctor initialiser). Tile counts derived from the parsed level JSON.

findings.title: Level.h pulls 17 headers into every consumer; one is unused and six are needed only for pointer members
findings.detail:
Level.h includes ICollisionGameObject.h, TeamColour.h, level_stage.h, PlayerInput.h, Player.h, ResolutionManager.h, ViewportManager.h, DebugText.h, CameraTools.h, InterfaceGameplay.h, LevelEndInfo.h, TextDropShadow.h, SoundBank.h, IPaintableGameObject.h, ResourceManager.h, ThreadPool.h, Partitioner.h. Because LevelBuilder.h:4 includes Level.h, that whole graph lands in LevelBuilder.cpp, GameStates.cpp and everything downstream.

- `IPaintableGameObject.h` (line 17) is referenced nowhere in Level.h — I grepped for `PaintTotal` and `IPaintable` and the include is the only hit. Its only user is Level.cpp:720.
- `SoundBank`, `ResolutionManager`, `ViewportManager`, `ResourceManager`, `ThreadPool`, `Partitioner` appear only as raw pointer members (Level.h:107, 117-119, 146-147) — forward declarations suffice.
- `DebugText`, `CameraTools`, `InterfaceGameplay`, `TextDropShadow` are `unique_ptr` members; declaring `~Level();` out-of-line in Level.cpp lets all four become forward declarations too.
- `level_stage.h` (line 6) supports `_stage`, which is dead.

Same issue at LevelObjectBuilder.h:7, which includes StructurePaintable.h although the header only mentions `ICollisionGameObject` and `IGameObject`; and LevelObjectBuilder.h:6 / LevelLoadedInfo.h:5 both pull rapidjson into every consumer.
findings.suggestion: Forward-declare the pointer-member types, declare `~Level();` out-of-line, move IPaintableGameObject.h and StructurePaintable.h into the .cpp files, and delete level_stage.h along with the dead `_stage`. This is a prerequisite for the engine ever shipping as a library with a public header surface.
findings.verify_note: Read Level.h:1-20 and cross-checked each include against the header's actual uses; grepped Level.h for PaintTotal/IPaintable (include line only). Read LevelObjectBuilder.h in full.

findings.title: throw std::exception("literal") is an MSVC-only extension, used 54 times project-wide
findings.detail:
The `std::exception(const char*)` constructor does not exist in the C++ standard; it is a Microsoft extension. libstdc++ and libc++ provide only the default constructor, so none of these compile off MSVC.

In this module: LevelObjectBuilder.cpp:34, 55, 77, 98, 129, 158, 179, 199 (eight in one file); Level.cpp:312, 319, 500, 590, 616, 649, 729; LevelEndInfo.cpp:77, 94, 111; PaintTile.cpp:136. I grepped the tree and counted 54 `std::exception("` sites across first-party .cpp files.

For a project whose stated purpose is a reusable engine, this pins it to one toolchain for no benefit. Several of the messages are also load-bearing diagnostics for level authors (`"Invalid collision type"`, `"Invalid rectangle type"`, `"Invalid paintable edges"`) but carry no context — no file, no object index — so a typo in a level JSON produces an unattributable abort.
findings.suggestion: Use `std::runtime_error` / `std::invalid_argument` from `<stdexcept>` (already in pch.h). For the builder, include the offending object's index and type string: `throw std::invalid_argument("collision_objects[" + std::to_string(i) + "]: unknown collision_type '" + collision_type + "'");`.
findings.verify_note: Read the cited lines; ran `grep -rn 'std::exception("' --include=*.cpp` over the first-party tree — 54 matches.

findings.title: Public `= default` constructors produce half-built objects that the very next call dereferences — and one of them is silently deleted
findings.detail:
Five classes in this module declare a defaulted default constructor alongside a real one, none of which is called anywhere:
- `Level() = default;` (Level.h:57) leaves all four object-list `unique_ptr`s null (Level.h:95-105) and every service pointer null; `Level::update` dereferences immediately (`*this->_player_objects` at Level.cpp:78, `*this->_collision_objects` at :183).
- `Structure() = default;` (Structure.h:10) leaves `_collision_shape = nullptr` (Structure.h:40), so `get_shape()` (Structure.cpp:55-58) returns null and `Level::is_object_out_of_bounds` does `object->get_shape()->get_bounding_box()` unguarded (Level.cpp:692) for every collision object every frame.
- `PaintTile() = default;` (PaintTile.h:54) leaves `_dt` null.
- `PaintTileSplash() = default;` (PaintTile.h:26) exists only because `PaintTile::_splash` is default-constructed then reassigned in the ctor *body* (PaintTile.cpp:25-28) instead of in the init list.
- `StructurePaintable() = default;` (StructurePaintable.h:28) is implicitly **deleted**, because `_paintable_edges` is a reference member with no initialiser. The declaration reads as "you may default-construct this" and means the opposite; it compiles only because nobody calls it.

Each one widens the null surface of the whole level pipeline for no benefit.
findings.suggestion: Delete all five — the user-provided constructors already suppress the implicit ones. Move `_splash` into PaintTile's member-init list, which removes the need for `PaintTileSplash()` too. Add asserts/throws on the injected pointers in the real constructors.
findings.verify_note: Read all five declarations and the corresponding member defaults; confirmed StructurePaintable's reference member at .h:56 makes the defaulted ctor ill-formed-if-used, and confirmed none of the five has a caller.

findings.title: PaintTile::is_colliding has no type filter while on_collision hard-throws for anything that isn't a projectile
findings.detail:
Unlike every sibling implementation (Player.cpp:148-159 calls `is_matching_collision_object_type` first), `PaintTile::is_colliding` (PaintTile.cpp:84-109) skips the type check entirely — it does AABB then narrow phase and returns true for *any* overlapping object, including players, structures and same-team projectiles.

`PaintTile::on_collision` (PaintTile.cpp:114-140) then does the opposite and hard-throws:
```cpp
else { throw std::exception("PaintTile::on_collision() - other_type is not a projectile"); }
```
