The pair only works because the single caller, `StructurePaintable::on_collision` (StructurePaintable.cpp:64-101), pre-filters to offensive projectiles before consulting the tiles. But `PaintTile` implements the full `ICollisionGameObject` interface, so the first time anyone puts paint tiles into `Level::_collision_objects` — the obvious next step for making paint interact with anything — the game throws on the first player-tile overlap, with no handler anywhere on the stack.

The two branches in `on_collision` also hand-rewrite `is_team_a_projectile` / `is_team_b_projectile`, which already exist as inline functions at collision_object_type.h:57-73.
findings.suggestion: Add the type filter to `is_colliding` so the two functions agree on what a PaintTile collides with, and make `on_collision` ignore non-projectiles rather than throwing. Call the existing predicates instead of respelling them.
findings.verify_note: Read PaintTile.cpp:84-148, Player.cpp:148-185 (which does filter), StructurePaintable.cpp:64-102 (the pre-filter), collision_object_type.h:57-73.

findings.title: draw_zoom_out_level dispatches one task to the thread pool and immediately blocks on it; num_threads is dead
findings.suggestion: Call `draw_zoom_out_level_component` directly and delete both the pool round trip and the unused local. Turn on TreatWarningAsError for at least the Debug configuration so the next one of these is caught at the point of writing.
findings.verify_note: Read Level.cpp:595-607 and ThreadPool.cpp:38-58; grepped ArtAttack.vcxproj for TreatWarningAsError (absent) and WarningLevel (Level4 in all four configs).

findings.title: Hand-rolled swap-erase relies on unique_ptr self-move-assignment and unsigned wraparound; the codebase uses zero standard algorithms
findings.suggestion: `objs.erase(std::remove_if(objs.begin(), objs.end(), [](const auto& o){ return o->get_for_deletion(); }), objs.end());` — order-preserving, one pass, no index arithmetic. Convert the other sites too, and bind `Player& player = *(*_player_objects)[i];` at the top of the draw loop.
findings.verify_note: Read Level.cpp:296-305 and 496-592, StructurePaintable.cpp:300-319. Confirmed `<algorithm>` IS in pch.h:42 (correcting the candidate) and confirmed zero uses of any standard algorithm across the first-party tree by grep.

findings.title: _zoom_out_camera is one frame stale at the ACTIVE→ZOOM_OUT transition, producing a visible camera pop
findings.detail:
The transition to ZOOM_OUT happens inside the `if (_state == level_state::ACTIVE)` branch (Level.cpp:126-138), and the branch that computes `_zoom_out_camera` is `else if (_state == level_state::ZOOM_OUT)` (:139) — chained off the same if. So on the frame the match timer expires, the state flips to ZOOM_OUT but the else-if is not evaluated.

`Level::draw` (:365-372) then routes that frame to `draw_zoom_out_level`, which renders with `_zoom_out_camera` still holding its declared initial value `MattMath::Camera::DEFAULT_CAMERA` (Level.h:126). One frame rendered with the identity camera before the interpolation starts on the following frame — a snap at the exact moment the whistle blows.

This is the generic hazard of an if/else-if ladder over a state enum with no entry hooks: any state entered in this tick has its handler skipped until the next tick.
findings.suggestion: Compute the zoom-out camera at ratio 0 when entering the state, or restructure `update()` as a `switch` with explicit `enter_state()` hooks so the handler for a newly-entered state runs in the same frame.
findings.verify_note: Read Level.cpp:126-175 and 354-373, Level.h:126. The if/else-if chaining and the resulting one-frame skip are unambiguous; only the visual severity is a judgement call, hence low.

findings.title: Three ramp classes are 100% commented out but still in the build, while ramps are faked as a Structure carrying an enum tag
findings.detail:
StructureRamp.h is entirely commented out (all 23 lines) and StructureRamp.cpp is a lone `#include "pch.h"` followed by 26 commented lines. StructureRampLeft.h/.cpp and StructureRampRight.h/.cpp are the same. Yet all six files are still listed in ArtAttack.vcxproj (lines 252-254 and 348-350), and LevelObjectBuilder.h:10-11 still carries their commented-out includes.

Meanwhile the real ramp construction (LevelObjectBuilder.cpp:144-177) builds a plain `Structure` from a `TriangleRightAxisAligned` and distinguishes ramp-ness only by `collision_object_type::STRUCTURE_RAMP_LEFT/RIGHT`. So "ramp" is a behavioural variant expressed as an enum tag on a base class, which forces `Player::on_collision` to branch on the tag (Player.cpp:236-238) to get ramp movement. The one genuinely ramp-specific behaviour, `get_gradient()`, exists only in the commented-out code (StructureRamp.cpp:23-27).

This is also the direct cause of the projectiles-pass-through-ramps bug reported separately.
findings.suggestion: Pick one: delete the six dead files and their vcxproj entries, or finish the type and give it `get_gradient()`/`get_surface_normal()` so ramp behaviour is polymorphic instead of an enum branch inside Player. Given the wider collision_object_type problem, the right destination is a slope/material property on the collider.
findings.verify_note: Read StructureRamp.h and .cpp in full (fully commented), grepped ArtAttack.vcxproj confirming all six files are still compiled/included, read LevelObjectBuilder.h:10-11 and .cpp:144-177.

findings.title: IGameObject's two draw overloads force every class to duplicate its draw body verbatim
findings.detail:
`IGameObject` (IGameObject.h:11-12) requires both `draw(SpriteBatch*, const Camera&)` and `draw(SpriteBatch*)`. In this module alone that produces four verbatim duplications:
- `PaintTile::draw(sb, camera)` (:34-53) and `PaintTile::draw(sb)` (:54-75) — identical 19-line bodies including the whole team→colour switch, differing only in whether `camera` is forwarded.
- `StructurePaintable::draw` ×2 (:45-52 vs :54-62)
- `Structure::draw` ×2 (Structure.cpp:31-34 vs :35-38)
- `PaintTileSplash::draw` ×2 (PaintTile.cpp:189-192 vs :193-196)

The camera-less overload exists only for UI-space drawing, which the level path never uses — and `MattMath::Camera::DEFAULT_CAMERA` already exists (Level.h:126) to express exactly that.

Related: `PaintTileSplash::set_colour` (PaintTile.cpp:181-184) and `::update` (:185-188) are pure forwarding overrides whose only effect is to widen `DrawObject::set_colour` from protected (DrawObject.h:27) to public (PaintTile.h:40).
findings.suggestion: Collapse to a single `virtual void draw(DirectX::SpriteBatch*, const MattMath::Camera& = Camera::DEFAULT_CAMERA) const = 0;` and delete the second overload from every implementer. For the access widening, `using AnimationObject::set_colour;` in the public section states the intent and generates no code.
findings.verify_note: Read IGameObject.h, PaintTile.cpp:34-75 and 181-196, StructurePaintable.cpp:45-62, Structure.cpp:31-38, DrawObject.h:19-31.

findings.title: The projectile/team type-enum chain is hand-rewritten in four places instead of using the predicates that already exist
findings.detail:
`Level::count_projectiles` (Level.cpp:663-675) writes a 10-way `type == PROJECTILE_*_TEAM_*` disjunction that is character-for-character the body of `is_projectile()` at collision_object_type.h:43-55 — and the local variable even shadows its name.

The same shape appears three more times: `StructurePaintable::on_collision` (StructurePaintable.cpp:68-78, another 10-way chain equal to `is_projectile`) and `PaintTile::on_collision` (PaintTile.cpp:118-133, which is `is_team_a_projectile` / `is_team_b_projectile` from collision_object_type.h:57-73 split in two).

Every new weapon adds two enum values and requires editing all four chains plus the predicate helpers; missing one fails silently — a projectile that paints nothing, or a debug counter that under-reports.

The root cause is that the enum cross-multiplies class × team × weapon into 23 flat values (collision_object_type.h:4-29), so "what kind of thing is this" and "whose team is it" can only be answered by enumeration.

`count_projectiles` is also called from inside the per-player draw loop (Level.cpp:574) whenever a player has debug enabled — recomputed per viewport, from multiple threads, over a list unchanged since `update`, for a value identical for every player.
findings.suggestion: At minimum call the existing `is_projectile` / `is_team_a_projectile` / `is_team_b_projectile` helpers. Properly: split the axes — an `object_kind`, a separate `TeamId`, and a weapon id — and expose `get_team()` on `ICollisionGameObject` so `PaintTile::on_collision` becomes `_team = other->get_team();` with no chain and no throw. Compute the projectile count once at the end of update and cache it.
findings.verify_note: Read Level.cpp:658-682 and 571-578, StructurePaintable.cpp:64-84, PaintTile.cpp:114-140, collision_object_type.h:43-73. All four chains are literal duplicates of the inline helpers.

findings.title: Every LevelLoadedInfo getter re-walks the retained JSON DOM and returns a fresh heap-allocated value
findings.detail:
All eleven accessors are computed on demand from the retained `rapidjson::Document _json_doc` (LevelLoadedInfo.h:34): `get_level_name()` (LevelLoadedInfo.cpp:15-18) allocates a string per call; `get_team_a_spawns()` (:19-23) re-parses the array and builds a fresh `std::vector<Vector2F>` per call; `get_out_of_bounds_rectangle()` (:30-37) does four DOM lookups.

So `LevelLoadedInfo` keeps the whole parsed document alive for the process lifetime (it is cached in ResourceManager) purely to re-derive a handful of scalars. `LevelBuilder::build_level` (LevelBuilder.cpp:66-74) calls seven of them per build, and `Level`'s constructor then copies the two spawn vectors and the level name into members it never reads — three allocations per level load for data that is thrown away.

Retaining the Document is only genuinely required for `get_collision_objects_json()` / `get_non_collision_objects_json()`, which return `const rapidjson::Value&` and thereby leak rapidjson into the header (LevelLoadedInfo.h:5, 26-27) and into every TU that includes it.

None of the getters is `[[nodiscard]]`, so `get_music_volume();` on its own line compiles silently.
findings.suggestion: Parse once in the constructor into plain value members, return `const&` for containers and strings, and drop the Document once the object arrays have been consumed into engine-neutral descriptors — which also removes rapidjson from the public header.
findings.verify_note: Read LevelLoadedInfo.h and .cpp in full and LevelBuilder.cpp:30-83. Confirmed the seven getter calls per build and the three discarded copies into Level.

findings.title: A fresh vector is allocated per player per frame to carry projectiles that usually don't exist
findings.suggestion: Change the weapon API to append into a caller-supplied container so the common case is zero allocations. If the by-value return stays, at least use `insert` with `std::make_move_iterator` so the destination grows once. Longer term, pool projectiles. And route spawns through a deferred queue drained at end of tick rather than into the live container.
findings.verify_note: Read Level.cpp:188-222; the per-player-per-frame vector and element-by-element move are exactly as described.

findings.title: Heap-allocated instance of an all-static class; build_level should be const and [[nodiscard]]
findings.detail:
```cpp
std::unique_ptr<TeamColourTools> _team_colour = nullptr;          // LevelBuilder.h:29
this->_team_colour = std::make_unique<TeamColourTools>();         // LevelBuilder.cpp:23
const TeamColour team_colours = _team_colour->generate_random_team_colour();  // LevelBuilder.cpp:36
```
`TeamColourTools` (TeamColour.h) has no data members and all its functions are static. The `unique_ptr`, the `make_unique` and the `->` are ceremony around what could be `TeamColourTools::generate_random_team_colour()`.

Relatedly, `LevelBuilder::build_level` (LevelBuilder.h:26) is non-`const` although it mutates nothing — it reads pointer members and calls LevelObjectBuilder's `const` methods — and it is the module's principal factory with no `[[nodiscard]]`, so discarding its result silently builds and destroys an entire level.
findings.suggestion: Turn `TeamColourTools` into a namespace of free functions, delete the member and its allocation, and mark `build_level` `[[nodiscard]] ... const` (which requires raising the language standard — see that finding).
findings.verify_note: Read LevelBuilder.h and .cpp in full; confirmed the member is used only at line 36 for one static call.

findings.title: No LanguageStandard set (defaults to C++14) and no TreatWarningAsError, so /W4 findings accumulate unseen
findings.detail:
I grepped all four configurations. `WarningLevel` is `Level4` (lines 91, 113, 134, 160), `ConformanceMode` is `true` (96, 117, 141, 166), `FloatingPointModel` is `Fast` (94, 116, 139, 165), `PlatformToolset` is v145 (31, 38, 45, 53) — but there is **no** `LanguageStandard` element anywhere, so the compiler falls back to its default, `/std:c++14`. That blocks `[[nodiscard]]` (zero occurrences project-wide — I grepped), `inline` variables for the header constants, `std::string_view` for the parser comparisons, structured bindings, and `if constexpr` — every one of which is recommended by other findings in this review.

`TreatWarningAsError` is set nowhere, which is why the C4189 (unused `num_threads`, Level.cpp:599), C4101 (unused `e`, Level.cpp:727), C4018 (signed/unsigned at Level.cpp:386, StructurePaintable.cpp:189/191, GameStates.cpp:321) and C4100 (unused `other`, Structure.cpp:43/47) instances found in this review have survived.

`FloatingPointModel=Fast` also licenses the compiler to assume no NaN/inf, which interacts badly with the divide-by-zero in StructurePaintable.cpp:111/116 and the NaN in LevelEndInfo.cpp:115.
findings.suggestion: Add `<LanguageStandard>stdcpp20</LanguageStandard>` (or at least stdcpp17) to all four configurations, then enable `TreatWarningAsError` for Debug and fix the resulting list. Reconsider `/fp:fast` given the division guards this codebase does not have.
findings.verify_note: Grepped ArtAttack.vcxproj for LanguageStandard (absent), TreatWarningAsError (absent), WarningLevel/ConformanceMode/FloatingPointModel/PlatformToolset (present as described); grepped the whole tree for `nodiscard` (0 hits).

findings.title: Dead code in the module: unused local, empty never-called method, uncalled public mutator, 110 lines of commented-out drafts
findings.detail:
Consolidating the dead-code items, all verified by reading and grep:
- Level.cpp:599 — `int num_threads = ...` in `draw_zoom_out_level`, never used (C4189).
- Level.h:152 / Level.cpp:696-699 — `void Level::draw_end_screen() { // TODO }`: private, empty, zero call sites.
- Level.h:88 / Level.cpp:701-704 — `Level::set_state(level_state)` is public with zero callers and bypasses every transition side-effect in `update()` (music stop, sound stop, camera setup at :130-160).
- Level.cpp:331-353 and 402-490 — ~110 lines of commented-out earlier `draw`/`draw_active_level` implementations; line 402-404 is a stray fragment with no matching body.
- Structure.cpp:43-50 — both `is_colliding` and `on_collision` ignore their `other` parameter entirely (C4100).
- Level.cpp:727 — `catch (const std::bad_cast& e)` binds `e` and never uses it (C4101).
- StructurePaintable.cpp:118-180 — 60 lines of a commented-out earlier `generate_paint_tiles` implementation, plus the commented `PaintableFaces` struct at StructurePaintable.h:17-23 and LevelObjectBuilder.cpp:101-105 (which, ironically, is the correct design the working code should return to).
- LevelObjectBuilder.h:10-11 — commented-out includes for the fully-commented ramp headers.
findings.suggestion: Delete all of it. Version control is the archive for old implementations; commented-out code in the file is a maintenance tax and, in the PaintableFaces case, actively misleading about which design is live.
findings.verify_note: Read each cited range; grepped for callers of draw_end_screen and Level::set_state (zero outside the definitions).

findings.title: Level objects inherit their rendering implementation instead of composing a sprite, and polymorphic bases allow slicing assignment
findings.detail:
`class Structure : public TextureObject, public ICollisionGameObject` (Structure.h:7) and `class PaintTile final : public TextureObject, public ICollisionGameObject` (PaintTile.h:51) both inherit an *implementation* base (TextureObject → SpriteSheetObject → DrawObject) alongside an interface; `PaintTileSplash : public AnimationObject, public IGameObject` (PaintTile.h:23) does the same with the other rendering base.

Consequences visible here: `Structure` inherits five protected `draw` overloads it doesn't want (TextureObject.h:19-32) and must disambiguate with `this->TextureObject::draw(...)` (Structure.cpp:33, PaintTile.cpp:52/72); an object cannot have two sprites, or a sprite *and* an animation, without inheriting the same base twice; and `Structure`'s `_sprite_rectangle` doubles as both draw geometry and visibility bounds (Structure.cpp:39-42), so visual and collision extents cannot diverge.

Separately, none of these polymorphic bases suppresses assignment. `Structure` is a public base of `StructurePaintable`, declares no copy/move operations, and so gets a public implicit move-assignment — meaning `Structure& a = ...; a = std::move(b);` on two references that are actually StructurePaintables compiles and silently slices, stealing the collision shape and discarding `_paint_tiles`/`_team_colours`/`_sound_bank`. Same hole in `IGameObject` (IGameObject.h:6-14), `ICollisionGameObject` (ICollisionGameObject.h:8-17), `IPaintableGameObject` (IPaintableGameObject.h:10-15) and `DrawObject` (DrawObject.h:9-11), all of which have a public defaulted virtual destructor and no suppressed assignment. Not currently exercised, but free to close.
findings.suggestion: Compose rather than inherit: `Structure` should *hold* a `Sprite` and a `Collider`, not *be* a TextureObject. Meanwhile give every polymorphic base the standard non-sliceable shape (protected copy/move, public virtual dtor).
findings.verify_note: Read Structure.h, PaintTile.h, TextureObject.h, DrawObject.h, IGameObject.h, ICollisionGameObject.h, IPaintableGameObject.h — none declares or deletes copy/move assignment, and the disambiguating `this->TextureObject::draw` calls are present as described.

findings.title: ID3D11CommandList COM objects held as raw pointers with manual Release — leaked on any throwing path
findings.detail:
`FinishCommandList(TRUE, &command_lists->at(i))` (Level.cpp:587, and :646 in the zoom-out path) hands back a COM object with refcount 1 into a raw `ID3D11CommandList*` slot. The only `Release()` is the manual loop in the caller (GameStates.cpp:321-330).

Everything between is a leak window. `draw_player_view_level` processes a whole partition in one loop and throws at :500 and :590, so a failure on partition element 2 leaks the list already produced for element 1; unwinding past GameStates.cpp:321 leaks every list produced by the other workers. (In practice the throw terminates the process anyway — see that finding — so the leak is academic today, hence low.)

Relatedly, the `add_task` loop at Level.cpp:386-397 is not exception-safe: `command_lists` points at a stack local in `GameLevel::draw` (GameStates.cpp:313), and `ThreadPool::add_task` can throw (`new std::function` bad_alloc, or `CreateThreadpoolWork` failure at ThreadPool.cpp:44). If task 0 is submitted and task 1's `add_task` throws, the unguarded `wait_for_tasks_to_complete()` at :399 is skipped and the stack frame is destroyed while worker 0 is still writing into it.

`Microsoft::WRL::ComPtr` is already available and used elsewhere in the project, so this is inconsistency, not a constraint.
findings.suggestion: Change the parameter to `std::vector<Microsoft::WRL::ComPtr<ID3D11CommandList>>*` and pass `ReleaseAndGetAddressOf()`; the caller then does `ExecuteCommandList(list.Get(), TRUE)` and the vector's destructor releases. Have `ThreadPool` hand back a scope guard whose destructor waits, so the wait cannot be skipped.
findings.verify_note: Read Level.cpp:375-400/580-592/640-651, GameStates.cpp:311-330, ThreadPool.cpp:38-58. The add_task-throws path is real but requires an allocation failure, hence low.

findings.title: LevelEndInfo mixes a score record with UI string formatting and hardcoded English copy
findings.detail:
A 3-field struct with 14 member functions. Alongside the legitimate score queries it carries presentation:
- `winning_team_string()` (LevelEndInfo.cpp:62-78) returns the literal UI copy `"Team A Wins!"` / `"Team B Wins!"` / `"Draw!"` — no localisation seam.
- `team_a_percentage_string()` and `team_b_percentage_string()` (:42-61) are byte-identical apart from which field they read, and format by `std::to_string` then `find('.')` then `substr` rather than with a formatting facility.

That is presentation policy living in the scoring record, with the two teams hardcoded into both the field names and the copy — the same two-team assumption flagged on `IPaintableGameObject`.
findings.suggestion: Reduce to a plain results record (per-team scores keyed by TeamId, plus `winner()`), and move string production into the results-menu UI where font, language and rounding policy live. Deduplicate the two percentage-string functions into one taking a `player_team`, formatted with `std::ostringstream << std::fixed << std::setprecision(1)`.
findings.verify_note: Read LevelEndInfo.h and .cpp in full; the two *_percentage_string bodies differ only in the call at line 44 vs 54.

findings.title: level_mode is stored on MenuLevelSettings but no code ever reads it — there is no rule-set abstraction
findings.detail:
`enum class level_mode { STANDARD_MODE, TEAM_DEATHMATCH, DEATHMATCH, PRACTICE };` is stored on `MenuLevelSettings` (MenuLevelSettings.h:32) and set from the mode-select menu. I grepped the whole tree: `MenuLevelSettings::get_game_mode()` (MenuLevelSettings.h:18, .cpp:37) has **zero callers**. `LevelBuilder::build_level` (LevelBuilder.cpp:30-83) never asks for it and `Level` never sees it.

This is the symptom of the missing abstraction: there is exactly one hardcoded rule set (paint-area scoring on a 240s timer) spread across `Level::update`, `Level::get_level_end_info` and `LevelEndInfo`, so a second mode has nowhere to live.

I am **downgrading** this from the reported medium and correcting the reported consequence: one reviewer claimed "the player can pick Deathmatch and get a paint-area match". That is false — MainMenu.cpp:673-680 plays `ERROR_SOUND` and refuses to advance for the `"tdm"` and `"dm"` elements; only `"standard"` proceeds (MainMenu.cpp:663-671). The menu does not lie; the enum values are simply unimplemented placeholders.
findings.suggestion: Introduce a `GameMode` interface owned by the level (`on_start`, `update`, `is_finished`, `build_results`) and have `LevelBuilder` select the implementation from `settings.get_game_mode()`; `PaintCoverageMode` becomes one implementation. Until then, either remove the unimplemented enumerators or leave them — but delete the unreachable `get_game_mode` accessor so it stops looking wired up.
findings.verify_note: Grepped level_mode across the tree — only MainMenu.cpp, MenuLevelSettings and the enum itself. Read MainMenu.cpp:650-690 and found the tdm/dm branches play ERROR_SOUND rather than proceeding, which refutes the reported consequence.

findings.title: Pause menu indexes the input vector by player number with no bounds check
findings.detail: `PauseMenuInitial::update()` (lines 48-59) reads `int player_num = get_pause_menu_data()->get_player_num();` and then does `inputs[player_num].action == ...` at lines 53, 54, 59, 82, 98. `MenuInput::update_and_get_menu_inputs()` (MenuInput.cpp:138-149) only `push_back`s entries for pads where `current[i].connected` is true, so `inputs.size()` is the count of CONNECTED pads, not 4. `player_num` was captured on an earlier frame by `GameLevel::check_for_pause_input` (GameStates.cpp:144-146, 345-357) as an index into a differently-built compacted `PlayerInputData` vector. If a pad disconnects while the pause menu is open, `inputs.size()` shrinks; `operator[]` is unchecked, so this reads past the end. If all pads drop, `inputs` is empty and `inputs[player_num]` dereferences a null data pointer. `PauseMenuConfirmation::update()` repeats the identical pattern at lines 222, 229, 256, 257. `PauseMenuData::_player_num` also defaults to `-1` (PauseMenuData.h:19) with no validation in the setter. Note the rest of the module defends itself by bounding the loop (`i < num_inputs && i < player_count`, MainMenu.cpp:1160, 1443, 1790) — the pause menu is the one place that indexes blind.
findings.suggestion: Make MenuInput return a fixed 4-slot result so the index is the pad slot (see the MenuInput API finding). Until then, guard at the top of both `update()` bodies: `if (player_num < 0 || player_num >= static_cast<int>(inputs.size())) return;`.
findings.verify_note: Read PauseMenu.cpp:46-114 and 215-268 — all six indexing sites use raw operator[] with no size check. Read MenuInput.cpp:131-150 and confirmed the push_back is guarded by current[i].connected. Read GameStates.cpp:345-357 confirming player_num comes from a separate compacted PlayerInput vector.

findings.title: MenuInput returns a compacted vector, so the input index silently stops matching the player index
findings.suggestion: Return `const std::array<ProcessedMenuInput, MAX_PLAYERS>&` indexed by gamepad slot, with `connection` set honestly from `current[i].connected`, and introduce `constexpr int MAX_PLAYERS = 4` in a shared header. Index == player becomes true by construction, the bounds hazard disappears, and menus can render "Player 3: controller disconnected" instead of hanging.
findings.verify_note: Read MenuInput.cpp:131-150 and MenuInput.h in full. Confirmed the compaction, the unconditional CONNECTED at line 127, the DISCONNECTED default at MenuInput.h:41 that can never be observed, and the four hardcoded 4s.

findings.title: Choosing more players than connected controllers makes team/weapon select impossible to complete
findings.detail: `MainMenuPlayerCount::update` sets the player count purely from the highlighted widget with no check that that many pads are connected (lines 899-950, e.g. `set_player_count(4)` at 942-943). `MainMenuTeamSelect::update` then loops `for (int i = 0; i < num_inputs && i < player_count; i++)` (line 1160), where `num_inputs` is the number of connected pads, while `all_players_confirmed()` (1236-1246) loops all the way to `get_player_count()`. With 4 players selected and 2 pads connected, `_select_states[2]` and `[3]` can never become CONFIRMED, so the page can never advance. `MainMenuWeaponSelect` has the identical shape (1443, 1555-1565). Nothing on screen indicates why. Correction to the original report: this is recoverable, not a hard lock — the BACK branch checks `all_players_unconfirmed()` first (1162-1171), so a player who has confirmed can press BACK once to unconfirm themselves and again to leave the screen. The defect is that the forward path is unreachable with no feedback.
findings.suggestion: Count connected pads (the `connection_state` field exists for exactly this and is currently never populated honestly) and either reject/grey out player counts above that number in `MainMenuPlayerCount`, or visibly mark slots with no controller and exclude them from `all_players_confirmed()`.
findings.verify_note: Read MainMenu.cpp:880-1009 (no connectivity check on any of the four set_player_count calls), 1154-1224 (loop bounded by num_inputs), 1236-1257 (confirmed/unconfirmed loops bounded by get_player_count). Traced the BACK path to establish the escape route the original candidate said did not exist.

findings.title: Results fill bars are sized in 1920x1080 design units after the container was already scaled
findings.detail:
`ResultsMenuInitial::init()` builds everything in design space and scales once at lines 194-197 (`_texture_container->scale_objects_to_new_resolution(DEFAULT_RESOLUTION, resolution)`). But `update_team_a_fill()` / `update_team_b_fill()` run every frame after that and write raw design-space numbers into the already-scaled rectangles:
```cpp
float max_width = RESULTS_MENU_TEAM_FILL_SIZE.x * score;  // 680.0f, unscaled (ResultsMenu.h:21-23)
this->_team_a_fill->set_width(fill * max_width);
```
`calculate_team_b_fill_top_right_position()` (254-261) is worse — it adds the already-scaled `_fill_box` position and width to the UNSCALED `RESULTS_MENU_TEAM_FILL_BORDER` constant. This happens to be consistent when called from `init()` at line 153 (pre-scale) but is inconsistent when called from `update_team_b_fill()` at line 251 (post-scale). At 1280x720 (scale 0.667) `_fill_box` renders ~466px wide while the bars are driven to 680px, overflowing the box; at higher resolutions a 100% bar underfills. The height IS correct because it was baked in before scaling (lines 114, 125), so the aspect is wrong too. Only 1920x1080 is right.
findings.suggestion: Derive the bar extent from the live, already-scaled `_fill_box` rectangle every frame — `max_width = _fill_box->get_rectangle().get_width() - 2 * scaled_border.x` — so the animation is scale-agnostic by construction, and delete the design-space constant from the per-frame path.
findings.verify_note: Read ResultsMenu.cpp:73-200 and 214-261 plus results_menu_consts in ResultsMenu.h:11-52. Verified RESULTS_MENU_TEAM_FILL_SIZE is {680,180} computed from unscaled constants, that scaling happens once at init line 194, and that the update functions run every frame from update() line 41.

findings.title: Menu pages draw once per viewport of a stale screen_layout, tiling the main menu after a multiplayer quit
findings.detail: `MenuPage::draw_mobject_in_viewports` loops over whatever `ViewportManager` currently reports (lines 99-115) and draws the widget once per viewport. That is right for the pause menu; the main menu uses the identical path. `ViewportManager::set_layout` is called from exactly two places in the whole codebase — `GameStates.cpp:122-123` (on level start, sets the match layout) and `Level.cpp:618` (only inside `draw_zoom_out_level_component`, reached on the level-end zoom-out). Nothing resets the layout on the quit path: `GameLevel::update` case `pause_menu_action::QUIT` (GameStates.cpp:203-212) transitions straight to `GameMenu` with `screen = HOME`, and `GameMenu::init` (GameStates.cpp:19-62) never touches the viewport manager. So after a 3- or 4-player match, pause -> Quit leaves `_layout == FOUR_PLAYER` and `MainMenuHome` is rendered four times, once into each quadrant.
findings.suggestion: Have `GameMenu::init()` call `get_viewport_manager()->set_layout(screen_layout::ONE_PLAYER)`. Longer term split the API: `draw_in_all_viewports()` for in-match overlays vs `draw_fullscreen()` for the front-end, so the front-end does not depend on residual match state.
findings.verify_note: grep for set_layout across ArtAttack/ returned exactly GameStates.cpp:123, Level.cpp:619, and the definition. Read GameStates.cpp:196-212 (QUIT path) and 19-62 (GameMenu::init) — neither resets the layout. Read MenuPage.cpp:99-115 confirming the per-viewport loop.

findings.title: Menu drawing throws from inside Win32 thread-pool callbacks, which terminates the process
findings.detail: `draw_mobject_in_viewports` throws on two paths — `throw std::exception("Deferred context not created")` (line 96) and `throw std::exception("Failed to finish command list")` (line 120) — and is only ever reached from the lambda submitted at lines 142-149. `ThreadPool::work_callback` (ThreadPool.cpp:59-65) is `void CALLBACK f(...) { (*task)(); delete task; }` with no try/catch, so an escaping exception unwinds out of an OS callback and calls `std::terminate`; `delete task` is also skipped and every sibling task's already-created `ID3D11CommandList` leaks because the `Release()` loop at MenuPage.cpp:154-163 never runs. Worse, `DeviceResources::get_deferred_context(int)` — called at MenuPage.cpp:175 from inside the same worker — is declared **`noexcept`** (DeviceResources.cpp:737-738) and unconditionally `throw std::out_of_range("Invalid index.")` on a bad index, which is a guaranteed immediate `std::terminate` rather than a catchable error. `ResourceManager`/`SpriteSheet` lookups reached through `MObject::draw` can also throw. A device reset or a missing asset while a menu is on screen kills the process with no diagnostics.
findings.suggestion: Wrap the task body in `try { ... } catch (...) { store exception_ptr }` inside `ThreadPool::work_callback` and rethrow on the calling thread after `wait_for_tasks_to_complete()`. Remove `noexcept` from `get_deferred_context` or make it return nullptr. Store `Microsoft::WRL::ComPtr<ID3D11CommandList>` so release is automatic on every path.
findings.verify_note: Read MenuPage.cpp:89-178 in full, ThreadPool.cpp:37-65 (no try/catch, task deleted only on success, add_task throws after earlier SubmitThreadpoolWork), and DeviceResources.cpp:732-745 — get_deferred_context really is `noexcept` and really does throw.

findings.title: Options 'Apply' has a dead SetWindowPos, discards the chosen resolution in fullscreen, and sizes the window rect instead of the client rect
findings.detail:
Three separate defects in the apply path:
1. **The `SetWindowPos` at lines 334-340 is dead.** `apply_fullscreen_setting` (427-451), called two lines later at 344, overrides it in both branches — the fullscreen path issues `SetWindowPos(..., SWP_NOSIZE, ...)` then `ShowWindow(hWnd, SW_SHOWMAXIMIZED)`, and the windowed path re-issues `SetWindowPos(hWnd, HWND_TOP, 0, 0, res_i.x, res_i.y, ...)` with the same values plus `SWP_FRAMECHANGED`, which the first call omits.
2. **In fullscreen the chosen resolution is discarded.** `SW_SHOWMAXIMIZED` (line 438) sizes the window to the monitor, but `ResolutionManager::_resolution` and the save file now say e.g. 1280x720. `ViewportManager::calculate_d3d11_viewport` derives every viewport from `_resolution_manager->get_resolution_vec()` (ViewportManager.cpp:45-58), so the game renders into a rect that does not match the back buffer.
3. **In windowed mode the resolution is applied as a window rect.** `WS_OVERLAPPEDWINDOW` (line 442) adds caption and borders, so the client area — and the back buffer — is always smaller than the resolution `ResolutionManager` claims. No `AdjustWindowRect` anywhere on this path. `Main.cpp:150` computes `AdjustWindowRect(&rc, WS_OVERLAPPEDWINDOW, FALSE)` and then ignores `rc`, passing `res_ivec2.x/y` to `CreateWindowExW` — the same bug at startup.
Everything downstream (`scale_objects_to_new_resolution(DEFAULT_RESOLUTION, get_float_resolution())` in all twelve `init()`s) is laid out against a resolution the window never actually has.
findings.suggestion: Delete the redundant `SetWindowPos` at 334-340. Compute the target rect with `AdjustWindowRectEx` for windowed mode; for fullscreen either go borderless at the desktop resolution and force `ResolutionManager` to match, or do a real DXGI mode set. Feed the actual client rect back through `WM_SIZE` so there is one source of truth for render resolution.
findings.verify_note: Read MainMenu.cpp:300-451 in full and Main.cpp:145-166. Confirmed the ordering (SetWindowPos at 334 precedes apply_fullscreen_setting at 344), the SW_SHOWMAXIMIZED at 438, the missing AdjustWindowRect in both the menu and Main.cpp paths, and that rc is computed and never used in Main.cpp.

findings.title: transition_to destroys the running state from inside its own update(); correctness rests on an unwritten 'return immediately' rule
findings.suggestion: Make transitions deferred: have `State::update()` return a requested transition (or set a pending `unique_ptr<State>` on the context) and have `StateContext::update()` apply it after `_state->update()` returns. That removes the whole class of bug and the need for the `return;` discipline.
findings.verify_note: Read StateContext.cpp in full and every cited call site in PauseMenu.cpp:46-114/215-268 and MainMenu.cpp. Verified the missing returns at PauseMenu.cpp:70-80 and MainMenu.cpp:165-168, and disproved the 'quit branch evaluated on destroyed object' claim by re-reading the else-if chain.

findings.title: MenuPage — the base class for all UI — is a D3D11 command-list orchestrator
findings.detail: `MenuPage`'s protected API, the surface every UI subclass sees, is raw graphics plumbing: `draw_mobject_in_viewports(ID3D11DeviceContext* deferred_context, ID3D11CommandList*& command_list, DirectX::SpriteBatch*, MObject*, ID3D11SamplerState*)` (38-41), `draw_mobjects_in_viewports(std::vector<std::pair<MObject*, ID3D11SamplerState*>>*)` (43-44), `draw_range_of_mobjects_in_viewports(int, int, vector<pair<MObject*,ID3D11SamplerState*>>*, vector<ID3D11DeviceContext*>*, vector<ID3D11CommandList*>*, vector<SpriteBatch*>*)` (46-50) and `get_point_clamp_sampler_state()` (52). The implementation (MenuPage.cpp:89-183) calls `ViewportManager::apply_player_viewport`, `SpriteBatch::Begin/End`, `FinishCommandList`, `ThreadPool::add_task`, `Partitioner::partition`, `ExecuteCommandList` and `Release()`. For a project whose stated goal is a reusable 2D engine, the UI base class being a renderer means no UI can exist without D3D11, DirectXTK, the thread pool and the partitioner.
findings.suggestion: Split into two types: `MenuPage`/`UIScreen` owns a widget tree and exposes `build(UIContext&)`, `update(const InputFrame&)` and nothing else; a separate `UIRenderer` owns deferred contexts, sprite batches, sampler states, viewport iteration and command-list submission and is handed to pages as an interface. No UI header should include d3d11.h.
findings.verify_note: Read MenuPage.h in full and MenuPage.cpp:89-183. Every claimed signature and every claimed call is present as described.

findings.title: Menu data classes inherit a copy of the whole GameData service locator, and publish results by writing through raw out-pointers
findings.detail: `class MenuData : public GameData` with `MenuData::MenuData(const GameData* game_data) : GameData(game_data)` (MenuData.cpp:4-8) does not reference the master GameData — `GameData::GameData(const GameData*)` (GameData.cpp:4-19) copies all 13 raw pointers field by field. Each `MainMenuData`/`PauseMenuData`/`EndMenuData`/`ResultsMenuData` is therefore an independent frozen snapshot of `ResourceManager*`, `CommonStates*`, `ThreadPool*`, `ViewportManager*`, `Partitioner*`, `vector<SpriteBatch*>*` and `float* _dt`. Those are not stable: `Game::OnDeviceRestored()` (Game.cpp:283-287) calls `create_device_dependent_resources()`, which builds a new `ResourceManager` (Game.cpp:239), `ThreadPool` (236), `ViewportManager` (247), `CommonStates` (252), `Partitioner` (255) and `_dt` (244) and publishes them only on the master GameData. `Game::OnDeviceLost()` (269-279) resets all 16 SpriteBatches and `_states` while `MenuPage::get_point_clamp_sampler_state()` (MenuPage.cpp:180-183) dereferences `get_common_states()` on every page draw. After one device-lost/restore cycle a live page's whole draw path is use-after-free. On top of that each subclass bolts the page's OUTPUT channel on as a raw pointer (`MainMenuData::_is_ready_to_load_level` bool*, `PauseMenuData::_action`, `EndMenuData::_action`, `ResultsMenuData::_action`), so pages publish results by pointer-writing into parent-owned memory (`*get_pause_menu_data()->get_action() = pause_menu_action::QUIT`, PauseMenu.cpp:242-243) that the parent polls after `update()` (GameStates.cpp:188-240). Input, services and output are fused into one inherited bag, so no page can be constructed or tested without the whole engine.
findings.suggestion: Stop deriving the per-screen data classes from GameData — hold a `const GameData*` (better: a narrow `UIServices` interface with only what menus need). Return the result from `update()` instead of writing it through a raw pointer, so the compiler can tell you a page forgot to set it.
findings.verify_note: Read MenuData.h/.cpp, GameData.h/.cpp:1-30, all four *MenuData.h, and Game.cpp:225-290. Confirmed the field-by-field pointer copy, the recreation of every subsystem in create_device_dependent_resources, and that only `this->_data->set_*` (the master) is updated.

findings.title: Menu navigation and activation are implemented as ~90 string comparisons against widget names
findings.detail: Focus is a widget pointer; the identity of the focused item is recovered with `this->get_highlighted_widget()->get_name()` and compared against string literals. `MainMenuHome::update` (131-203) alone has 11 such comparisons across the PROCEED/UP/DOWN branches. The same shape repeats in `MainMenuOptions::update` (300-425, ~16), `MainMenuModeSelect::update` (645-743, ~18), `MainMenuPlayerCount::update` (880-1009, ~16), `PauseMenuInitial::update` (PauseMenu.cpp:46-114, ~11), `PauseMenuConfirmation::update` (PauseMenu.cpp:215-268, ~6) and `EndMenuInitial::update` (EndMenu.cpp:26-131, ~15). Renaming a widget silently breaks navigation with no compile error; adding one menu item requires edits in four separate if/else ladders (activate, up, down, and the widget-construction block). `MObject::get_name()` already returns `const std::string&` (Mh.h:13), so each of these also takes a gratuitous `std::string` copy per frame per page.
findings.suggestion: Make `MenuHighlight` (or a composed `FocusGroup`) hold `std::vector<MWidget*>` in navigation order plus an index, and expose `move_focus(menu_direction)` with wraparound. Put activation on the item as a `std::function<void()>` or typed command, so a page becomes `add_item("Play", [this]{ push<ModeSelect>(); })` and the up/down handling is written once in the engine.
findings.verify_note: Read all seven cited update() bodies. The counts are in the right ballpark and every cited construct is present. Verified MObject::get_name returns const std::string& at Mh.h:13 / Mh.cpp:14-17, so the `std::string highlighted_element = ...` locals are copies.

findings.title: No navigation stack: every page hardcodes its predecessor as a concrete sibling class
findings.suggestion: Give `StateContext` a stack (`push_state`/`pop_state`) and handle BACK generically in `MenuPage` as `pop()`. Express forward transitions as data on the item or in one flow table so the sequence lives in a single place.
findings.verify_note: Read every cited transition site. All present as described, including the player-count branch at MainMenu.cpp:1450-1461.

findings.title: Game content (weapon, stage and mode catalogues) is hardcoded in switch statements and header string constants
findings.detail: `update_weapon_select_visuals` (1577-1626) switches over `wep_type` to hardcode both sprite frame and label per weapon (`case wep_type::SPRAYER: set_sprite_frame("sprayer"); set_text("Sprayer");` … six cases plus an ERROR default). `weapon_description(wep_type)` (1736-1755) is a second switch returning six `const static std::string` constants declared in the header (MainMenu.h:84-89). `update_stage_select_visuals` (1852-1883) is the same pattern for `level_stage`. `MainMenuModeSelect` hardcodes four modes as four `MTextDropShadow` members (MainMenu.h:196-199), three of which are non-functional stubs that just `play_wave(ERROR_SOUND)` (MainMenu.cpp:673-684). Adding a weapon means editing an enum, two switches, a header constant block and the widget-construction loop across five files. This is exactly the game-specific content welded into what should be engine code — and the project already vendors RapidJSON and loads levels from JSON.
findings.suggestion: Define `struct SelectableItem { std::string id, display_name, description, icon_frame; bool enabled; }` and one data-driven `SelectionPage` taking `std::vector<SelectableItem>` loaded from JSON. WeaponSelect/StageSelect/ModeSelect collapse into one page; the `enabled` flag replaces the ERROR_SOUND stubs so unimplemented modes are greyed out rather than silently buzzing.
findings.verify_note: Read MainMenu.cpp:1577-1626, 1736-1755, 1852-1883, 661-692 and MainMenu.h:84-89, 196-199. All switches, constants and stub branches present as described.

findings.title: A menu page performs raw Win32 window management and duplicates the window-creation logic from Main.cpp
findings.detail: `MainMenuOptions::apply_fullscreen_setting` calls `SetWindowLongPtr(hWnd, GWL_STYLE, WS_POPUP)`, `SetWindowLongPtr(hWnd, GWL_EXSTYLE, WS_EX_TOPMOST)`, `SetWindowPos(..., SWP_FRAMECHANGED)` and `ShowWindow(hWnd, SW_SHOWMAXIMIZED)` — re-implementing the WS_POPUP vs WS_OVERLAPPEDWINDOW branch that `wWinMain` already contains (Main.cpp:154-166). `MainMenuOptions::update` additionally calls `SetWindowPos` directly (334-340), writes the save file twice (329, 343), mutates `ResolutionManager` (324) and manually re-scales its own containers (347-350). `MainMenuHome::update` calls `DestroyWindow(get_main_menu_data()->get_window())` (167). UI code owning the platform window is a hard blocker for engine reuse: there is no path to another windowing backend and no other screen can change resolution without copying this code. Note that this path never calls `DeviceResources::WindowSizeChanged` itself — it relies on the synchronous `WM_SIZE` that `SetWindowPos`/`ShowWindow` dispatch into `WndProc` (Main.cpp:281-303) -> `Game::on_window_size_changed` (Game.cpp:197-205), i.e. device/swapchain teardown re-enters while `MainMenuOptions::update()` is still on the stack.
findings.suggestion: Add an engine-level `DisplayManager`/`IWindow` with `set_resolution()`, `set_fullscreen()`, `request_close()` that owns the Win32 styles, the swapchain resize and persistence. The Options page reduces to `display->apply({res, fullscreen})`, and the apply should be deferred to a defined point in the frame rather than executed mid-update.
findings.verify_note: Read MainMenu.cpp:318-451 and 165-168, Main.cpp:145-166 and 281-303, Game.cpp:197-205. Confirmed the duplication and confirmed that WM_SIZE is dispatched synchronously into on_window_size_changed -> DeviceResources::WindowSizeChanged.

findings.title: draw() is byte-identical in all twelve page classes, as are the container members and the init() scaling tail
findings.suggestion: Move the two containers into `MenuPage` with `add_widget(Layer, MWidget*)`, implement `draw()` once as non-virtual in the base, and have the base `init()` call a pure `build_widgets()` hook then apply the resolution scaling. Twelve overrides and 24 member declarations disappear.
findings.verify_note: Read all twelve draw() bodies and all twelve member declaration blocks. Byte-identical as claimed.

findings.title: Member declaration order makes menu pages outlive every object they point at
findings.detail: Members are destroyed in reverse declaration order. In `GameMenu` (GameStates.h:24-29): `_menu` (the `StateContext` owning the live page) is declared FIRST, so it is destroyed LAST — after `_menu_input`, `_menu_data`, `_menu_level_settings` and `_is_ready_to_load_level`, all of which the page's `MenuPage::_data` / `MainMenuPage::_data` chain points into. `GameLevel` (55-70) has the same inversion three times: `_pause_menu` (60) is destroyed after `_pause_menu_action` (61), `_pause_menu_data` (62) and `_menu_input` (63); `_results_menu` (64) after `_results_menu_data` (66); `_end_menu` (67) after `_end_menu_action` (68) and `_end_menu_data` (69). Currently survivable only because `~MainMenuPage`, `~PauseMenuPage`, `~EndMenuPage` and `~ResultsMenuPage` are all `= default` and touch nothing. One obvious line in a page destructor (`stop_effect(MUSIC)`, or writing a final value through `get_action()`) turns this into a use-after-free, and nothing records the constraint.
findings.suggestion: Declare the `StateContext` members LAST in both classes so pages are torn down before the data they borrow, and add a comment stating the dependency. Better: `_menu.reset();` at the top of the owning destructor so the order is stated in code.
findings.verify_note: Read GameStates.h in full and confirmed the declaration order; read the four page-base destructor declarations (MainMenu.h:114, PauseMenu.h:48, EndMenu.h:46, ResultsMenu.h:68) — all `= default`.

findings.title: highlighted_element is snapshotted before the input loop and never refreshed after change_highlight
findings.detail: Every highlight-driven page reads `std::string highlighted_element = this->get_highlighted_widget()->get_name();` once, before the loop over inputs, then processes every input against that stale string while `change_highlight()` mutates `MenuHighlight::_highlighted_widget` inside the loop. With two pads connected — the normal case here — two DOWN events in the same frame both evaluate against the pre-loop name, so both move the highlight to the same target: the cursor advances one step while the click sound plays twice. On `MainMenuOptions` it is worse: the apply branch (318-353) has no `return`, so a second PROCEED in the same frame re-runs the entire resolution/fullscreen application — two save-file writes, two SetWindowPos/ShowWindow sequences, and a second `scale_objects_to_new_resolution` pass on containers already scaled. Sites: MainMenu.cpp:135-136 (Home), 304-305 (Options), 649-650 (ModeSelect), 884-885 (PlayerCount); PauseMenu.cpp:50-51, 219-220; EndMenu.cpp:29-30. `EndMenuInitial` masks the staleness with a different bug — every `change_highlight` there is followed by `return` (EndMenu.cpp:78, 83, 88, 93, 98, 107, 112, 117, 122, 127), so only the first input of the frame is handled and all other players' inputs are silently discarded.
findings.suggestion: Read the highlight fresh at the top of each loop iteration as `const std::string&`, or drop the stringly-typed identity entirely in favour of an ordered widget vector plus index (see the string-comparison finding), which cannot desynchronise.
findings.verify_note: Read all seven update() bodies. Confirmed the pre-loop snapshot, the in-loop change_highlight calls, the missing return in the Options apply branch, and the ten early returns in EndMenu.cpp that suppress multi-input handling.

findings.title: The mobject index is silently reused as the deferred-context, sprite-batch and command-list index
findings.detail:
```cpp
for (int i = start; i < end; i++)
    this->draw_mobject_in_viewports(
        get_data()->get_device_resources()->get_deferred_context(i),
        command_lists->at(i), sprite_batches->at(i),
        mobjects->at(i).first, mobjects->at(i).second);
```
`i` indexes four unrelated containers. The conflation is visible one frame up: `command_lists` is sized from the CONTEXT count (`std::vector<ID3D11CommandList*> command_lists(deferred_contexts->size(), nullptr);`, MenuPage.cpp:128) while the partitioning at 134-135 is over `mobjects->size()`. The unwritten, unasserted invariant is `mobjects.size() <= 16` (`NUM_THREADS_MAX`, Game.h:14). Exceed it and `get_deferred_context(i)` throws `std::out_of_range` from a `noexcept` function inside a thread-pool worker — instant `std::terminate`. There is no assert and no comment. The partitioning is also pointless at this size: `Partitioner::partition(2, 16)` (Partitioner.cpp:4-22, loop bounded by `i < num_partitions && i < num_elements`) yields exactly two single-element ranges, so two OS work items are dispatched to record one sprite each, with a full barrier.
findings.suggestion: Bind the context/batch/command-list to the partition ordinal, not the mobject index, and assert `mobjects->size() <= deferred_contexts->size()`. For two mobjects, drop the thread pool and record on one deferred context.
findings.verify_note: Read MenuPage.cpp:124-178, Partitioner.cpp in full, Game.h:13-14, DeviceResources.cpp:737-745. Verified partition(2,16) returns exactly two ranges and that get_deferred_context is noexcept.

findings.title: MenuLevelSettings keeps _player_count and _player_settings.size() as two independent facts and indexes with unchecked operator[]
findings.detail: All six per-player accessors (`set_player_setting`, `set_player_team`, `get_player_team`, `set_player_weapon`, `get_player_weapon`, `set_player_num`, lines 62-84) use unchecked `operator[]`. The vector is sized only by `set_player_count` (9-25), and `_player_count` (MenuLevelSettings.h:34) is stored SEPARATELY from `_player_settings.size()`; the invariant that they agree is established in one function and asserted nowhere. Callers drive their loops from `get_player_count()` while indexing containers sized in a different call on a different frame: `MainMenuTeamSelect::set_level_settings` (MainMenu.cpp:1227-1234), `MainMenuTeamSelect::init` (1345-1351), `MainMenuWeaponSelect::init` (1671-1677). `MenuLevelSettings` is also copied by value into `MainMenuMidwayLoadSettings` (MainMenu.h:107) and back out (GameStates.cpp:12-16, 247, 257, 267), crossing several boundaries with nothing revalidating. A default-constructed `MenuLevelSettings` has `_player_count == 0` and an empty vector, so `get_player_team(0)` on one is UB — reachable today only via the HOME entry point which never indexes. The redundant loop in `set_player_count` (15-19) also shows the confusion: `resize()` already value-initialises the new elements, then the loop assigns `MenuPlayerSettings()` over them again (and `MenuPlayerSettings` has default member initialisers for all three fields, MenuPlayerSettings.h:8-11).
findings.suggestion: Delete `_player_count` and make `get_player_count()` return `static_cast<int>(_player_settings.size())` — one source of truth, invariant unbreakable. Collapse `set_player_count` to a single `resize()`. Use `.at()` (or an assert) in the accessors so an out-of-range index fails loudly.
findings.verify_note: Read MenuLevelSettings.h/.cpp in full and MenuPlayerSettings.h. Confirmed the separate _player_count member, the redundant re-initialisation loop, and all six unchecked operator[] accessors.

findings.title: 'Random' is resolved into the persistent settings, so a rematch replays the same weapon and stage forever
findings.detail:
On confirmation, `MainMenuWeaponSelect::update` (1494-1508) overwrites the player's actual choice:
```cpp
if (this->_select_states[i].type == wep_type::RANDOM_PRIMARY)
    this->_select_states[i].type = get_random_weapon();
this->set_level_settings();   // writes the RESOLVED weapon into MenuLevelSettings
```
`MainMenuWeaponSelect::init` seeds from those same settings (`state.type = get_player_weapon(i)`, 1675), so pressing BACK from Stage Select — which constructs a fresh `MainMenuWeaponSelect` (1798) — shows the rolled weapon, not "Random". Identical at 1816-1820 for the stage, and `MainMenuStageSelect::init` reads `get_level_settings()->get_stage()` (1900-1901). Because End Menu -> "Change Level" re-enters stage select with the same `MenuLevelSettings` (GameStates.cpp:263-273), a rematch with Random selected replays the same stage every time — the opposite of what "Random" means.
findings.suggestion: Keep the user's selection (`RANDOM_PRIMARY` / `level_stage::RANDOM`) in `MenuLevelSettings` and resolve it at level-build time in `LevelBuilder`, so each rematch re-rolls.
findings.verify_note: Read MainMenu.cpp:1494-1523, 1671-1677, 1784-1851, 1892-1901 and GameStates.cpp:263-273. Confirmed the resolve-then-persist ordering and that both init()s seed from the persisted settings.

findings.title: rand() is never seeded, so 'Random' weapon and 'Random' stage pick the same values every launch
findings.detail:
```cpp
wep_type MainMenuWeaponSelect::get_random_weapon()
{ int random = rand() % static_cast<int>(wep_type::MAX_PRIM_WEP); return static_cast<wep_type>(random); }
```
and the same shape at 1892-1897 for `get_random_stage()`. A repo-wide grep finds `srand` **zero** times and only three `rand()` call sites: MainMenu.cpp:1521, MainMenu.cpp:1894, TeamColour.cpp:29. The C standard specifies `rand()` behaves as if `srand(1)` were called, so the sequence is byte-for-byte identical on every launch: the first Random pick always yields the same weapon, the second the same second weapon, and Random Stage always resolves to the same stage on the first match of a session. `rand() % n` is also modulo-biased and MSVC's RAND_MAX is 32767. The modulo ranges themselves are correct — `MAX_PRIM_WEP == RANDOM_PRIMARY == 5` so `% 5` yields SPRAYER..BUCKET, and `MAX_STAGE == RANDOM == 3` so `% 3` yields the three real stages — but only because `MAX_*` aliases the last enumerator, a convention the neighbouring `cycle_*` functions read as an INCLUSIVE bound instead.
findings.suggestion: Replace with a single engine-owned `std::mt19937` seeded from `std::random_device` (or the QPC value already in `StepTimer`), exposed through `GameData`, using `std::uniform_int_distribution`. Split the enum sentinel into an explicit `COUNT` that is one past the end so the two readings cannot drift.
findings.verify_note: grep for rand()/srand across ArtAttack/ returned exactly the three call sites and no srand. Read wep_type.h and level_stage.h confirming MAX_PRIM_WEP = RANDOM_PRIMARY and MAX_STAGE = RANDOM.

findings.title: get_menu_inputs() is const and get_-prefixed but consumes global input edge state, and heap-allocates every frame
findings.detail: `std::vector<ProcessedMenuInput> MenuPage::get_menu_inputs() const` (MenuPage.h:53) forwards to `get_data()->get_input()->update_and_get_menu_inputs()` (MenuPage.cpp:185-188). That is not a read: `MenuInput::update_and_get_menu_inputs` overwrites `_prev_inputs[i] = current[i]` (MenuInput.cpp:147), the edge-detection state the entire menu system depends on. So a `const` accessor named `get_*` silently mutates shared state, and calling it twice in one frame makes the second call see no edges and swallow every button press. Every page's `update()` happens to call it exactly once (MainMenu.cpp:49, 133, 302, 647, 882, 1156, 1439, 1786; PauseMenu.cpp:48, 217; EndMenu.cpp:28; ResultsMenu.cpp:32) — the invariant is real but nothing enforces or documents it. Separately, the vector is built with no `reserve`, returned by value from `MenuInput`, returned by value again from `MenuPage`, and copied into a by-value local at every call site: at least one malloc/free per frame per page for at most four 12-byte PODs.
findings.suggestion: Split the responsibilities: `MenuInput::update()` (non-const, called once per frame by the owning state) and `const std::array<ProcessedMenuInput, MAX_PLAYERS>& get_inputs() const` returning a reference to a member. `MenuPage::get_menu_inputs() const` then becomes legitimately const and allocation-free.
findings.verify_note: Read MenuPage.h:53, MenuPage.cpp:185-188, MenuInput.cpp:131-150 (line 147 writes _prev_inputs unconditionally) and every listed call site.

findings.title: All four page base constructors call a member function on a half-built object from the mem-initializer list
findings.detail:
```cpp
MainMenuPage::MainMenuPage(MainMenuData* data) :
    MenuPage(data),
    SoundBankObject(main_menu_consts::SOUND_BANK, this->get_resource_manager()),
    _data(data)
```
`get_resource_manager()` is `MenuPage::get_resource_manager()` (MenuPage.cpp:76-79), which dereferences `MenuPage::_data`. This is well-defined ONLY because `MenuPage` is listed before `SoundBankObject` in `class MainMenuPage : public MenuPage, public SoundBankObject` (MainMenu.h:110). Reordering the base-specifier list — a change that looks purely cosmetic — leaves `MenuPage::_data` as raw uninitialised storage (its `= nullptr` default member initializer has not run either), giving an indeterminate-pointer dereference with no compiler diagnostic. Identical, undocumented, at PauseMenu.cpp:9-16 (PauseMenu.h:44, with `MenuHighlight` sitting between the two bases), EndMenu.cpp:8-14 (EndMenu.h:42) and ResultsMenu.cpp:9-16 (ResultsMenu.h:64). It also dereferences `data` with no null check before the page body runs. Three of the same classes then compound this with alternate constructors whose entire body is a global side effect: `MainMenuTeamSelect` (1137-1142), `MainMenuWeaponSelect` (1420-1425) and `MainMenuStageSelect` (1767-1772) each do `get_main_menu_data()->set_level_settings(settings);`, rewriting state every other page reads.
findings.suggestion: Pass the ResourceManager explicitly from the parameter, not from a half-built `this`: `SoundBankObject(SOUND_BANK, data->get_resource_manager())`. Better still, make sound a composed member rather than a base. Inject the level settings from `GameMenu` before the page is constructed instead of from the page's constructor.
findings.verify_note: Read all four constructors and all four class declarations to confirm base ordering, plus MenuPage.cpp:76-79 and MenuPage.h:57 (`MenuData* _data = nullptr`). Read the three alternate constructors.

findings.title: MainMenuData is constructed with three null pointers and only becomes usable after a separate init() call
findings.detail: Both `GameMenu` constructors (GameStates.cpp:4-17) build `_menu_data` with the one-argument `MainMenuData(GameData*)` ctor, which leaves `_menu_level_settings`, `_is_ready_to_load_level` (MainMenuData.h:20-21) and `MenuData::_input` (MenuData.h:16) all null. They are filled only later by `GameMenu::init()` -> `set_main_menu_data_ptrs()` (19-24, 63-70), which must run before `transition_to` creates the first page at line 26. Between construction and `init()` the object is a live, publicly reachable `MainMenuData` whose three getters return nullptr, and every consumer dereferences them unchecked: `MainMenuPage::get_player_count()` does `get_level_settings()->get_player_count()` (MainMenu.cpp:22-26), `MenuPage::get_menu_inputs()` dereferences `get_input()` (MenuPage.cpp:185-188), `MainMenuStageSelect::update` writes `*get_is_ready_to_load_level() = true` (MainMenu.cpp:1821-1822), and `GameMenu::update()` dereferences `*this->_is_ready_to_load_level` unconditionally (GameStates.cpp:72-77). Calling `update()` before `init()` is an immediate null dereference. The four-argument ctor that would avoid all of this already exists and is never used (MainMenuData.h:12-13).
findings.suggestion: Construct `_menu_input`, `_menu_level_settings` and `_is_ready_to_load_level` in `GameMenu`'s constructor and use the existing four-argument `MainMenuData` ctor, so the object is never observable half-built. Delete the one-argument ctor and the `set_*` mutators.
findings.verify_note: Read GameStates.cpp:4-84 and MainMenuData.h. Confirmed the one-arg ctor is used in both GameMenu constructors, that the four-arg ctor exists and is unused, and that GameMenu::update dereferences _is_ready_to_load_level with no null check.

findings.title: Options 'Apply' re-enters the device/window pipeline mid-update and then uses resources that teardown may have destroyed
findings.detail: Inside `MainMenuOptions::update()`, `SetWindowPos` (334-340) and then `apply_fullscreen_setting` (344 -> 427-451, which does `SetWindowLongPtr` + `SWP_FRAMECHANGED` + `ShowWindow`) dispatch `WM_SIZE` **synchronously** into `WndProc` (Main.cpp:281-303) -> `Game::on_window_size_changed` (Game.cpp:197-205) -> `DeviceResources::WindowSizeChanged`, which on a `DXGI_ERROR_DEVICE_REMOVED/RESET` from `ResizeBuffers` calls `HandleDeviceLost()` -> `Game::OnDeviceLost()` + `OnDeviceRestored()`. That teardown destroys `CommonStates`, all 16 SpriteBatches and (on restore) the `ResourceManager` itself (Game.cpp:239, 252, 269-279) while `MainMenuOptions::update()` is still on the stack. Lines 347-350 then walk `MTexture`/`MTextDropShadow` widgets that each hold a raw `ResourceManager*`, and this page's `MainMenuData` snapshot still points at the destroyed `CommonStates`/`ThreadPool`/`ViewportManager` (see the MenuData finding). The next `draw()` dereferences all of it. Severity is medium rather than high because the destructive branch only fires when `ResizeBuffers` actually reports device loss.
findings.suggestion: Do not mutate the window from inside `update()`. Record the requested change as pending state and apply it at a defined point in the frame (after Present, or via a posted message), then re-query resources and rebuild the page rather than reusing widgets built against the old device.
findings.verify_note: Traced the full call chain in source: MainMenu.cpp:334-350 -> 427-451, Main.cpp:299-302, Game.cpp:197-205, Game.cpp:269-287. The re-entrancy is real; only the device-lost branch inside WindowSizeChanged is conditional.

findings.title: GameData is a public base of five menu data classes but has no virtual destructor and is freely copyable and sliceable
findings.detail: `GameData` (GameData.h:13-62) is a concrete bag of thirteen raw pointers with no `virtual ~GameData()`, no protected destructor and no copy/move control, yet it is publicly inherited by `MenuData` (MenuData.h:7), `MainMenuData`, `PauseMenuData`, `EndMenuData` and `ResultsMenuData`. It actively hands out upcasts: `GameData* GameData::get_game_data()` returns `this` (GameData.cpp:122) and `MenuData* MenuData::get_menu_data()` returns `this` (MenuData.cpp:26-28) — both of which a grep shows are called from **nowhere** in the codebase. Nothing deletes through a `GameData*` today (GameStates.h holds `unique_ptr<MainMenuData>` etc.), but the API invites it, and one `unique_ptr<GameData>` is undefined behaviour that leaks `PauseMenuData::_action` and `ResultsMenuData::_level_end_info`. The implicit copy constructor is equally live and is already used deliberately by `MenuData::MenuData(const GameData*)`. The ctor const-qualification also drifted for no reason: `MenuData(const GameData*)` and `ResultsMenuData(const GameData*, ...)` vs `MainMenuData(GameData*)`, `PauseMenuData(GameData*, ...)`, `EndMenuData(GameData*, ...)`.
findings.suggestion: Make the base non-polymorphic and non-inheritable (`final`, held by composition in the *MenuData classes — the right fix anyway), or give it `virtual ~GameData() = default;` plus deleted copy/move. Do not leave it in the middle. Settle on one const-qualification across the four ctors and delete the dead `get_game_data()`/`get_menu_data()`.
findings.verify_note: Read GameData.h in full — no destructor declared, no copy control. grep confirmed get_game_data and get_menu_data have zero call sites outside their own definitions. Read all four *MenuData.h ctor signatures to confirm the const drift.

findings.title: Four parallel *MenuPage bases exist solely to shadow MenuPage::_data with a duplicate typed pointer
findings.detail: `MainMenuPage` stores `MainMenuData* _data` (MainMenu.h:122) even though `MenuPage` already stores the same object as `MenuData* _data` (MenuPage.h:57) — two members pointing at one object, kept in sync only by the constructor passing `data` twice (`MenuPage(data), ..., _data(data)`, MainMenu.cpp:9-14). The identical pattern is copied in `PauseMenuPage` (PauseMenu.h:61 + PauseMenu.cpp:9-16), `EndMenuPage` (EndMenu.h:53 + EndMenu.cpp:8-14) and `ResultsMenuPage` (ResultsMenu.h:75 + ResultsMenu.cpp:9-16), each with its own `get_X_menu_data()` accessor whose whole job is to return the duplicate. Four near-identical class bodies exist to re-type one pointer.
findings.suggestion: Make the base generic over its data type — `template <class TData> class MenuPageT : public MenuPage { protected: TData* data() const { return static_cast<TData*>(MenuPage::get_data()); } };` — or drop the typed base and have pages call a checked `get_data<MainMenuData>()`. All four intermediate classes and the duplicated members go away.
findings.verify_note: Read all four page-base class declarations and constructors plus MenuPage.h:57. The duplication is exactly as described.

findings.title: MenuHighlight is inherited at three different levels, and per-player selection is re-implemented from scratch twice
findings.detail: `MenuHighlight` is inherited by individual pages in MainMenu (`MainMenuHome`, `MainMenuOptions`, `MainMenuModeSelect`, `MainMenuPlayerCount` — MainMenu.h:141, 158, 184, 204), by the SHARED BASE in PauseMenu and EndMenu (`class PauseMenuPage : public MenuPage, public MenuHighlight, public SoundBankObject`, PauseMenu.h:44; EndMenu.h:42), and not at all by `ResultsMenuPage` or by `MainMenuTeamSelect`/`WeaponSelect`/`StageSelect` (MainMenu.h:224, 259, 296). The three that opted out hand-roll multi-player selection instead: `MainMenuTeamSelect` has `TeamSelectState` + `_select_states` + `update_team_select_visuals`/`deselect_and_unconfirm_all_widgets`/`all_players_confirmed`/`all_players_unconfirmed` (MainMenu.cpp:1236-1309), and `MainMenuWeaponSelect` has a near-identical `SelectState` + `unconfirm_all_widgets`/`all_players_confirmed`/`all_players_unconfirmed` (1555-1636). `all_players_confirmed()` and `all_players_unconfirmed()` are literally the same ten lines duplicated in both classes.
findings.suggestion: Replace the mixin with composition: `std::vector<FocusGroup> _focus` held by `MenuPage`, one group per player slot. Single-cursor pages use `_focus[0]`; per-player pages use one each, and 'all confirmed / all unconfirmed' becomes one method on the collection. That deletes both duplicated pairs and unifies the two visual-refresh routines.
findings.verify_note: Read MenuHighlight.h/.cpp, every page class declaration in MainMenu.h/PauseMenu.h/EndMenu.h/ResultsMenu.h, and diffed MainMenu.cpp:1236-1257 against 1555-1576 — identical bodies apart from the member name.

findings.title: Every menu header transitively pulls in D3D11, XAudio2, the thread pool and the save system, and MenuPage.h is not self-sufficient
findings.detail: `MenuData.h` includes `GameData.h`, which includes ResolutionManager.h, Save.h, ResourceLoader.h, ResourceManager.h, DeviceResources.h, ViewportManager.h, ThreadPool.h and Partitioner.h. `MenuPage.h` includes `MenuData.h`, and every page header includes `MenuPage.h` — so `MainMenu.h`, a file that describes buttons and labels, drags in the entire platform layer. Conversely `MenuPage.h` uses `std::vector`, `std::pair`, `std::string`, `ID3D11DeviceContext`, `ID3D11CommandList`, `ID3D11SamplerState` and `DirectX::SpriteBatch` without including `<vector>`, `<utility>`, `<string>` or `<d3d11.h>`; it compiles only because every .cpp includes `pch.h` first and because MenuData.h happens to pull them in. It also includes `Mh.h` solely for `MObject*` in three declarations. `MainMenu.h:11`, `PauseMenu.h:8` and `EndMenu.h:8` include `StateContext.h` although `State.h:3` already forward-declares `StateContext` and only the .cpp calls `transition_to`.
findings.suggestion: Include what you use (`<vector>`, `<utility>`, `<string>`, `<d3d11.h>`) and forward-declare the rest (`class MObject; class MenuData; class ResolutionManager; class Save; class ResourceManager; class ViewportManager; namespace DirectX { class SpriteBatch; }`). Move `#include "StateContext.h"` into the .cpps. Introduce narrow UI-facing interfaces so no UI header includes d3d11.h at all.
findings.verify_note: Read MenuData.h, GameData.h:1-11, MenuPage.h and State.h. Confirmed State.h:3 declares `class StateContext;` and that MenuPage.h includes none of the standard headers whose types it names.

findings.title: No UI theme abstraction: four const namespaces redefine the same fonts, colours, shadows and sounds, with drift
findings.detail: `main_menu_consts` (MainMenu.h:14-90), `pause_menu_consts` (PauseMenu.h:11-42), `end_menu_consts` (EndMenu.h:11-40) and `results_menu_consts` (ResultsMenu.h:9-62) independently redefine the same values: `DEFAULT_RESOLUTION = {1920,1080}` x4, `ITEM_FONT = "gill_sans_mt_bold_48"` x4, `HEADING_FONT = "gill_sans_mt_bold_72"` x4, `DETAIL_FONT` x3, `SHADOW_COLOUR` + the four shadow offsets x4, `STANDARD_HIGHLIGHT`/`STANDARD_UNHIGHLIGHT` x3, and `SOUND_BANK`/`DIRECTION_SOUND`/`CONFIRM_SOUND`/`CANCEL_SOUND` x4. The drift is already visible: the heading colour is `TEAM_ORANGE` in Pause/End but `GOLDENROD` in Results. Because these are namespace-scope `const`/`const static` objects they have internal linkage, so every TU that includes the header gets its own copy WITH A DYNAMIC INITIALIZER — `MattMath::Colour` is built from a hex string and every `std::string` constant heap-allocates at static-init time. Several are dead: `pause_menu_consts::TITLE_SHADOW_OFFSET`, `end_menu_consts::TITLE_SHADOW_OFFSET`, `end_menu_consts::DETAIL_SHADOW_OFFSET`, `results_menu_consts::TITLE_SHADOW_OFFSET`, `results_menu_consts::ITEM_SHADOW_OFFSET`, `results_menu_consts::DIRECTION_SOUND`, `results_menu_consts::CANCEL_SOUND`. Spelling is inconsistent even within one block (`const static std::string TITLE_FONT` vs `const std::string SOUND_BANK`). (The original report also listed `end_menu_consts::DETAIL_FONT` — that constant does not exist.)
findings.suggestion: Collapse into one `struct MenuTheme { FontSet fonts; ColourSet colours; ShadowSet shadows; SoundSet sounds; Vector2F design_resolution; }` reachable from `MenuPage`. Set `<LanguageStandard>stdcpp20</LanguageStandard>` in ArtAttack.vcxproj — it is currently unset, so the project defaults to an old standard — then these become `inline constexpr` with zero startup cost and one definition. Delete the seven unused constants.
findings.verify_note: Read all four const namespaces in full and grepped each suspected-dead constant against its .cpp. Confirmed the duplication, the TEAM_ORANGE/GOLDENROD drift, the internal-linkage `const static std::string` pattern, and that ArtAttack.vcxproj sets WarningLevel/ConformanceMode but no LanguageStandard. Corrected the DETAIL_FONT claim.

findings.title: Resolution scaling is a destructive one-shot transform in init(), with an ad-hoc re-scale bolted into Options::update
findings.detail: Every page ends `init()` with `_texture_container->scale_objects_to_new_resolution(DEFAULT_RESOLUTION, resolution)` and the same for `_text_container` — widget geometry is authored in 1920x1080 units and baked destructively into the tree once. There is no subscription to resolution changes, so the only page that can survive one is the page that causes it, and it does so by hand: `MainMenuOptions::update` caches `prev_resolution` (322), applies the new resolution, then manually re-scales its own two containers (347-350). Any resolution change from elsewhere (WM_SIZE, alt-enter, a future settings path) leaves every other page mis-laid-out, and because the scaling mutates positions in place it is cumulative and lossy. The ResultsMenu per-frame fill-bar bug is a direct consequence of this model.
findings.suggestion: Keep widget geometry in design space and resolve to pixels at draw time (`transform = viewport_size / design_resolution`), or make resolution change an event the UI root re-lays-out from the authored values. The design resolution should be one engine constant, not a `DEFAULT_RESOLUTION` copy in four headers.
findings.verify_note: Read the init() tail of all twelve pages and MainMenu.cpp:322-351. Confirmed the one-shot model and the manual re-scale.

findings.title: The same 'cycle an enum with wraparound' routine is copy-pasted three times, with an unchecked int round-trip
findings.suggestion: One helper: `template <class E> constexpr E cycle_enum(E value, int step, E last)`, or better a `CyclicSelector<T>` holding `std::vector<T>` + index, which removes the sentinel-aliasing convention entirely and works for data-driven item lists.
findings.verify_note: Read all three functions and both enum headers. The bodies are identical modulo the type, and MAX_PRIM_WEP/MAX_STAGE really do alias the last enumerator.

findings.title: Analog menu edge detection has zero hysteresis — the two thresholds are set to the same value
findings.suggestion: Set `DIGITAL_ABSENCE_THRESHOLD` meaningfully below `DIGITAL_PRESENCE_THRESHOLD` (e.g. 0.8 / 0.4) so the detector is a real Schmitt trigger, use `DEAD_ZONE_CIRCULAR` as `PlayerInput` does, and add a repeat delay so a held direction scrolls at a fixed rate.
findings.verify_note: Read MenuInput.h:9-13, MenuInput.cpp:16-34 (DEAD_ZONE_NONE at line 19) and 72-87, plus PlayerInput.cpp:17-21 (DEAD_ZONE_CIRCULAR). All as described.

findings.title: Widget draws do string-keyed std::map lookups on a non-const map concurrently from thread-pool workers
findings.detail: `widget->draw(sprite_batch, viewports[i])` (MenuPage.cpp:112) bottoms out in string-keyed lookups on every draw. `TextObject::draw` calls `get_resource_manager()->get_sprite_font(this->_font_name)` (TextObject.cpp:27-30), and `ResourceManager::get_sprite_font` is a NON-const member whose body is `return this->_sprite_fonts[font_name].get();` wrapped in a `try/catch (const std::out_of_range&)` that can never fire because `operator[]` does not throw (ResourceManager.cpp:27-38). `SpriteSheet::draw` does `this->_sprite_frames[frame_name].get_source_rectangle()` (SpriteSheet.cpp:105) — same pattern. Two consequences: (a) a missing key makes `operator[]` DEFAULT-CONSTRUCT AND INSERT, so a misspelled font silently returns nullptr into `sprite_font->DrawString(...)` and a misspelled sprite frame silently draws a garbage source rect, with the dead catch block guaranteeing no diagnostic; (b) `draw_mobjects_in_viewports` dispatches these draws to two thread-pool workers concurrently (MenuPage.cpp:142-149), so two threads call a non-const `std::map::operator[]` on the same map in the same frame — a data race by the standard's rules, and a structural mutation of shared state if a key is ever absent.
findings.suggestion: Make every ResourceManager/SpriteSheet getter `const` and use `.find()`/`.at()` so a missing key is a diagnosable error rather than a silent insert. Resolve `SpriteFont*`/`SpriteSheet*`/`SpriteFrame` once in the widget constructor and cache the raw pointer, so the per-frame draw does no lookup at all.
findings.verify_note: Read ResourceManager.cpp:27-38 (operator[] inside a dead try/catch, non-const member), SpriteSheet.cpp:95-112, TextObject.cpp:27-31, and MenuPage.cpp:99-115 and 142-149 confirming the concurrent dispatch.

findings.title: Asset names are bare string literals with no validation; a typo renders garbage, a missing asset returns nullptr
findings.detail: The menus reference every asset by hardcoded string literal — sheet names (`"sprite_sheet_1"`), frame names (`"pixel"`, `"square_white_4"`, `"team_select_a_selected"`, `"stage_king_of_the_hill"`, `"results_menu_fill_box"`, `"sprayer"`, `"random"`, `"error"`, `"stage_test_1"`), font names (MainMenu.h:22-27) and wave/effect names (MainMenu.h:74-81, PauseMenu.h:37-41, EndMenu.h:36-39, ResultsMenu.h:54-61) — roughly 20 frame names and 6 font names in this module, none validated at load. Every failure mode is silent or fatal: `SpriteSheet::draw` uses `_sprite_frames[frame_name]` (SpriteSheet.cpp:105) so a misspelled frame default-constructs and inserts, drawing a garbage source rect; `ResourceManager::get_sprite_font` uses `_sprite_fonts[font_name].get()` (ResourceManager.cpp:29) so a missing font returns nullptr into `sprite_font->DrawString(...)`; `get_sound_bank` (ResourceManager.cpp:91) has the same shape and `MainMenuTitle::init` line 107 `play_effect(MUSIC, true, MUSIC_VOLUME)` dereferences the result. `MainMenuStageSelect::init` even constructs `_stage_icon` with `"stage_test_1"` (line 1927), a name no `update_stage_select_visuals` case ever produces.
findings.suggestion: Give `ResourceManager` `const`, `find`-based getters that throw a descriptive error (or return a checked nullptr) instead of `operator[]` that silently inserts. Validate every menu asset name once at load and fail naming the missing asset. Longer term, replace raw string keys with typed handles resolved at load time.
